rows.what: Henry Robert at 21 — a boarder in Letchworth, and a trade he kept for life
rows.note: FOUND 16 September on Findmypast after Ancestry flagged a 1911 entry it would not show. THE LAST GAP IN HIS LIFE CLOSES. 1911 census, 9 RIDGE ROAD, LETCHWORTH, RG14/7576/0009: HENRY ROBERT WEAR, BOARDER, SINGLE, 21, PRINTER'S ASSISTANT, born Bermondsey — lodging with Harriet Reeves, a 36-year-old widow, her five-year-old son, her brother Albert Charter a trimmer, and another young boarder, James B Dykes, a fitter. HE WAS NOT THERE WITH FAMILY. HE WAS THERE FOR WORK. Letchworth was a new town and J. M. Dent & Sons had put the Temple Press there; he followed the trade, boarded where he could, and married a Baldock girl at Hitchin three years later. THIS IS THE MISSING BRIDGE between the widowed mother's house in Watford in 1891 and the Hitchin marriage in 1914, and it is an ordinary one: a young man moved for a job. AND THE TRADE RUNS THE WHOLE LENGTH OF HIS LIFE WITHOUT A BREAK — printer's assistant at 21 in 1911; printer's machine minder for J. M. Dent & Sons at 72 Pix Road in 1921; MACHINE MINDER on the Durban Castle passenger list at 49 in 1939. Twenty-eight years at one trade, carried to Johannesburg. Saved to data/wear-1911-letchworth.tsv.

rows.what: the tree shared by a second-cousin match, worked properly — nine Castle children and a generation above them
rows.note: DONE 16 September after David asked whether everything had been pulled from the shared tree into the archive. IT HAD NOT — only the horizontal chart had been read, and no person page opened. THAT WAS A MISTAKE AND IT HAD ALREADY PUT A FALSE SENTENCE IN THE DRAFT LETTER: the chart shows only the focus person's direct line, so it looked as though his tree lacked Martha Maud. IT DOES NOT. It carries her, four more Castle siblings the archive did not know, and a whole generation above George William. THE HAUL. MARTHA MAUDE CASTLE, BORN 21 JULY 1895 AT BALDOCK — an exact date where this archive had only a year — baptised there 22 September 1895, married October 1914 at Hitchin. GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLE, born 1862 AT WILLIAN not Baldock, baptised St Mary's Baldock 4 January 1863 with the note 'Parents George & Martha, abode Willian'; agricultural labourer at Middle Row in 1891, farm labourer at Norton End in 1901; died 1916. CAROLINE WALLIS 1862-1957, died Baldock, 'came to Baldock from Weston just before her first marriage'. THE MARRIAGE IS OCTOBER 1882 AT HITCHIN, A YEAR EARLIER THAN THIS ARCHIVE HAD IT. NINE CHILDREN, not the handful known: SARAH ANN WALLIS b. 19 Aug 1882 at Maiden Street, Weston — BORN BEFORE THE MARRIAGE, which is why she carries her mother's surname and is a third independent instance of the WALLIS spelling; George William 1885-1939; Ada May 1886-1969; FREDERICK JAMES abt 1889, entirely new; Agnes Kate 1891-1967; Martha Maude 1895; Sidney Charles 1898-1900, died at two; Florence Margaret Hilda 1901-1985; Ernest Albert Cyril 1903-1988. AND A GENERATION ABOVE: GEORGE CASTLE 1840-1885 x MARTHA GIDDINGS 1841-1863. MARTHA GIDDINGS DIED THE YEAR AFTER HER SON WAS BORN, which is why he is with his grandparents in both 1871 and 1881 — that is what a motherless child looks like in a census — AND IT EXPLAINS WHY A GRANDDAUGHTER BORN THIRTY-TWO YEARS LATER WAS CHRISTENED MARTHA MAUDE. MARKED INFERRED ON THE TREE, NOT PROVED: it is another researcher's tree and its cited sources have not been read directly. NO PHOTOGRAPHS — Martha Maude's gallery is empty and guest role cannot add media. Saved to data/castle-from-match-tree.tsv.

rows.what: Read the Castle sources directly, rather than trusting a tree
rows.note: RAISED 16 September. Everything taken from the tree shared by a second-cousin match is currently marked INFERRED because it is a USER TREE, not a record set. ITS OWN CITED SOURCES ARE NAMED AND ALL OF THEM ARE ON FINDMYPAST, WHICH IS PAID FOR UNTIL ABOUT 16 OCTOBER: the 1871, 1881, 1891, 1901 and 1911 censuses; the England & Wales Christening Index; the civil registration birth, marriage and death indexes; and Public Member Trees, which is not a source and should be discounted. IN PRIORITY ORDER. (1) THE 1871 AND 1881 CENSUSES AT NORTON END, which should show George William as a child in his grandparents' house and NAME THOSE GRANDPARENTS — a further generation, free. (2) THE BAPTISM, St Mary's Baldock, 4 January 1863, which the tree quotes as 'Parents George & Martha, abode Willian' — read the register entry itself. (3) MARTHA GIDDINGS' DEATH IN 1863, which would say whether she died in or soon after childbirth. (4) THE OCTOBER 1882 MARRIAGE AT HITCHIN, which on a certificate names BOTH FATHERS and would settle George Castle senior independently. (5) CAROLINE'S SECOND MARRIAGE, implied by the tree's phrase 'her first marriage' and not yet looked for — she outlived George William by forty-one years. (6) FREDERICK JAMES CASTLE abt 1889, a sibling nobody has traced, AND A POSSIBLE DNA ROUTE: his descendants would share with Derrick through the Castles only. FIRST ITEM DONE 16 September, and it paid immediately. THE 1871 CENSUS AT NORTON END — RG10/1365 folio 27 — does name the grandparents, and THEY ARE NOT CASTLES. The household is JAMES GIDDINS, 57, agricultural labourer, born Baldock; ELIZABETH GIDDINS, 57, born Norton, doing PLATTING; GEORGE CASTLE, 30, AGRICULTURAL LABOURER, ENUMERATED AS SON-IN-LAW; and GEORGE CASTLE, 8, AS GRANDSON. Martha is not there — she had been dead eight years — BUT THOSE TWO RELATIONSHIP WORDS ONLY WORK THROUGH HER, and they are the census's own, not a tree's. So the widower took his motherless boy to HIS WIFE'S PARENTS rather than his own, and they raised him. THE 1861 CENSUS FOUND THE SAME FAMILY TEN YEARS EARLIER at 9 COTTAGES AT NORTON END, BALDOCK, RG9/816 folio 69: James and Elizabeth with George 14, John 12 and Emma 6. MARTHA, WHO WOULD HAVE BEEN 20, IS ALREADY GONE FROM THE HOUSE — in service or married. The Castle generation above George William is therefore PROVED from records rather than taken on trust from another researcher's tree, which is what this row asked for. TWO DISCREPANCIES WORTH KEEPING: the census gives George William's birthplace as BALDOCK where the tree says WILLIAN, and his birth year as 1863 where the tree says 1862. AND A THIRD SPELLING PROBLEM: the tree writes GIDDINGS, both censuses write GIDDINS. Saved to data/giddins-norton-end.tsv.

rows.what: The Oppenheimer control — naturalisation files are not indexed at all, and a negative had to be withdrawn
rows.note: FOUND 16 September, out of David's question 'are there any naturalisation certs for Kurt even?', and it is the most useful thing the day produced about method. THE SEQUENCE. First the archives index was searched on eleven spellings of Ivone's maiden surname and on all three Luwinski spellings: NO NATURALISATION FILE ANYWHERE. A negative was written and published saying so. THEN THE CONTROL WAS RUN, and it should have been run first. WALTER OPPENHEIMER, Kurt's business partner, IS KNOWN TO HAVE NATURALISED — the Union Gazette carries his application as notice 1462, gazette 3007 of 20 February 1942, page 115, and that citation has been on /kurt/ for weeks. HE WAS SEARCHED FOR. HIS NATURALISATION FILE IS NOT IN THE INDEX EITHER. A KNOWN POSITIVE THAT THE INSTRUMENT CANNOT DETECT. So the absence of a Figueiredo or Luwinski naturalisation file says nothing whatever about whether such files exist, and the negative was WITHDRAWN WITHIN THE HOUR. It had mistaken the limits of a finding aid for a fact about the world — which is the second time in one day this archive has done that, after reading a dead hostname as a dead service. WHAT SURVIVES: the sixteen KAB immigration files are still real evidence about WHERE the Portuguese are indexed, just not about naturalisation. WHAT IT CHANGES: the only route left is somebody standing in the reading room asking whether a naturalisation register or card index exists, so that question is now in BOTH outstanding letters — to Ms Xaba, who as Reading Room supervisor would know what finding aids exist, and to the researcher, framed as a question rather than a search and with the Oppenheimer control quoted to her so she knows why it cannot be answered online. AND THE TWO CASES ARE NOT ALIKE. Ivone married a Mr de Witt on 2 February 1948, inside the rule that gave a foreign wife her husband's nationality automatically — that remains the best explanation for her. IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN KURT, who arrived in 1933, was an alien for thirty-five years, and died one.

rows.what: Robert Wear's death certificate, Q1 1890 — vol 1D p141
rows.note: ORDER FROM THE GRO. He died at THIRTY-ONE at St Olave Southwark, six months after his son was born. A death certificate of that period gives the OCCUPATION, THE ADDRESS, THE CAUSE and THE INFORMANT. The informant at the death of a married man of thirty-one is usually the widow — but it can be a parent, and if it is, it names a Wear of the generation above WILLIAM. The cause also matters: a man of thirty-one in Bermondsey in 1890 died of something, and whatever it was probably explains why Emma took three children to Hertfordshire within the year. CHEAP, AND THE SINGLE BEST-VALUE CERTIFICATE ON THIS LIST.

rows.what: The William Weare x Sarah Bloom marriage — FOUND, Stepney 1842, and the certificate names two fathers
rows.note: NOT FOUND, AND THE FAILURE IS RECORDED. A sweep of the England & Wales marriage index on the forename WILLIAM with surname WEAR across 1842-1852 returned eighteen results, almost all NORTHERN — Newcastle, Dewsbury, Stockton, Whitehaven, Hexham — and NOT ONE in a south London district. Their eldest traced child, William, was born about 1850 at Bermondsey, so the marriage should be there. NEXT: search the index the OTHER WAY, on SARAH BLOOM, which is the rarer name of the two; try the London parish registers for St Olave and St Mary Magdalen Bermondsey directly; and widen to 1840-1855. FINDMYPAST, FREE UNTIL ABOUT 16 OCTOBER. WORKED 16 September, and the census did more than the index could. THE MARRIAGE INDEX REMAINS UNHELPFUL: a search on SARAH BLOOM across 1841-1853 returns three, and TWO OF THE THREE ARE NORFOLK — Aylsham 1850 and Depwade 1845 — with one at Stepney in 1842. A paired search, Bloom with spouse surname Wear across 1836-1860, returns ZERO; but that filter infers spouses from index page-mates rather than reading them, so a zero there is weak evidence and is not recorded as a negative. THE 1851 CENSUS ANSWERED WHAT THE INDEX WOULD NOT. SALISBURY STREET, BERMONDSEY — HO107/1560 folio 212: WILLIAM WEAR, HEAD, MARRIED, 28, A SADLER, BORN WALWORTH, SURREY; SARAH WEAR, WIFE, 29, BORN DEPTFORD, KENT; and sons WILLIAM aged 3 and HENRY aged 1, both born Bermondsey. THREE THINGS FOLLOW. (1) THE MARRIAGE IS BEFORE 1848, not 1845-1850 — a son of three in March 1851 moves the window two years earlier than the archive has been searching, which is why the sweeps failed. (2) SARAH WAS BORN AT DEPTFORD, KENT, NOT BERMONDSEY. The 1871 census says Bermondsey. THAT IS A DIFFERENT COUNTY, NOT A SPELLING, and it changes where to look for her baptism and her family. Given the niece born at Yarmouth and two Norfolk marriages in the index, the Blooms may not be a London family at all. (3) HE IS A SADLER IN 1851 AND A HARNESS MAKER IN 1871 — the same trade, and the trade the three eldest sons all took up. *** FOUND THE SAME AFTERNOON, ONCE THE CENSUS MOVED THE WINDOW. *** With the marriage pushed before 1848, the index returns only TWO Sarah Blooms in 1838-1848, and the London one is it. ENGLAND & WALES MARRIAGES, THIRD QUARTER 1842, DISTRICT STEPNEY, COUNTY LONDON, VOLUME 2 PAGE 430. MarriageFinder lists the four people registered on that page: 'Sarah Bloom married one of these people: WILLIAM WEARE, Thomas Moyes, William George Smith, James Wicks.' WILLIAM WEARE — WITH AN E — IS THE ONLY WEAR-SHAPED NAME AMONG THE FOUR, and every other fact fits: she was born about 1822 and so twenty at the wedding; the couple are in Bermondsey by 1848 with a son; and BLOOM is her maiden name independently, from Robert's birth registration. HELD AS PROBABLE, NOT PROVED. Page-mates on an index page are not a marriage; four names on one page means the pairing is inferred, not read. AND STEPNEY IS EAST LONDON where everything else about this family is SOUTH — Walworth, Bermondsey, Deptford — which is not disqualifying but is not nothing either. WHY THE CERTIFICATE IS WORTH ORDERING AHEAD OF ALMOST ANYTHING ELSE: an England and Wales marriage certificate NAMES BOTH FATHERS WITH THEIR OCCUPATIONS. This one would give WILLIAM WEAR'S FATHER — the generation above the harness makers, born before civil registration and otherwise a parish-register problem — AND SARAH BLOOM'S FATHER, a family this archive reached only through a seventeen-year-old niece from Yarmouth. TWO NEW GENERATIONS FROM ONE CERTIFICATE, and it also settles whether she was born at Deptford or Bermondsey. ALSO A NEW SPELLING FOR THE NAMES PAGE: WEARE. *** 20 SEPTEMBER: THE TITLE OF THIS ROW WAS RIGHT AND THE BODY WAS WRONG, AND THE REASON IS A TRAP IN THE SEARCH ENGINE. *** SARAH BLOOM, marriage registered QUARTER 3 OF 1842, STEPNEY, VOLUME 2, PAGE 430 — and Findmypast's Marriage Finder names the other people printed on that page: WILLIAM WEARE, Thomas Moyes, William George Smith, James Wicks. SO SARAH BLOOM MARRIED ONE OF FOUR MEN AND ONE OF THE FOUR IS A WILLIAM WEARE. That is a one-in-four on a page, not a proved marriage, and the archive is calling it what it is. WHAT SETTLES IT IS ONE DOCUMENT: the GRO marriage certificate for Stepney Q3 1842 volume 2 page 430. AN 1842 MARRIAGE CERTIFICATE NAMES BOTH FATHERS. It would give WILLIAM WEAR'S OWN FATHER — the brick wall at the top of the Wear line, since William was born about 1823 at Newington before civil registration — AND SARAH BLOOM'S FATHER, which is the whole point of the Yarmouth enquiry in row 127. ONE CERTIFICATE, TWO GENERATIONS, BOTH SIDES OF THE LINE. It is a purchase, so it is David's. *** AND THE METHOD FAULT, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE ROW. *** A YEAR FILTER ON FINDMYPAST'S MARRIAGE INDEX SILENTLY RETURNS ZERO INSTEAD OF FILTERING. Positive control: James Shardalow Mort married at Yarmouth in 1885, the row was read; searching that surname and place with year=1885 give-or-take two returns NOTHING. Both yearofmarriage= and year= behave the same way. THIS ROW'S OWN EARLIER FINDING WAS A CASUALTY: it recorded three Sarah Bloom marriages in 1841-1853; unfiltered the search returns SIXTY-SEVEN, of which five are before 1870, and the 'Depwade 1845' it named is not in the list at all. THE RULE: do not put a year on a Findmypast marriage search, and run a find-then-filter control before trusting any filter on any dataset. In data/wear-bloom-1842.tsv.

rows.what: William Wear's parents — Newington, Surrey, about 1823
rows.note: PRE-CIVIL-REGISTRATION, so this stops being an index problem and becomes a PARISH REGISTER problem. He was born about 1823 at NEWINGTON, SURREY — from his stated age of 48 in the 1871 census and his birthplace as enumerated. Civil registration began in 1837, fourteen years too late. WHAT WOULD WORK: the Newington St Mary baptism register for 1820-1826, on Findmypast or at the London Metropolitan Archives; and the 1841 and 1851 censuses, which would put him in his own father's household as a young harness maker. THE TRADE IS THE LEVER — harness making ran in this family and a Newington saddler or harness maker with a son William is a narrow target. 17 September: A CHEAPER ROUTE TO THE SAME ANSWER HAS APPEARED, and it is one certificate rather than a parish sweep. WILLIAM JOHN WEAR — the eldest of the four brothers — MARRIED IN Q2 1871 AT ST OLAVE SOUTHWARK, VOLUME 1D PAGE 269. A CIVIL MARRIAGE CERTIFICATE OF 1871 HAS A FATHER'S NAME AND OCCUPATION COLUMN, which is exactly what is missing above William Wear the saddler of Walworth. It would name the grandfather of the line and it costs one GRO order. AND THE SAME ENTRY TIGHTENS THE FENNER ROAD IDENTIFICATION: a marriage in 1871 and a first son in 1875 fit a man of twenty-three, which is what the 1851 census, the GRO birth index and the 1890 death index all make him — against the single 1881 age of 38 that had made him doubtful. ONE WARNING ATTACHED: Findmypast's MarriageFinder offers MARY JANE ALFORD or MARY ELIZABETH GREEN as the bride. THOSE ARE PAGE-MATES IN AN INDEX, NOT A MARRIAGE, and this archive is not writing either of them down as a wife.

rows.what: Sarah Bloom's family — and the Yarmouth connection
rows.owner: David — the same GRO certificate as row 125
rows.note: THE HOUSEHOLD GAVE A FREE LEAD AND IT HAS NOT BEEN FOLLOWED. On census night 1871 at Jamaica Road there was a niece, SARAH ANN BLOOM, 17, BORN YARMOUTH, NORFOLK. A niece of that name in that house is almost certainly the daughter of one of Sarah's brothers, and she is named for her aunt. SO SARAH BLOOM'S FAMILY HAS A NORFOLK BRANCH, and Sarah Ann's own birth registration about 1854 at Yarmouth would give her father's name — Sarah's brother — and through him their parents. THIS IS A WHOLE FAMILY REACHED THROUGH ONE TEENAGER IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S HOUSE. WORKED 17 September, two steps closer and not closed. THE NIECE'S BIRTH REGISTRATION: SARAH ANN BLOOM, YARMOUTH, THIRD QUARTER 1853, VOLUME 4B PAGE 1, MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME MORT. THE HOUSEHOLD BEHIND IT, 1861: Row 80, 80 HOWARD STREET, YARMOUTH — SARAH BLOOM, HEAD, MARRIED, 44, BORN YARMOUTH, her occupation transcribed only as '...wife'; with JAMES 13, SARAH 7, ROBERT 5 and ALLAN 3, every one of them born at Yarmouth. So the mother is SARAH BLOOM BORN MORT, and the niece who turns up in Bermondsey ten years later is her daughter. THE FATHER IS NOT IN THE HOUSE, WHICH IS WHY THE BROTHER IS STILL NOT NAMED. A wife enumerated as head, married, with an occupation ending in 'wife', at a fishing port on census night, ordinarily means A MARINER AT SEA. WHAT STILL DOES NOT FIT, AND IT IS WORTH HOLDING ONTO. Our Sarah was born at DEPTFORD, KENT in the 1851 return and at BERMONDSEY in the 1871. This family is Norfolk to the bone — mother and all four children born at Yarmouth. A brother who went to sea and settled in a different port is an ordinary story, but it is a story, not a record. AND 'NIECE' NEED NOT MEAN A BROTHER'S CHILD; it can be a sister's child keeping the Bloom name only if the sister married a Bloom, or a niece by marriage. NEXT: the 1851 and 1871 Yarmouth returns for the same address, which should catch the husband ashore and name him. *** THREE ROUTES TRIED 17 SEPTEMBER; TWO FAILED INSTRUCTIVELY AND THE THIRD FOUND A CANDIDATE. *** (1) THE MARRIAGE CANNOT BE ASKED FOR DIRECTLY — Findmypast's marriage index carries no spouse surname before 1912, so BLOOM x MORT is unaskable. Asked the other way, SARAH MORT marrying 1841-1851 returns FIVE WOMEN AND EVERY ONE IS IN LANCASHIRE OR CHESHIRE. MORT IS A LANCASHIRE SURNAME. Either she married before civil registration or MORT IS A MIS-READING on that 1853 birth entry — SO THE MAIDEN NAME THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN WORKING FROM IS ITSELF NOW IN DOUBT. (2) THE 1851 CENSUS AT GREAT YARMOUTH has ONE Bloom in the whole town and it is an ELIZABETH BLOOM FIELD — Bloomfield. The family is not there under that spelling, though James was born in the town in 1848. (3) THE 1871 CENSUS PRODUCED A CANDIDATE: RG10 piece 1784, folio 36, page 30, schedule 176, 'Row, Great Yarmouth' — JAMES BLOOM, HEAD, 52, BORN YARMOUTH 1819, OCCUPATION MARINER; wife ANN b.1826; ROBERT b.1856; ALFRED b.1858; Alice b.1860. HE IS A MARINER, which is exactly what the 1861 household implied. AND TWO CHILDREN MATCH — Robert 1856 and a son born 1858, called ALLAN in 1861 and ALFRED in 1871. IT IS NOT PROVED AND IS NOT BEING ROUNDED UP: THE WIFE'S NAME IS WRONG (Sarah b.1817 in 1861, Ann b.1826 in 1871), the address is different, and James and Bloom are both common in a town full of mariners. TWO READINGS FIT — Sarah died in the 1860s and James remarried, which would name William Wear's brother-in-law at last; or there were two Bloom mariner households in one town. WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT: the 1861 page itself at 80 Howard Street, and the death index for a SARAH BLOOM at Yarmouth in the 1860s. Neither has been read. || 20 SEPTEMBER, WORKED AND STOPPED AT A WALL THAT IS WORTH NAMING. The lead was the niece's mother's maiden name, MORT, which should name Sarah Bloom's brother through his marriage. IT DOES NOT, BECAUSE THE MARRIAGE IS NOT AT YARMOUTH AND MAY NOT BE IN NORFOLK AT ALL: the whole England and Wales marriage index holds FIVE Mort marriages in Norfolk, ever, and the earliest is 1885 — thirty-two years after Sarah Ann Bloom was born. A Bloom-to-Mort pairing returns nothing. So the brother married a Mort somewhere else, and the index cannot be asked where without a year, which on this dataset is broken (see row 125). WHAT NOW CARRIES THIS ROW INSTEAD: the GRO marriage certificate for Stepney Q3 1842 volume 2 page 430, which would name SARAH BLOOM'S FATHER outright and make the brother findable from above rather than from the side. This row and row 125 have collapsed into the same purchase.

rows.what: The Hawkins parents of Aldenham — John b.1820 and Emma b.1822
rows.note: ALSO PRE-REGISTRATION, and the same shape of problem as the Wears. Both were born at ALDENHAM about 1820 and 1822 and both were still there in 1871 at The Red Lion Cottages. THE 1841 AND 1851 CENSUSES for Aldenham would put each of them in a parent's household as a young person, and the Aldenham parish registers cover the baptisms. A PARISH OF THAT SIZE IS SMALL ENOUGH TO READ ENTIRE — the 1871 search returned only nineteen Hawkinses in the whole village, so the family can be reconstructed rather than searched for. Findmypast holds the censuses.

rows.what: Louisa and Rosetta Wear — both traced, and only one of them leaves descendants
rows.note: THE MOST DNA-RELEVANT THING ON THIS LIST, and it was only discovered on 16 September. They are HENRY ROBERT WEAR'S SISTERS — Louisa born Wimbledon 1883, Rosetta born Bermondsey 1886, both in the widow's household at Watford in 1891. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: any living descendant of theirs shares with Derrick THROUGH ROBERT WEAR AND EMMA HAWKINS BUT NOT THROUGH MARTHA MAUD CASTLE. Every match that currently supports the reconstruction runs through the Castles. A Louisa or Rosetta descendant would test the WEAR half of the couple INDEPENDENTLY, which nothing has yet done. TRACE: their marriages in the England index from about 1903, then children, then a public tree or a DNA match list. WORKED 16 September, one of the two traced. LOUISA S A WEAR MARRIED A SHENTON IN THE THIRD QUARTER OF 1918, REGISTERED AT HITCHIN, HERTFORDSHIRE — the same district in which her brother Henry Robert had married Martha Maud Castle four years earlier, which is itself a small confirmation that the Watford children stayed within reach of one another. SHENTON IS THEREFORE A LIVE SURNAME: descendants of Louisa carry it, and they would share with Derrick THROUGH ROBERT WEAR AND EMMA HAWKINS ONLY, not through the Castles — which is the independent test of the Wear half that nothing has yet supplied. ROSETTA IS NOT FOUND. A marriage-index search on Rosetta* Wear across 1896-1924 returns NOTHING AT ALL. She may have died young, married later, or been registered under a form the index does not carry — Rosetta was already an unusual name for a Bermondsey girl in 1886 and is exactly the kind that gets written down as Rose or Rosa. NOT CLOSED. AND THE DIRECT SURNAME TEST ON THE MATCH LIST COMES UP EMPTY: 115 match holders searched for SHENTON, HAWKINS, BLOOM, WEAR, CASTLE, WALLIS and WALLS, and not one carries any of them. The only hits are the two Giddins already shown to be a Warwickshire family. THAT IS WEAKER EVIDENCE THAN IT LOOKS, and the Giddins episode is why: a match holder's surname is one of eight great-grandparental lines and there is no reason it should be the relevant one. The absence means only that no match is CONVENIENTLY LABELLED, not that none descends from these people. *** ROSETTA IS TRACED END TO END, 17 SEPTEMBER, AND SHE NEVER MARRIED. *** She had been unfindable because the archive was searching a fifteen-year-old who had left home and because her full name was not known. THE 1901 CENSUS GAVE HER BACK: at 22 Mount Pleasant, St Albans, aged 15, an APPRENTICE STRAW HAT MAKER — the Hertfordshire county trade. THE 1911 CENSUS GAVE HER NAME IN FULL: ROSETTA EMMA WEAR, named for her mother, aged 25, SINGLE, a SHOP ASSISTANT LIVING IN AT A BAKERY AT 145 HIGH STREET, WATFORD, in the household of John Alfred Guthrie, baker and pastry cook. LIVING-IN SERVICE IS WHY SHE MOVED AND WHY SHE WAS HARD TO HOLD. AND THE DEATH INDEX ENDS IT: ROSETTA EMMA WEAR, BORN 1885, DIED 1980, SURREY NORTH WESTERN — about ninety-four years old, and STILL A WEAR. A marriage search on every Ros- form across 1910 to 1940 returns Rosalind, Rosamond, Rosannah, Rose, Rosemary, Rosie and Rosina, AND NO ROSETTA. SHE OUTLIVED HER BROTHER HENRY ROBERT BY ELEVEN YEARS. WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE DNA, AND IT NARROWS THINGS USEFULLY: ROSETTA LEAVES NO DESCENDANTS, so the independent test of the Wear half CANNOT come through her. IT RESTS ENTIRELY ON LOUISA, who married a SHENTON at Hitchin in 1918 — and now also on the two HULL half-siblings, who test the Hawkins line instead. AND A 1980 DEATH IS RECENT: the certificate names an informant, who at ninety-four is very likely a niece, a nephew or their children.

rows.what: Martha Giddings' death, 1863 — and whether it was childbirth
rows.note: SHE DIED THE YEAR AFTER HER SON WAS BORN. George William Castle was born at Willian in 1862 and baptised at Baldock on 4 January 1863; his mother MARTHA GIDDINGS, born 1841, is recorded as dying in 1863 aged about 22. He is with his grandparents in BOTH the 1871 and 1881 censuses, which is what a motherless child looks like. A DEATH CERTIFICATE WOULD GIVE THE CAUSE AND THE DATE, and if the date is close to the baptism then this family lost a mother of twenty-two to childbirth and the whole shape of George William's upbringing follows from it. Also: DID GEORGE CASTLE REMARRY? He lived until 1885. *** FOUND 16 SEPTEMBER, AND IT CORRECTS SOMETHING THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED THIS MORNING. *** ENGLAND & WALES DEATHS, THIRD QUARTER 1863, DISTRICT HITCHIN, HERTFORDSHIRE, VOLUME 3A PAGE 188 — the only Martha Castle registered in that district that year. Hitchin is the district covering Baldock, Willian and Norton. THE QUARTER IS THE POINT. Her son was baptised at St Mary's Baldock on 4 JANUARY 1863; the third quarter runs JULY TO SEPTEMBER. SO SHE LIVED AT LEAST SIX MONTHS AFTER THE BAPTISM AND HER BOY WAS ABOUT A YEAR OLD WHEN SHE DIED. THE ARCHIVE HAD PUBLISHED, ON /leonard/ AND IN THE LETTER TO A DNA MATCH, THAT 'IF MARTHA GIDDINGS DIED IN 1863 SHE CANNOT HAVE KNOWN HER SON AT ALL'. THAT IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. She knew him for the better part of a year, which is a different fact and a sadder one. THE INFERENCE THAT SURVIVES IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED: he is with his grandparents in 1871 and 1881, and a widower of twenty-two took his motherless boy to his wife's people. STILL WORTH ORDERING: the death certificate at 3A/188 gives the AGE AT DEATH, which would confirm the 1841 birth this archive has only from a user tree, and the CAUSE, which would say whether this was childbed fever months later, consumption, or something else entirely. CORRECTION TO THE CORRECTION, SAME HOUR. The commit recording this said the claim was corrected 'in both places', on /tree/ and on /leonard/. IT WAS NEVER ON /leonard/ — that page contains no mention of Giddings at all, and the replace that was supposed to fix it silently matched nothing, which is the same class of bug as the stylesheet link earlier today. ONLY /tree/ CARRIED IT AND ONLY /tree/ NEEDED FIXING. IT IS ALSO IN A LETTER THAT HAS GONE. The reply sent to the second-cousin DNA match this afternoon says: 'If Martha Giddings died in 1863 she cannot have known her son at all, and I notice your George William is with his grandparents in both 1871 and 1881.' The condition is true — she did die in 1863 — so the consequent was asserted, and it is wrong. SHE DIED IN THE THIRD QUARTER AND HE WAS BAPTISED IN THE JANUARY. That goes in the next message to him, not in a fresh email for one sentence. *** ANSWERED 20 SEPTEMBER, AND THE ANSWER TO THE SECOND HALF IS NO. *** Three GRO index entries, all Hitchin registration district, in this order: the MARRIAGE of George CASTLE to a GIDDINGS in QUARTER 3 OF 1862; the birth of GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLE in QUARTER 4 OF 1862 - within three months of the wedding; and the death of MARTHA CASTLE in QUARTER 3 OF 1863, volume 3A page 188. SO IT WAS NOT CHILDBIRTH. She died nine to twelve months after her son was born, not at his birth, and the two events are not connected. A second Castle birth in the window, GEORGE MUNT CASTLE of Q4 1863, CANNOT be hers because she was already dead when he was registered - a different Castle family in the same district, written down before it costs anybody a day. THE BOUND, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED: the marriage index prints the groom as George Castle and the bride only as a Giddings - IT DOES NOT GIVE HER FORENAME - and the pre-1866 death index carries NO AGE, so the second Martha Castle death at Hitchin in 1865 cannot be ruled out on the index alone. Closing it properly needs two GRO certificates: the 1862 marriage, which names both fathers, and the 1863 death, which gives her age and cause. WHAT MAKES IT HANG TOGETHER ANYWAY is that George William is with his GRANDPARENTS in 1871 and again in 1881, which is what happens to a boy whose mother died before he was one. In data/castle-giddings-1862.tsv.

rows.what: The Castle-Wall(i)s marriage certificate, October 1882, Hitchin
rows.note: IT SETTLES TWO THINGS AT ONCE AND IT IS ONE CERTIFICATE. An England and Wales marriage certificate NAMES BOTH FATHERS with their occupations. So it would give GEORGE CASTLE 1840-1885 independently of a user tree, and it would give CAROLINE'S FATHER — WHICH DECIDES WALLS AGAINST WALLIS, a contradiction this archive has published seven times one way and five the other. The date is October 1882 at Hitchin, and the tree that supplied it notes she 'came to Baldock from Weston just before her first marriage'. NOTE ALSO that their eldest, Sarah Ann, was born 19 August 1882 at Maiden Street, Weston — TWO MONTHS BEFORE THE WEDDING. NOTE 17 SEPTEMBER: THE SPELLING QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED AND NO LONGER NEEDS THIS CERTIFICATE. The GRO birth index gives MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME WALLIS for six of her children and nothing for Walls. THE CERTIFICATE IS STILL WORTH ORDERING for the other thing it does — it NAMES BOTH FATHERS WITH THEIR OCCUPATIONS, giving George Castle senior independently of a user tree and Caroline's own father for the first time. 17 September: the 1911 census gives YEARS MARRIED as 28, which from 2 April 1911 puts the wedding between April 1882 and April 1883 and so agrees with the Q4 1882 index entry. It is corroboration, not the certificate; the certificate is still what names the two fathers.

rows.what: Caroline remarried in 1920 and was CAROLINE JAMES for the rest of her life
rows.note: A PHRASE IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S TREE. The note against her October 1882 marriage reads 'came to Baldock from Weston just before HER FIRST MARRIAGE'. That wording implies a second, and the arithmetic supports it: GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLE DIED IN 1916 AND SHE LIVED UNTIL 1957 — forty-one years a widow, from the age of fifty-four. NOBODY HAS SEARCHED FOR IT. A remarriage certificate would give her father's name a second time, which is the cheapest possible cross-check on Walls against Wallis, and a second married surname would explain why she has been hard to follow after 1916. *** FOUND 17 SEPTEMBER, AND THE PHRASE IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S TREE WAS RIGHT. *** Q3 1920, DISTRICT HITCHIN, VOLUME 3A PAGE 2077: CAROLINE CASTLE MARRIED JAMES JAMES. MarriageFinder names him outright rather than offering four page-mates. She was 57, and George William had been dead four years. THEN THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS BIGGER THAN THE MARRIAGE. FROM 1920 SHE WAS CAROLINE JAMES. Every tree carrying her as 'Caroline Wallis 1862-1957' has been hunting a death registered under a surname she stopped using thirty-seven years before she died. TESTED AND CONFIRMED: England & Wales deaths, CAROLINE JAMES, birth year 1862, died 1957, HITCHIN, HERTFORDSHIRE. AND THE 1939 REGISTER HAS HER, which closes another row in the same stroke: RG101/1598B/017/25, schedule 134, 38 NORTON ROAD, BALDOCK — CAROLINE JAMES, WIDOWED AGAIN, unpaid domestic duties, AND BORN 28 FEBRUARY 1863. AN EXACT DATE OF BIRTH, and it is 1863, NOT the 1862 that this archive and the tree it came from both carry. SHE OUTLIVED TWO HUSBANDS AND DIED AT NINETY-FOUR.

rows.what: Fredrick James Castle registered 1889 — so the Baldock man of 1887 is somebody else
rows.note: NEW ON 16 SEPTEMBER and nobody has touched him. One of the nine children of George William Castle and Caroline, born at Baldock about 1889, between Ada May 1886 and Agnes Kate 1891. NO DEATH DATE in the tree that supplied him, which usually means he was not followed. WHY HE MATTERS: he is a CASTLE MALE LINE. Descendants of his would carry the Castle surname forward and would share with Derrick through George William and Caroline — and, unlike the Brown and Wear descendants already matched, A MALE-LINE CASTLE COULD ALSO BE Y-TESTED if the question ever needed it. *** WORKED 17 SEPTEMBER, AND IT RAISES A PROBLEM RATHER THAN CLOSING ONE. *** A Frederick Castle is in the 1939 Register AT BALDOCK — TNA R39/1598A/017/15, schedule 157 — BORN 10 APRIL 1887, MARRIED, occupation 'VERTICAL DRILLER ON AIRCRAFT WORK', living with ELLA CASTLE born 12 November 1895, AND A THIRD PERSON IN THE HOUSEHOLD WHOSE RECORD IS STILL OFFICIALLY CLOSED. The deaths index carries a FREDERICK JAMES CASTLE, birth year 1887, DIED 1975 AT HITCHIN. Same town, same name, and 1887 in both. THE ARITHMETIC DOES NOT WORK. The tree that supplied the Castle children gives ADA MAY CASTLE AS BORN 10 DECEMBER 1886. A brother born 10 APRIL 1887 IS FOUR MONTHS LATER, WHICH IS IMPOSSIBLE FOR FULL SIBLINGS. THREE READINGS AND NONE IS PICKED. (a) This Frederick is a different Castle — Baldock is small but the surname is not rare there. (b) ADA MAY'S DATE IS WRONG; it comes from the same user tree that put Frederick at 'about 1889' and put George William's birth at Willian when the census says Baldock, so that tree has been wrong twice already today. (c) FREDERICK'S OWN DATE IS WRONG, though a 1939 Register entry is a man stating his own date of birth to a registrar and is about as good as that gets. WHAT SETTLES IT: the birth registration for Frederick James Castle at Hitchin, which would give the quarter and the mother's maiden name — WALLS OR WALLIS — and would either place him in this family or take him out of it. HE STILL MATTERS FOR THE SAME REASON AS BEFORE: if he is theirs, he is a CASTLE MALE LINE and the only Y-testable branch on that side, and the closed record in his 1939 household suggests a descendant. *** RESOLVED THE SAME HOUR, AND THE TREE WAS RIGHT AFTER ALL. *** The GRO birth index, searched on MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME WALLIS at Hitchin, returns FREDRICK JAMES CASTLE REGISTERED IN 1889 — exactly the 'about 1889' the tree gave. SO THE FREDERICK CASTLE BORN 10 APRIL 1887 IN THE 1939 REGISTER AT BALDOCK IS A DIFFERENT MAN, and the four-month impossibility against Ada May dissolves: she is registered 1887 and he is registered 1889, two years apart, which is ordinary. The vertical driller on aircraft work, his wife Ella and the closed record in their household belong to another family. HE IS STILL UNTRACED AND STILL MATTERS: a Castle male line is the only Y-testable branch on that side. What is now known is his registration year and that his death is NOT the 1975 Hitchin one, which belonged to the 1887 man.

rows.what: The British Newspaper Archive — Letchworth, Hitchin and Baldock
rows.note: UNTOUCHED, AND THE SUBSCRIPTION IS PAID FOR. Findmypast surfaced a hit in THE CITIZEN (LETCHWORTH) against Henry Robert Wear's own record and it was never opened. WHAT A LOCAL PAPER CARRIES THAT NO INDEX DOES: emigration send-offs, works notices, marriage reports naming the whole wedding party, obituaries naming survivors, and court and inquest reports. TARGETS: the Wears at 72 Pix Road 1917-1939 and the 1939 departure; the Castles at Baldock and Norton; J. M. Dent's Temple Press staff notices; and MARTHA GIDDINGS' DEATH IN 1863, which a Hertfordshire paper may report where a certificate is slow and costs money. EXPIRES ABOUT 16 OCTOBER. ATTEMPTED 16 September AND BLOCKED, and the blocker is the interface rather than the subscription. The full-text search at findmypast.com.au/search-newspapers DOES load — it reports 108,257,013 newspaper pages and renders its own form — but IT WILL NOT SUBMIT. The name field accepts a value by every route tried, including a native setter with an input event; the Search button is present and reports as clicked; and the page simply stays where it is with no results and no error. Tried also: the URL forms /search/british-newspapers, /search/newspapers and /newspapers with query strings, ALL OF WHICH REDIRECT to the generic world-records page. SEPARATELY, the indexed FAMILY NOTICES set at search-world-records-in-newspapers-and-publications DOES work and returns NOTHING for WEAR at Letchworth — but that set is not the newspaper archive and says so itself: 'what you are able to search here today is just a small sample of the records to come.' SO THE NEGATIVE IS WORTHLESS AND IS NOT RECORDED AS ONE. WHAT TO TRY NEXT: the Advanced Search link on the same page, which is a different form; britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk directly, which a Findmypast subscription usually covers but which needs its own sign-in; or simply the same search on another day, since the rest of the site has worked all afternoon and this one page has not.

rows.what: The 1939 Register — for the Castles who stayed
rows.note: THE WEARS LEFT IN AUGUST 1939. THE REGISTER WAS TAKEN ON 29 SEPTEMBER 1939, so it catches everyone who did NOT go — and it carries EXACT DATES OF BIRTH, not quarters. TARGETS: Sarah Ann Wallis b.1882, Ada May Castle b.1886, Frederick James b.1889, Florence Margaret Hilda b.1901 and Ernest Albert Cyril b.1903, all of whom died in England; Agnes Kate Castle and Walter George Brown at Blackwater; and CAROLINE HERSELF, then 77 and widowed twenty-three years, whose entry would give her exact date of birth and her household. ALSO WORTH CHECKING WHETHER LEONARD IS IN IT — he is on neither 1939 ship, and an English entry in September 1939 would prove he was still in England a month after his mother sailed. *** WORKED 17 SEPTEMBER, and it produced two findings and one exclusion. *** FIRST, CAROLINE. There is no Caroline Castle in Hertfordshire in the 1921 census at all, and there is one CAROLINE JAMES — RG15 piece 7079, schedule 125, 9 BOSCOMBE PLACE, LETCHWORTH, wife of JAMES JAMES, born WESTON, Herts, aged 56 years 4 months. IN THE HOUSE WITH THEM: ERNEST ALBERT CYRIL CASTLE and FLORENCE MARGARITE HILDA CASTLE, ENUMERATED AS STEP-CHILDREN. The remarriage is no longer an index line, it is a household, and the two youngest Castles have their full names for the first time. The age puts her birthday in February, agreeing with the 28th; the year is two out and she gave it herself. AND SHE HAD MOVED TO LETCHWORTH, where her daughter was raising the Wears. SECOND, THE SIBSHIP IS BIGGER THAN ANYBODY THOUGHT. The 1911 census at THE CHURCH YARD, ST MARY'S COTTAGES, BALDOCK — RG14/7572, schedule 173 — asks the fertility question and Caroline answers NINE BORN, EIGHT LIVING, ONE DIED. Six are known from the GRO index and Martha Maud is a seventh. AT LEAST TWO CASTLE CHILDREN HAVE NEVER BEEN IDENTIFIED, and one of the nine was dead before April 1911. JOSEPH WALLIS is in that household as Caroline's father, spelt WALLIS. THIRD, FREDERICK IS NOT SETTLED AND THE 1975 MAN IS NOT HIM: see the row below.

rows.what: Electoral registers — 72 Pix Road, and bracketing the departure
rows.note: A DIFFERENT WAY AT THE SAME QUESTION, and Findmypast holds the series. Electoral registers list adults at an address year by year, so the year 72 PIX ROAD, LETCHWORTH stops listing Wears is the year the household broke up — which should be 1939 and can now be tested rather than assumed. MORE USEFULLY: LEONARD WAS TWENTY-ONE IN 1938 and would appear in his own right. If he is on the register for 1938 or 1939 and gone by 1940, that dates HIS departure, which BT 27 has so far refused to. WORKED 16 September, AND THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE TURNED OUT TO BE WRONG. It said Leonard 'was twenty-one in 1938 and would appear in his own right', so that the year he vanished would date his departure. HE SAILED IN MARCH 1937, AGED TWENTY — found the same afternoon — AND THE VOTING AGE WAS TWENTY-ONE. He could never have appeared on an English register as an adult, and no amount of searching will put him there. The row cannot do what it was raised to do. WHAT THE REGISTERS DO GIVE IS THE HOUSEHOLD, AND IT IS A SOLID RUN. HENRY ROBERT WEAR IS ON THE LETCHWORTH REGISTER EVERY YEAR FROM 1919 TO 1930 — 1919, 1920, 1921, 1922, 1923, 1924, 1925, 1926, 1928, 1929, 1930, with only 1927 missing from the returned set. Parliamentary County of Hertfordshire, Hitchin Division, polling district LETCHWORTH; British Library SPR.Mic.P.16/BL.H.57. ELEVEN UNBROKEN YEARS is a man rooted in one town, and it brackets the settled period before the emigration. TWO LIMITS, BOTH STATED. The transcripts give the YEAR AND THE POLLING DISTRICT BUT NOT THE STREET — the address is on the original image and has not been read, so this does not yet date the move to 72 Pix Road. AND THE SET ENDS IN 1932, so it CANNOT bracket the 1939 departure from the English end; nothing in it reaches the years that matter for that.

rows.what: MOTA — 288 archive records, and the most important untested name
rows.owner: the National Archives of South Africa — NAAIRS is down
rows.note: STATED AS A GAP ON /names/ AND STILL OPEN. MOTA FIGUEIREDO is the fullest form anybody ever wrote of Ivone's maiden name — it comes from WLD 1950/1948, the first divorce — and MOTA alone returns 288 records in the archives index, far past the harvest cap used on the other spellings. NOBODY HAS READ THEM. The name is common enough that most will be nothing, but it is the one search where a relative could be hiding in plain sight under a name this archive already knows she used. NEEDS NAAIRS BACK UP — it returned 'the connection to the Search Manager Server is inactive' on the afternoon of 16 September. || BLOCKED 20 SEPTEMBER: NAAIRS has stopped answering altogether — not 503 as on 17 September but no response at all, portal and search service alike, four days running. See row 179. This row cannot move until it comes back, and marking it 'next' overstated what this archive can do.

rows.what: Morris Isaac Salkow — his whole litigation history, and his estate at Cape Town
rows.owner: the National Archives of South Africa — NAAIRS is down
rows.note: FOUND 16 SEPTEMBER BY SPELLING VARIANTS AND ONLY LOGGED, NOT WORKED. Ivone married him on 13 February 1953 and he had sued or been sued at least six times: TPD 467/1950 Rosaline born Bernhardt v him; TPD 2854/1960 him v Rosaline Burns formerly Spence-Wilson formerly Salkow; WLD 1593/1962 him v Gertie formerly Moagus; WLD 3317/1963 him v Cecilia Maud born Shein; WLD 2225/1953 him v Ivonne; and WLD 15934/1979 Mayveen Properties v him. HE MARRIED AT LEAST FOUR TIMES. AND HIS ESTATE PAPERS ARE AT KAB, MOOC 6/9/5171 ref 61416 — CAPE TOWN, where this archive ALREADY HAS AN OPEN REQUEST for the Lerena death notice. IT COULD RIDE ALONG AT NO EXTRA TRAVEL. || BLOCKED 20 SEPTEMBER: NAAIRS has stopped answering altogether — not 503 as on 17 September but no response at all, portal and search service alike, four days running. See row 179. This row cannot move until it comes back, and marking it 'next' overstated what this archive can do. *** AND A CHECK BEFORE ANYBODY TRAVELS, 20 SEPTEMBER — THIS ROW MAY BE SENDING A RESEARCHER TO THE WRONG PROVINCE. *** The row proposes that the Cape Town estate KAB MOOC 6/9/5171 ref 61416 'ride along' with the Lerena request. BUT THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN corrections.json SAYS MORRIS ISAAC SALKOW DIED AT JOHANNESBURG: 'Johannesburg Chevrah Kadisha burial register: died 08.11.1991, buried 10.11.1991, WESTPARK BLOCK U GRAVE 2469.' A man who dies and is buried in Johannesburg in 1991 has his estate at the Master there, numbered 1991 or 1992 — NOT at the Cape. AND THERE IS A BETTER CANDIDATE FOR THE CAPE FILE, found in the FamilySearch sweep of 20 September: ISAAC MORRIS SALKOW, born 1897 in LITHUANIA, DIED 10 OCTOBER 1938 IN THE CAPE PROVINCE, with probate 1938 to 1939 in the Cape Probate Records of the Master of the High Court, wife ANNIE DEBORAH born GOLDSMITH. THE FORENAMES ARE REVERSED AND THE DEATHS ARE FIFTY-THREE YEARS APART. MOOC 6/9/5171 fits a 1938 Cape estate far better than a 1991 Johannesburg one. DO NOT ORDER IT AS IVONE'S HUSBAND'S UNTIL THE MOOC REFERENCE HAS BEEN CHECKED AGAINST A DATE. Ivone's husband's estate should be sought at TAB or the Master in Johannesburg for 1991-92.

rows.what: Paula Luwinski sequestrated a man's estate in 1972 — and the OCR nearly made her the debtor
rows.note: OPPOSED APPLICATION. PAULA LUWINSKI VERSUS PHILLIP CRYSTAL, TAB WLD 2451/1972. Found in the variant sweep and not yet explained. THE ARCHIVE KNOWS A PAULINE LUWINSKI — Kurt's widow, born Rappoport 1914, died 1985 — AND PAULA IS NOT PAULINE, or at least is not obviously. The file is from 1972, four years after Kurt died. IF PAULA IS PAULINE UNDER A SHORTER NAME, this is the widow in court over something four years on; IF SHE IS NOT, there is a Luwinski woman in Johannesburg nobody has accounted for. EITHER ANSWER IS WORTH A ROW. It is a TAB file and belongs on any future researcher list. *** ANSWERED 16 SEPTEMBER FROM THE GAZETTE. *** Government Gazette 3701 of 10 NOVEMBER 1972, page 126, a table of sequestrations: 'No. of estate / Name and description of estate / Date upon which and division of court by which order made / UPON THE APPLICATION OF'. ENTRY T1301/72: 'PHILLIP CRYSTAL, AN ADULT WHITE MALE, A COMMERCIAL TRAVELLER, MARK HOTEL, O'REILLY ROAD, BEREA, JOHANNESBURG' — order made 17/10/72 in the Witwatersrand Local Division — UPON THE APPLICATION OF PAULA LUWINSKI. So the court file WLD 2451/1972, 'OPPOSED APPLICATION, PAULA LUWINSKI VERSUS PHILLIP CRYSTAL', is a SEQUESTRATION SHE BROUGHT AND WON. She was his creditor; he was the one living in a hotel and he was the one whose estate went. AND THE FIRST READING OF IT WAS WRONG, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING. The text-extraction of that page returned the fragment 'Paula Luwinski, a commercial traveller, Mark Hotel' — the OCR had jammed two columns of a four-column table into one line, and it read as though PAULA were the commercial traveller living in the hotel. SHE WAS NOT. HE WAS. It took rendering the page as an image at 170 dpi to see the table structure, which is the same technique this archive has needed before on these scans. A COLUMN BOUNDARY IS INVISIBLE TO A TEXT DUMP. WHAT IS NOW KNOWN ABOUT HER: a Luwinski woman in Johannesburg in 1972, four years after Kurt died, solvent enough to be a creditor and determined enough to take an opposed application to judgment. WHAT IS STILL NOT KNOWN is who she was to him — she is not Pauline, whose name appears in every record as Pauline and who was born Rappoport.

rows.what: Who else sailed on the Dunvegan Castle and the Durban Castle
rows.note: CHAIN MIGRATION IS A REAL PATTERN AND IT HAS NOT BEEN TESTED HERE. The Dunvegan Castle carried 406 passengers out of London on 10 August 1939 and Martha Maud and four children were five of them. THE QUESTION IS WHETHER ANYONE ELSE ABOARD CAME FROM LETCHWORTH, HITCHIN OR BALDOCK — because people from one small town emigrating in one year usually go together or follow each other, and a neighbour on that manifest would explain WHY Johannesburg of all places, which this archive has never satisfactorily answered. Same for the Durban Castle in April. Findmypast allows browsing a voyage rather than searching a name. WORKED 16 September AS FAR AS THE INDEX ALLOWS, WHICH IS NOT FAR ENOUGH. Findmypast will browse a voyage rather than a name, and the Dunvegan Castle of 10 August 1939 returns FORTY-THREE INDEXED PASSENGERS — not the 406 the manifest states, so the indexed set is a fraction, most likely one class or one sheet. The forty-three are Bliss (two), Catto, Corbett, Coxen, Downwaite, Farber (three), Furneaux, Goldsmith, Griffin, Haward, Hay, Hobling, John, Luslie (two), Macnab and the rest, with the five Wears among them. NOT ONE OF THEM CAN BE PLACED. THE INDEXED FIELDS DO NOT INCLUDE AN ADDRESS — five Wear transcripts from this voyage were read in full earlier today and none carries one — so there is no way from the index to tell whether anybody aboard came from Letchworth, Hitchin or Baldock, which is the entire question. THE ANSWER IS ON THE IMAGE AND ONLY THERE. A BT 27 outbound form carries a column for the passenger's LAST ADDRESS IN THE UNITED KINGDOM, and that column is what would show a neighbour. SO THE ROW IS NOT DONE, IT IS RE-AIMED: view the original manifest images for both voyages — TNA BT27/1542/00/0024 for the Dunvegan Castle and BT27/1540/00/0042 for the Durban Castle — and read the address column beside the Wear entries. That is a reading job, not a search, and it is the only route to why Johannesburg.

rows.what: J. M. Dent & Sons, and the Letchworth Garden City records
rows.note: TWO INSTITUTIONAL LETTERS NOBODY HAS WRITTEN. Henry Robert Wear was a PRINTER'S ASSISTANT boarding at 9 Ridge Road in 1911 and a PRINTER'S MACHINE MINDER AT J. M. DENT & SONS at 72 Pix Road in 1921 — the Temple Press, which was the reason Letchworth existed for men like him. DENT'S BUSINESS RECORDS survive in part and staff registers sometimes name date of engagement and previous employer. SEPARATELY, THE LETCHWORTH GARDEN CITY HERITAGE FOUNDATION holds tenancy and estate records for the town's houses — both 9 Ridge Road and 72 Pix Road were Garden City property. A tenancy file would date the family's arrival and departure from the other end, independently of the passenger lists.

rows.what: Ivone's 1924 birth registration — try Lisbon, not only Maputo
rows.note: THE CENTRAL QUESTION, AND ONE ROUTE TO IT HAS NEVER BEEN TRIED. The archive has written to Mozambique and had no answer, and row 8 records eleven institutional letters still unanswered. WHAT HAS NOT BEEN TRIED IS THE PORTUGUESE SIDE OF THE SAME RECORD. Portuguese colonial civil registration was duplicated centrally, and the CONSERVATÓRIA DOS REGISTOS CENTRAIS IN LISBON holds registrations from the former overseas territories. A Portuguese assento de nascimento names BOTH PARENTS AND ALL FOUR GRANDPARENTS — far more than a South African form ever asked. SHE WAS BORN AT LOURENÇO MARQUES ON 4 MARCH 1924 and died at Porto, so she was a Portuguese national to the end and her record should exist on the metropolitan side.

rows.what: Request 18 is dead — superseded by the letter that actually went
rows.note: CLOSED 16 September. Request 18 was drafted and HELD as a separate approach to the researcher about the 1951 ante-nuptial contract. IT NEVER NEEDED TO GO. The contract is in the letter that was actually sent on 16 September — item 3 of three, LEONARD AUBREY ROBERT WEAR and MARJORIE EILEEN DUNLOP born WALKER, certificate 1397 of 1951, flagged to her as THE ONE TO GET IF SHE CAN ONLY GET ONE. Holding it as a separate letter would have been exactly the scattering Ms Xaba complained about, in a different inbox. THE FILE STAYS ON DISK as the record of an approach considered and folded into another.

rows.what: The two Giddins matches — chased the same day, and it is the wrong Giddins family
rows.note: FOUND 16 September, AND FOUND BY A GUARD RATHER THAN BY LOOKING. Publishing the newly proved Giddins generation made check:matches fail, flagging GIDDINS as a surname belonging to a living match holder. The obvious move was to call it a coincidence and add it to the ambiguous list. IT IS NOT A COINCIDENCE. TWO MATCH HOLDERS CARRY THE SURNAME GIDDINS — 43.36 cM with a twelve-person tree, and 62.89 cM with an eighty-nine-person tree and a public pedigree — AND BOTH SIT IN CLUSTER 12. THE ARITHMETIC FITS. James Giddins of Norton End, born about 1815, is Derrick's THREE-TIMES-GREAT-GRANDFATHER: James to Martha to George William Castle to Martha Maud to Leonard to Derrick. A descendant of James through Martha's brothers GEORGE b.1847 or JOHN b.1849 would be a FOURTH COUSIN, expected around 35 cM on a range that runs to 139. 43 and 63 sit comfortably inside it. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ANOTHER MATCH: every piece of DNA evidence this archive holds for the Castle side runs through GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLE AND CAROLINE — the Brown cousins, the Halsey line, all of it. THESE TWO ARE THE FIRST THAT REACH ABOVE HIM, and they do it on his MOTHER'S side, which no paper record had even identified before this morning. NEXT: read the eighty-nine-person tree and look for George or John Giddins of Norton End; check whether the two Giddins matches also match each other and the Brown cousins, because if they match the Browns too the connection is through Caroline and not the Giddinses at all; and TEST THEIR SEGMENTS against the twelve-region Wear signature, which should show NOTHING — a Giddins cousin shares the Castle side only, so overlap with the Wear regions would mean the reading is wrong. *** CHECKED WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CLAIM ABOVE IS WITHDRAWN. *** The larger tree — eighty-nine people, a public pedigree — was opened and read. ITS GIDDINS LINE IS WARWICKSHIRE, NOT HERTFORDSHIRE. Its GEORGE GIDDINS, 1846-1890, whose dates sat so neatly against our George b.1847, WAS BORN ON 17 JULY 1846 AT WITHYBROOK, WARWICKSHIRE and died in the Wandsworth district; HIS FATHER IS RICHARD GIDDINS, NOT JAMES. The surrounding surnames in that tree — Ratcliffe, Conway, Woodhams, Wall, McMellon, Prescott — are nowhere near Baldock. SO THE SURNAME IS NOT THE CONNECTION. The match is real — 62.89 cM is 62.89 cM — but a match holder's surname is only one of eight great-grandparental lines and there is no reason it should be the relevant one. WHAT I DID WRONG, AND IT IS WORTH NAMING: I saw a surname I had discovered that morning, found dates that fitted, and wrote three paragraphs about 'the first DNA to touch the Castle line above George William' BEFORE OPENING THE TREE. The arithmetic I did was sound and the premise was never checked. It took four minutes to check and it was wrong. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT: two real matches at 43.36 and 62.89 cM in cluster 12, connected to Derrick for some reason that is not the Giddins surname; the smaller tree (twelve people) is too thin to read and has not been. THE HERTFORDSHIRE GIDDINSES REMAIN UNTOUCHED BY ANY DNA.

rows.what: The masthead and hero, aligned to the Defranceschi archive
rows.note: DONE 16 September on David's instruction, with the painting he had sent days earlier and the Defranceschi site as the reference. THE PLUMBING WAS ALREADY THERE AND NOBODY HAD NOTICED: index.astro has looked for hero.jpg in site/public since it was written, and its alt text ALREADY DESCRIBED THIS EXACT PAINTING — a railway running away from the viewer, winter in the foreground, dry highveld beyond, a river town at the vanishing point. The image had simply never been dropped in. THE IMAGE: 3.2 MB PNG down to 500 KB JPEG at 1800px, which is the difference between a header and a penalty. THE HERO now follows their pattern rather than sitting under it — a gradient that darkens only the lower third so the sky stays open, a gold letterspaced kicker, the title set OVER the plate, and the page's own h1 suppressed so it is not printed twice. Caption below the band, unchanged: 'An illustration, not a document. Nothing in this archive rests on it.' THE HEADLINE WAS REWRITTEN AFTER LOOKING AT IT. The first version ran to four lines and covered the whole painting; the Defranceschi one is a short concrete claim, so this is now OUT OF EAST PRUSSIA AND MOZAMBIQUE, INTO ONE JOHANNESBURG MARRIAGE, which is three lines and leaves the vanishing point visible. THE MASTHEAD: sticky bar, serif wordmark with ARCHIVE in italic accent, and TWENTY-THREE FLAT LINKS REPLACED BY FIVE GROUPED DROPDOWNS — Start, Our line, Places, People & names, Evidence — with a search pill, and a Menu drawer under 62rem. AND THE PHONE WAS CHECKED AND WAS WRONG: at 375px the caption block had covered the entire painting and there was no picture left. Image height raised to 26rem, headline down to 1.5rem, crop shifted left to 42% so the winter side stays in frame.

rows.what: Aligned to the sibling archives — house stylesheet, fonts, grouped nav. NOT the ring.
rows.note: DONE 16 September on David's instruction to bring this site closer to the Mazza and Defranceschi archives. WHAT THE INVESTIGATION FOUND: those two share a HOUSE STYLESHEET — identical variable names, identical class names, differing only in palette — and a COMPONENT LIBRARY in @daviddef/archive-kit that this archive already depends on and was using for exactly one thing, the work list. The kit ships SiblingArchives, Evidence, AncChart, EraTimeline, SovereigntyTimeline, MarriageChart, Distribution, Numbers, Spine, Search, Atlas, Bloodline and more. WHAT WAS ADOPTED: the house stylesheet, repalletted to this archive's own rust and slate rather than shipping a second set of colours; the three house typefaces, EB Garamond, Libre Franklin and IBM Plex Mono; and ALIAS TOKENS so shared component CSS resolves against the existing palette instead of duplicating it. The grouped dropdown nav and the hero were already done earlier the same day. AND WHAT WAS TAKEN BACK OUT, WHICH MATTERS MORE. I added this archive to the ring of sibling archives and wired the component into the footer. DAVID: 'i dont want the other archives on the luwinski page. not related.' HE IS RIGHT, AND IT IS A CORRECTNESS POINT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. The ring's own sentence reads 'each following a different line of THE SAME FAMILY'. The seven are David's own lines — Istria, Kvarner, Carnia, Sicily, Calabria, the Cape, Ireland. THIS FAMILY IS HIS WIFE'S FATHER'S, out of East Prussia and Portuguese East Africa, and it meets the others nowhere. Publishing it would have made all eight sites assert a relationship that does not exist, in a sentence none of them would have re-read. Removed from the layout and from the kit's own archives.json, so the other seven do not start claiming him either. ONE CHANGE KEPT: the component now reads its count from the file rather than saying 'one of seven' in words, which was wrong the moment an eighth was added and would have been wrong again.

rows.what: /tree/ moved onto the shared five-word evidence ladder — and one claim demoted for it
rows.note: DONE 16 September. The tree page had four hand-rolled marks — proved, inferred, unknown, excluded — invented that morning. The sibling archives share a FIVE-WORD LADDER in @daviddef/archive-kit: DOCUMENTED, a record was read and it says this; PROBABLE, the evidence points one way and nothing points the other; INFERRED, reasoned from what is known and not witnessed in a record; FAMILY, told or written on somebody's chart and not sourced; DISPUTED, two sources disagree and neither has been ruled out. The page now uses the shared component, so a level means the same thing wherever a reader meets it. TWO OF THE OLD FOUR WERE NEVER EVIDENCE GRADES AND ARE NOT FORCED ONTO THE LADDER. 'Unknown' is the ABSENCE of a claim; 'excluded' is a claim TESTED AND FAILED. Both keep their own chips, drawn deliberately unlike the ladder — no fill, dashed edge — so they cannot be mistaken for a grade, and the legend says in capitals that they are not levels. AND THE EXERCISE COST ONE CLAIM, WHICH IS THE REAL VALUE OF IT. GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLE AND CAROLINE WALLIS WERE MARKED PROVED AND ARE NOW MARKED PROBABLE. The marriage, the nine children and the dates came from another researcher's tree, not from records this archive has read. What IS documented, because the 1871 census was pulled and read here, is that a George Castle, 30, agricultural labourer, was at Norton End as SON-IN-LAW to James Giddins with a son George, 8. What is NOT is the birthplace at Willian, the October 1882 marriage and the nine children. THE CENSUS ALSO DISAGREES WITH THAT TREE TWICE — it gives the boy's birthplace as BALDOCK, not Willian, and his birth year as 1863, not 1862. Under the ladder that is exactly what PROBABLE means. The marriage certificate, already on the list, would settle it.

rows.what: JANETTE STAYED — the 1939 Register finds her in Letchworth lodgings seven weeks after her mother sailed
rows.note: DONE 16 September on the Findmypast subscription. The 1939 Register was taken on 29 SEPTEMBER 1939, seven weeks after the Dunvegan Castle left London — so it catches exactly the people who did not go. SEARCHED WEAR AT LETCHWORTH: ONE RESULT, AND IT IS HER. TNA R39/1620/1620C/004/42, 18 RIDGE AVENUE, LETCHWORTH, schedule 279: LOUISA CORBY b. 14 Jan 1870, single, unpaid domestic duties; LOTTIE CORBY b. 3 Mar 1881, single, hand sewer; and JEANNETT (E M) WEAR, B. 28 OCTOBER 1919, SINGLE, CINEMA CASHIER. AN EXACT DATE OF BIRTH WHERE THIS ARCHIVE HAD ONLY 'JANETTE 1919'. AND SHE IS NOT WITH FAMILY. She is nineteen, lodging with two spinster sisters, and working in a cinema. Her mother and the four youngest had sailed for Durban on 10 August; her father had gone in April. SHE STAYED, WITH A JOB AND A ROOM. Note also RIDGE AVENUE against the 9 RIDGE ROAD where her father boarded in 1911 — the same corner of the same small town, twenty-eight years apart. LEONARD IS NOT IN THE REGISTER AT LETCHWORTH OR HITCHIN, which is consistent with his having already gone, BUT IT IS NOT PROOF: the register's own notice says officially closed records are withheld for people not proven dead, and LEONARD'S DEATH YEAR IS PRECISELY WHAT THIS ARCHIVE CANNOT SETTLE — 1973 or 1979. If the National Archives does not know he died, his entry would be closed and would look exactly like absence. A search on WEAR born 1916-1918 returns 61 people and none is a Leonard. Saved to data/wear-1939-register.tsv.

rows.what: CORPORAL L A R WEAR, 141272 — a prisoner of war, and the reason for the silent decade
rows.note: SURFACED 16 September against the BT 27 transcript of Leonard's 1937 crossing and not yet read. FOUR RECORDS: L A R WEAR, GERMANY 1939; and L A R WEAR, GREAT BRITAIN, 1943, 1944 and 1945. TREAT THEM AS A PROBLEM BEFORE TREATING THEM AS A LEAD. A man who sailed from Southampton to the Cape in March 1937 and married at Rosebank, Johannesburg, in September 1940 is not obviously in GERMANY IN 1939, and the 1943-45 Great Britain records sit oddly against a life this archive believes was lived in Johannesburg. THREE READINGS, AND THEY ARE NOT EQUALLY LIKELY. (a) THEY ARE A DIFFERENT L A R WEAR — the initials are not rare and Findmypast's suggestions match on name alone, which is exactly how the Giddins error happened this afternoon. (b) THEY ARE HIM, AND HE CAME BACK — possible, and it would mean the 1937 emigration was not permanent. (c) THE 'GERMANY 1939' RECORD IS A PRISONER-OF-WAR OR CASUALTY INDEX whose date is the campaign rather than the man. WHAT TO DO: open each one and read the service number, the unit and any date of birth BEFORE deciding it is him. If any carries a birth date matching Q1 1917 at Hitchin, that settles it. THIS ALSO BEARS ON ROW 25, the SANDF service record, which assumes he served South African. *** READ 16 SEPTEMBER, AND THEY ARE HIM. *** The row said to treat them as a problem before a lead and to read the service number before deciding anything. THE SERVICE NUMBER IS WHAT DECIDED IT. All five records carry 141272; the rank is CORPORAL; and the force is not a British regiment but the SOUTH AFRICA UNION DEFENCE FORCES. TNA WO 392/15 and WO 392/21, the War Office Directorate of Prisoners of War lists for 1943-1945. HE WAS A PRISONER OF WAR, HELD IN GERMANY, listed in 1943, 1944 and 1945. THE 'GERMANY 1939' TAG THAT LOOKED SO WRONG IS THE CAMP, NOT A POSTING, and the 1939 is the collection's war-span label rather than a date. THE SOUTH AFRICAN FORCE IS WHAT TURNS INITIALS INTO A PERSON. Leonard sailed for the Cape in March 1937, married at Rosebank in September 1940, and was twenty-five when Tobruk fell in June 1942 and something over ten thousand South Africans were taken prisoner in a day. AND IT EXPLAINS THE SILENCE THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN RECORDING FOR WEEKS. Row 41: Leonard cannot be placed between 1941 and 1950 — no address, one recorded fact, a daughter born in 1941. A MAN IN A PRISON CAMP DOES NOT APPEAR IN A DIRECTORY, ON A VOTERS' ROLL OR IN A NEWSPAPER. The hole is not an absence of records; it is an absence of liberty. HELD AS PROBABLE, NOT DOCUMENTED: the lists give INITIALS ONLY AND NO DATE OF BIRTH, so the case rests on initials, force, a fitting age, and one number repeating across five records in two volumes. WHAT SETTLES IT IS THE SANDF SERVICE RECORD AT PRETORIA — row 25, wanted since the archive began and never askable precisely. IT CAN NOW BE ASKED FOR BY NUMBER.

rows.what: Follow-up to SANDF with the force number
rows.note: DRAFTED 16 September, NOT SENT. A FOLLOW-UP INSIDE THE EXISTING THREAD 1a0a3b70c6389154, not a new letter — the Centre already has the 15 September enquiry and a second approach would be the scattering Ms Xaba complained of, in a different inbox. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH SENDING IS THAT IT REMOVES WORK RATHER THAN ADDING IT. The original letter asked, at question 3, whether the medal rolls might yield a force number, and said in as many words that WITH A NUMBER THE REST BECOMES ORDINARY. The number is now in hand: 141272, Corporal, South Africa Union Defence Forces, prisoner of war in Germany, from TNA WO 392/15 and WO 392/21. SO QUESTIONS 3, 4 AND 5 OF THE ORIGINAL ARE WITHDRAWN — no medal-roll search, no nominal index needed. THE CAVEAT IS STATED RATHER THAN BURIED: the POW lists carry initials only and no date of birth, so the identification rests on initials, the South African force, a fitting age and one number repeating across five records. The letter says plainly that 141272 may belong to somebody else and that being told so would be a useful answer. FOUR ASKS: the attestation or personnel record for 141272; whatever it gives for PARENTS OR NEXT OF KIN, which is still the heart of it because South African marriage registers of the period have no parents' column and an attestation form does; the PRISONER-OF-WAR AND REPATRIATION PAPERS, which are sometimes filed separately and are worth asking for now rather than in a second exchange; and THE ADDRESSES GIVEN ON ENLISTMENT AND DISCHARGE, because a discharge address is the first thing that would place him after the war and 1948 is the year that matters. *** SENT 16 SEPTEMBER 2026, message 1a0aa27caa5e8b60, inside the existing thread 1a0a3b70c6389154. *** The chase clock on that thread is reset to a fortnight. IF THEY ANSWER AT ALL, THE ATTESTATION FORM IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS EVER ASKED ANYBODY FOR: the entire Wear chain rests on Leonard being a son of Henry Robert Wear and Martha Maud Castle, and the only source that says so is a seven-person tree built by his own daughter. An attestation form naming his parents would turn that into a government record.

rows.what: TAB MHG 7584/69 — KURT'S OWN ESTATE, and it is not on the researcher's list
rows.note: FOUND MISSING 16 September while going deep on Kurt at David's instruction, AND IT IS THE MOST SERIOUS OMISSION ON THE PRETORIA LIST. Twenty-six references went to the researcher this afternoon — seven Booyzen, seven Wear and Luwinski court files, five Lerena, and the six already agreed — AND KURT'S OWN ESTATE FILE IS NOT AMONG THEM. It has been in this archive's own records for days: ZA TAB MHG_#_7584/69, LUWINSKI, KURT, the estate opened after he died at Johannesburg on 15 December 1968. WHY IT MAY BE THE MOST IMPORTANT MHG FILE IN THE WHOLE ARCHIVE. A South African death notice, form J294, asks THREE things this archive wants and cannot otherwise get. (1) THE DECEASED'S PARENTS. Kurt's father was JACOB LEIBHOLZ, deported to Auschwitz in February 1943, and his mother AUGUSTE LUWINSKI — who did not marry until January 1924, TWELVE YEARS AFTER KURT WAS BORN, which is why he stayed a Luwinski while his younger brother was registered a Leibholz. THE ARCHIVE ASSERTS THAT PARENTAGE FROM GERMAN SOURCES AND HAS NO SOUTH AFRICAN DOCUMENT FOR IT. The J294 would be one, signed by whoever buried him. (2) HIS PLACE OF BIRTH, which would test the East Prussian story against a form filled in by his family rather than by him. (3) AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: THE LIST OF SURVIVING CHILDREN. Derrick was legally Kurt's son and was about twenty when Kurt died. WHETHER THE DEATH NOTICE NAMES HIM — AND HOW — IS A FACT ABOUT WHAT THE FAMILY BELIEVED AND RECORDED IN 1968, twenty years after the marriage that produced him and fifty-eight before the DNA said otherwise. EITHER ANSWER IS WORTH HAVING. HOW IT SHOULD GO, AND NOT BY A THIRD EMAIL TODAY. The researcher has just been sent a long list and told to cut from the bottom; a separate message adding a twenty-seventh item would be exactly the scattering Ms Xaba complained of, in another inbox. SHE HAS NOT YET SENT THE INVOICE, so there will be a natural reply. IT RIDES ON THAT ONE, and it should be marked as belonging near the TOP, not the bottom.

rows.what: How Kurt actually got to South Africa — not through Britain, so the lists are Hamburg's
rows.note: TESTED AND ELIMINATED 16 September, and the elimination is the useful part. Kurt arrived in South Africa in 1933, a German Jew of twenty-one leaving the year Hitler took power, and THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER ESTABLISHED HOW HE TRAVELLED. The obvious test was BT 27, the British outbound passenger lists, because a great many refugees went out through Southampton. SEARCHED ON LUWINSK* ACROSS THE WHOLE SERIES 1890-1960: SIX RESULTS, ALL ONE POLISH FAMILY OF LUWINSKAS SAILING LIVERPOOL TO PORTLAND, MAINE, IN 1908. He is not in it. SO HE DID NOT LEAVE FROM A BRITISH PORT, and the record of his crossing is not at Kew. THAT POINTS SOMEWHERE SPECIFIC: the HAMBURGER PASSAGIERLISTEN, the Hamburg passenger lists, which run to 1934 and are held at the Staatsarchiv Hamburg — or the Bremen lists, most of which were destroyed. A Hamburg entry would give his age, his last residence, his occupation and his destination port IN HIS OWN EMIGRATION YEAR, which is the one document that would show what he left with and what he called himself. NOT REACHABLE FROM THE CURRENT SUBSCRIPTIONS: the Hamburg lists are indexed on Ancestry, which is signed in but not subscribed, and at the Staatsarchiv direct. A single pay-per-view or a trial month would cover it, which is the same narrow case already recorded for the WWI pension records. *** BOUNDED 17 SEPTEMBER RATHER THAN ANSWERED. *** The HAMBURGER PASSAGIERLISTEN run from 1850 TO 1934, so 1933 IS INSIDE THEM — the dates are right and the idea is sound. THE PROBLEM IS ACCESS. They are in practice an ANCESTRY-HELD dataset, and this archive is signed in to Ancestry but NOT SUBSCRIBED. A FAMILYSEARCH ROUTE WAS TRIED AND A FALSE NEGATIVE WAS CAUGHT BEFORE IT WAS BELIEVED. Searching what was taken to be the Hamburg collection for LUWINSKI returned zero — and then the same collection was searched for SCHMIDT, THE COMMONEST GERMAN SURNAME, AND ALSO RETURNED ZERO. THE COLLECTION IDENTIFIER WAS WRONG AND THE FIRST ZERO MEANT NOTHING. That is the third time in a week a control has stopped this archive publishing an empty search as a finding, and it is the reason the control is now run first. WHAT IS LEFT: an Ancestry subscription, which is a purchase and not mine to make; or the Staatsarchiv Hamburg direct. AND A NARROWING WORTH KEEPING: the archive has already excluded Britain through BT 27, and BREMEN'S PASSENGER LISTS WERE ALMOST ALL DESTROYED, so Hamburg is not merely the best remaining door — it is close to the only one. || BLOCKED 20 SEPTEMBER, and the bound is the same one row 119 describes. The Hamburger Passagierlisten run 1850-1934, so 1933 is inside them and the reasoning holds. In practice they are an Ancestry-held dataset and this archive is signed in there but NOT SUBSCRIBED. A FamilySearch route was tried and produced a false negative that a SCHMIDT control caught before it was believed. Nothing further can be done from here without the subscription or a direct order to the Staatsarchiv Hamburg.

rows.what: Pauline had two husbands before Kurt — two new court files
rows.owner: the National Archives of South Africa — NAAIRS is down
rows.note: FOUND 16 September going deep on Kurt. His last wife PAULINE, born RAPPOPORT 1914, died 1985, is carried in the register as 'Pauline Rappoport / Miller (Luwinski)' and nobody had asked what the Miller was. THERE ARE TWO EARLIER MARRIAGES AND BOTH ENDED IN COURT. TAB WLD 583/1944 — ILLIQUID CASE, DIVORCE, PAULINE MILLER (BORN RAPPOPORT) VERSUS JOSEPH. TAB WLD 332/1952 — ILLIQUID CASE, DIVORCE, PAULINE BERMAN (FORMERLY MILLER, BORN RAPPOPORT) VERSUS ISRAEL. So she married JOSEPH MILLER, divorced him in 1944, married an ISRAEL BERMAN, divorced him in 1952, and married Kurt after that. BOTH REFERENCES ARE NEW TO THIS ARCHIVE and are added to litigation.tsv. AND IT COMPLETES A PATTERN NOBODY HAD NAMED. Kurt married at least three times and EVERY WIFE HAD BEEN MARRIED BEFORE: Ivone was a de Witt when he married her in June 1948 and had been married four months; Frances Hostowsky appears in the records as Hostowsky Berner Sefton Luwinski, which is three surnames before his; and Pauline arrived with two divorces behind her. A man who married three much-divorced women in a decade in one city is a fact about the man, not just about them. PRIORITY LOW AS FILES — they are Pauline's marriages, not Kurt's, and neither would name his parents — but they belong on any future Pretoria list and they are cheap to add to one. || BLOCKED 20 SEPTEMBER: NAAIRS has stopped answering altogether — not 503 as on 17 September but no response at all, portal and search service alike, four days running. See row 179. This row cannot move until it comes back, and marking it 'next' overstated what this archive can do.

rows.what: No gazette notice for Kurt's estate, which is itself odd
rows.note: NOTICED 16 September while looking for the executor of MHG 7584/69. South African deceased estates are ADVERTISED IN THE GOVERNMENT GAZETTE — this archive has used exactly those notices to find the Wear estates at Cape Town and the two Figueiredo estates — and the notice names the executor and gives an address for claims. KURT DIED ON 15 DECEMBER 1968 AND HIS ESTATE IS MHG 7584/69, SO A NOTICE SHOULD APPEAR IN 1969 OR 1970. SEARCHED THE GAZETTE FOR LUWINSKI AND LUWINSKY ACROSS 1968 TO 1972: ONE HIT ONLY, and it is the 1972 sequestration brought by Paula Luwinski. NOTHING FOR KURT AT ALL. THREE READINGS AND THE ARCHIVE SHOULD NOT PICK ONE YET. (a) The OCR lost it — entirely possible on these scans, and this archive has already seen 'Figueiredo' rendered as 'Epo .Figueiredo,CarlosDe'. (b) The estate was small enough to be wound up without the advertisement that larger estates require. (c) The notice ran under a spelling nobody has tried. WHAT IT MEANS PRACTICALLY: the cheap route to Kurt's executor is closed, and MHG 7584/69 itself — already raised as the most serious omission from the Pretoria list — becomes the only way to the death notice and the children it names. *** CONTROLLED 20 SEPTEMBER, AND ONE OF THE THREE READINGS IS NOW DEAD. *** The row offered three explanations and said the archive should not pick one. THE FIRST CAN NOW BE ELIMINATED. Reading (a) was that the gazette corpus might not cover 1969 and 1970 properly. IT DOES: searching those years for the phrase every estate notice carries returns 221 issues in 1969 and 163 in 1970 for 'Estates of deceased persons'; 100 and 93 for the Afrikaans 'boedel'; 111 and 101 for 'Master of the Supreme Court'. THE GAZETTES ARE THERE, THEY ARE INDEXED, AND THEY ARE FULL OF ESTATE NOTICES IN EXACTLY THE YEARS HIS SHOULD HAVE APPEARED. Meanwhile LUWINSKI and LUWINSKY return the same EIGHT documents across the entire corpus — three of them the 1942 dissolution of the Oppenheimer partnership, two the 1941 transfer that created it, and one the 1972 Paula Luwinski sequestration — AND NOTHING AT ALL IN 1968, 1969, 1970 OR 1971. The nearest thing to a near-miss was chased and is not him: 'Lewinski' returns one hit in 1969 and one in 1970 and both are VON LEWINSKY in what appears to be a tariff list. READING (b) CANNOT BE ELIMINATED AND THE REASON IS MEASURABLE: the search does no prefix matching — 'Luwinsk' returns ZERO where 'Luwinski' returns eight — so a name the scanner mangled is simply invisible, and this archive has already watched this corpus render Figueiredo as 'Epo .Figueiredo,CarlosDe'. SO IT IS DOWN TO TWO: the OCR lost him, or no notice was ever published. NEITHER CAN BE SETTLED FROM OUTSIDE. What settles it is the estate file itself, TAB MHG 7584/69, which is row 152 and is not on the researcher's list.

rows.what: Tell the second-cousin match that the Martha Giddings line in my letter was wrong
rows.note: RAISED 16 September. The reply sent to him this afternoon contains one sentence that later research contradicts: 'If Martha Giddings died in 1863 she cannot have known her son at all, and I notice your George William is with his grandparents in both 1871 and 1881.' THE DEATH INDEX WAS THEN FOUND — third quarter 1863, Hitchin, volume 3A page 188 — AND HIS BAPTISM IS 4 JANUARY 1863. She lived at least six months past it; the boy was about a year old. SHE KNEW HIM. WHAT TO SAY AND WHAT NOT TO. It is one sentence in a long letter, it was offered as an observation about HIS tree rather than a claim about mine, and he has given no sign of caring either way. IT DOES NOT WARRANT AN EMAIL OF ITS OWN — a correspondent who sends a second message to amend a subordinate clause is a correspondent people stop answering. IT GOES IN THE NEXT REPLY, briefly, with the volume and page so he can check it, AND WITH THE PART THAT IS BETTER THAN AN APOLOGY: the finding itself is new to both trees, and it is his ancestor as much as ours. *** DRAFTED 17 SEPTEMBER, NOT SENT: requests/27-SEND-THIS-to-paul-correction.txt. *** It leads with the correction rather than burying it. THE ERROR: 'If Martha Giddings died in 1863 she cannot have known her son at all' — she died in the THIRD QUARTER of 1863 and he was baptised on 4 JANUARY of it, so she had him for something under a year. Both numbers were already on file and the quarters were never compared. IT ALSO CHANGES THE READING OF THE 1871 CENSUS, which the letter says: the widower is IN the house at Norton End, enumerated son-in-law with his boy as grandson, so he did not give the child away — he went to his dead wife's parents and was still there eight years later, and those two relationship words are the census's own and are now the proof of the line. A second caution goes with it: the same census gives the boy's birthplace as BALDOCK not Willian and his birth year as 1863 not 1862, and the letter says so rather than quietly amending his tree.
