THEN THREE THINGS THAT ARE HIS, not ours: CAROLINE REMARRIED — Q3 1920 Hitchin, Caroline Castle to JAMES JAMES — and was CAROLINE JAMES when she died in 1957, which is the whole reason his great-grandmother cannot be followed past 1916; her exact date of birth is 28 FEBRUARY 1863 from the 1939 Register at 38 Norton Road, not the 1862 every tree carries; and the surname is WALLIS not Walls, six GRO birth entries to none. It closes with Pix Road, flagged as not his line but worth having. Offers images of everything. *** THE ERROR IS NOW NAMED EXACTLY, 20 September. *** The drafted letter says "If Martha Giddings died in 1863 she cannot have known her son at all." THAT SENTENCE IS WRONG. George William Castle was registered in Q4 1862 and Martha Castle died in Q3 1863, so SHE HAD HIM FOR ABOUT NINE MONTHS. The letter is still unsent, so this is a correction to a draft rather than a correction in public - but it is the kind that has to go in before the envelope, not after. The rest of the Martha Giddings paragraph stands, including the reading that a granddaughter born thirty-two years later was christened Martha Maud for her.

rows.what: EMMA REMARRIED — she became Emma Hull, and the whole household is found in 1901
rows.note: FOUND 17 September, and it closes three separate questions at once. EMMA HAWKINS, WIDOWED AT THIRTY-TWO IN 1891, HAD NEVER BEEN FOLLOWED PAST THAT CENSUS. Three direct tests failed: no Emma Wear in Hertfordshire in the 1901 census, no remarriage indexed under Emma Wear, no death. SHE WAS SEARCHED FOR UNDER THE WRONG SURNAME. Coming at it through the children found her at once. 22 MOUNT PLEASANT, ST ALBANS — 1901 census, RG13/1312: JOHN HULL, head, 33, RAILWAY LABOURER; EMMA HULL, wife, 41, BORN ALDENHAM — which is what identifies her, since Aldenham is a small parish and it is her birthplace in both the 1861 and 1871 returns. With ALBERT J HULL aged 6 and EDITH M HULL aged 4, both born St Albans; and LOUISA S A WEAR 18, ROSETTA E WEAR 15, AND HENRY R WEAR 11, ALL ENTERED AS STEP-CHILDREN OF JOHN HULL. WHAT IT SETTLES. (1) Emma remarried about 1893-94 and had two more children. Henry Robert was raised from about four by a stepfather who was a railway labourer. (2) ROSETTA WAS ALIVE AT FIFTEEN and is an APPRENTICE STRAW HAT MAKER — the Hertfordshire county trade, the same industry in which her step-grandmother Elizabeth Giddins was doing 'platting' at Norton End in 1871. She had simply been searched for under Wear in the wrong decades. (3) LOUISA IS CONFIRMED AS LOUISA S A WEAR, which is exactly the form that married a SHENTON at Hitchin in 1918. AND IT OPENS SOMETHING NEW AND DNA-RELEVANT: ALBERT J HULL b.1895 AND EDITH M HULL b.1897 ARE HENRY ROBERT'S HALF-SIBLINGS. Their descendants would share with Derrick THROUGH EMMA HAWKINS ONLY — not through Robert Wear and not through the Castles — which isolates the Hawkins line by itself. No match on the current list carries Hull.

rows.what: 63 AND 72 PIX ROAD — Emma Hawkins was alive, blind and on her son's street when the family sailed
rows.note: FOUND 17 September while looking for Louisa's Shenton household, and it is the most striking thing the Findmypast month has produced. TNA R39/1620/1620G/011/28, SCHEDULE 305, 63 PIX ROAD, LETCHWORTH, taken 29 September 1939: EMMA HULL, BORN 7 FEBRUARY 1859, WIDOWED, 'INCAPACITATED - BLIND'; LOUISA SHENTON, born 29 November 1882, married; WILLIAM SHENTON, born December 1876, 'INCAPACITATED'. EMMA HULL IS EMMA HAWKINS. Born at Aldenham, married Robert Wear at Southwark in 1881, widowed in 1890, remarried John Hull about 1893, AND WIDOWED A SECOND TIME BY 1939. At eighty she is blind and living with the daughter who was eight when her father died. HER EXACT DATE OF BIRTH IS NOW KNOWN and it comes from the best kind of source — a woman of eighty giving it to a registrar in person. SO IS LOUISA'S: 29 NOVEMBER 1882. AND THE ADDRESS IS THE FINDING. HENRY ROBERT WEAR AND MARTHA MAUD RAISED SIX CHILDREN AT 72 PIX ROAD. HIS MOTHER AND HIS SISTER WERE AT 63 PIX ROAD. THE SAME STREET, a few doors along, in a garden city of eight thousand that had not existed forty years earlier. IT GIVES THE EMIGRATION A SHAPE IT DID NOT HAVE. Leonard went in March 1937, his father in April 1939, his mother in August with the four youngest — and the register, taken seven weeks after that ship sailed, finds still in Pix Road an eighty-year-old blind woman and the daughter keeping her, with Janette in lodgings half a mile off on Ridge Avenue. THE RECORD SAYS WHO WAS WHERE AND NOTHING ABOUT WHAT ANYBODY FELT, and the page says so. BUT IT IS NO LONGER TRUE THAT THE FAMILY SIMPLY LEFT. Still open: no children are in the Shenton household, so whether Louisa had any — the independent test of the Wear half — is unanswered; she was 57 and any would have gone.

rows.what: AT LEAST TWO CASTLE CHILDREN HAVE NEVER BEEN NAMED — Caroline bore nine and one was already dead in 1911
rows.note: OPENED 17 SEPTEMBER by the fertility question on the 1911 census. RG14/7572, schedule 173, St Mary's Cottages, Baldock: CHILDREN BORN 9, STILL LIVING 8, DIED 1. Against that this archive holds SEVEN names — George William 1884, Ada May 1887, Fredrick James 1889, Agnes Kate 1892, MARTHA MAUD 1895, Florence Margaret H 1901, Ernest Albert C 1904 — of which six came from the GRO birth index searched on the mother's maiden name WALLIS. SO TWO ARE MISSING AND ONE OF THE NINE DIED BEFORE APRIL 1911. WHERE THEY WILL BE: the gaps are 1889-1892 and 1895-1901, and the second gap is six years wide in a family that otherwise produced a child every two or three. HOW TO FIND THEM: re-run the GRO birth index on mother's maiden name across ALL spellings, not only Wallis — Walls, Wallice, Wallace — because the missing two may simply be mis-indexed; then the Baldock burial register for a Castle infant. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COMPLETENESS: an unidentified son is another chance at a Castle male line, and the only Castle male line this archive has is Frederick James, who has now vanished twice. *** WORKED THE SAME AFTERNOON, AND THE METHOD FAILED IN AN INSTRUCTIVE WAY. *** The plan was to re-run the birth index on every spelling of WALLIS. THAT IS NOT THE PROBLEM. MARTHA MAUD'S OWN BIRTH ENTRY — Q3 1895, Hitchin, volume 3A page 561 — HAS NO MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME IN THE INDEX AT ALL; THE FIELD IS BLANK. So the search that found six was never going to find nine, whatever it was spelt: it returns the children whose entries happen to carry the field and drops the others in silence, and the woman this archive descends from is one of the ones it drops. A FILTER ON A FIELD THAT IS SOMETIMES EMPTY IS A FILTER ON THE INDEXING, NOT ON THE FAMILY. THE DISTRICT SEARCH DOES NOT RESCUE IT EITHER: Castle births at Hitchin between 1884 and 1906 run to FOUR PAGES, because there are at least three unrelated Castle families in the town. WHAT IS LEFT, AND IT IS THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT ANYWAY: the BAPTISM REGISTER, which names both parents on every line. Martha Maud was baptised at Baldock on 22 September 1895, so the family used it. Findmypast's Hertfordshire Baptisms set has Castles at Baldock back to 1693 and would not take a year filter in the URL, so this needs the search form rather than a crafted address — or the Hertfordshire Archives register itself. THE TWO MISSING CHILDREN ARE STILL MISSING, and the gaps are still 1889-1892 and 1895-1901. *** WORKED TO ITS BOUND 17 SEPTEMBER, AND THE ROW IS STILL OPEN — but it is open for a known reason now. *** The plan was the BALDOCK BAPTISM REGISTER, which names both parents on every line. ALL 823 CASTLE BAPTISMS IN THE HERTFORDSHIRE SET WERE SORTED BY MOTHER'S FIRST NAME AND THE CAROLINE BLOCK READ. IT CONTAINS EXACTLY ONE ROW. Between the Barbara block and the Catharine block there is a single Caroline, and it is ADA MAY CASTLE, BAPTISED 10 APRIL 1887 AT WESTON. THE REASON IS A COVERAGE BOUND, NOT A SEARCH FAILURE: sorted by baptism year descending, the LATEST of 195 Castle baptisms at Baldock is 1879, and Caroline's children were born 1884 to 1904. THE INSTRUMENT ENDS FIVE YEARS BEFORE THE FAMILY STARTS. Martha Maud's own Baldock baptism of 22 September 1895 is not in the set either. SO THE TWO UNNAMED CHILDREN REMAIN UNNAMED, and the answer is at HERTFORDSHIRE ARCHIVES in the parish register itself, not in any index anybody can search from here. *** AND THEN IT CLOSED, the same afternoon, from the household rather than the register. *** THE 1901 CENSUS HAS THE WHOLE FAMILY: RG13 piece 1298, folio 49, page 26, SCHEDULE 192, NORTON END, NORTON, BALDOCK — George W Castle 36 a farm labourer, CAROLINE 36 born WESTON, and five children: George W 16, Ada 14, FREDERICK 11, Agnes K 9, and MARTHA 5. THEY HAD GONE BACK TO NORTON END, the hamlet where George William was himself raised by his GIDDINS grandparents in 1871 and 1881 after his mother died. He brought his own family home to it. THE NINTH CHILD IS SARAH ANN WALLIS, born 19 August 1882 at Maiden Street, Weston — TWO MONTHS BEFORE HER PARENTS MARRIED, AND REGISTERED UNDER HER MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME. She is not a Castle birth in the index at all, which is exactly why no search for Castle births could ever have returned her. AND THE ONE WHO DIED IS NAMED AND DOCUMENTED: SIDNEY CHARLES CASTLE, born Q2 1898 at Hitchin and DIED Q4 1900 AT HITCHIN, AGED TWO. One entry in the birth index, one in the death index, no competitors. He was gone five months before the 1901 census, which is why no census ever showed him. NINE BORN, EIGHT LIVING, ONE DIED — AND THE ARITHMETIC NOW CLOSES EXACTLY: Sarah Ann 1882, George William 1885, Ada May 1887, Fredrick James 1889, Agnes Kate 1892, Martha Maud 1895, Sidney Charles 1898-1900, Florence 1901, Ernest 1904. THE SIX-INSTEAD-OF-NINE WAS THREE SEPARATE INDEXING FAILURES, not one: Sarah Ann is filed under WALLIS; Martha Maud's entry has a BLANK mother's maiden name; and Sidney Charles never came back on that search either. A FILTER ON A FIELD THAT IS SOMETIMES EMPTY IS A FILTER ON THE INDEXING, NOT ON THE FAMILY — and this row is the proof of it.

rows.what: FREDERICK JAMES CASTLE FOUND — Sergeant, Cameronians (Scottish Rifles), 10061, and a career soldier into the 1920s
rows.note: THE EXCLUSION IS NOW DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN ASSERTED, 17 September. Frederick James Castle, born 1889 at Hitchin to a mother nee Wallis, is Martha Maud's brother and THE ONLY CASTLE MALE LINE THAT COULD EVER CARRY A Y TEST. The obvious candidate death — FREDERICK JAMES CASTLE, Hitchin, 1975 — BELONGS TO SOMEBODY ELSE. The 1939 Register has that man at 17 ORCHARD ROAD, BALDOCK, BORN 10 APRIL 1887, 'Vertical Driller On Aircraft Work', married to Ella, with a third person in the household whose record is officially closed. Same name, same town, two years out. AND BALDOCK SUPPLIES A THIRD: the 1921 census has an entirely separate Castle household at 5 CEMETERY ROAD — head James Castle, nine children — with its own Frederick, 33 years 2 months, a hydraulic press operator at Letchworth. THREE MEN OF ONE NAME IN ONE SMALL TOWN INSIDE TWO YEARS, which is exactly why name-only identification at Baldock is worthless. WHAT IS LEFT OF OUR MAN: he is in no Hertfordshire census in 1911, in no census in 1921, in no 1939 Register entry, and in NO ENGLISH DEATH INDEX BETWEEN 1889 AND 2007 under any Fred-form of the name. FOUR THINGS COULD EXPLAIN THAT and they are testable: he died in the Great War, at 25 in 1914 (check Soldiers Died and the CWGC register); he emigrated, which this family demonstrably did; he died abroad; or he is the one of the nine who was dead by 1911, in which case the 1889 birth and an infant burial at Baldock should meet. THE FIRST IS THE ONE TO RUN, because a war death would also be a record naming his mother and her address. 17 September, while checking Frederick: THE 1901 CENSUS PRODUCES A THIRD BALDOCK FREDERICK AND HE IS NOT OURS EITHER. RG13 piece 1298 folio 48 page 23 schedule 175, NORTON END, BALDOCK: head JAMES CASTLE, 38, farm labourer; wife ANNIE; ten in the household; and FRED CASTLE, 13, farm labourer, born 1888. The same family is at MIDDLE ROW, BALDOCK in 1891 — RG12/1105 f.45 — with Fred aged 4 and a brother ARTHUR aged 2. SO THE BALDOCK FREDS ARE: ours b.1889 to George William and Caroline; the b. 10 April 1887 man of 17 Orchard Road who died in 1975; and this one, b.1888, son of James and Annie of Norton End. THREE UNRELATED CASTLE HOUSEHOLDS AND THREE BOYS OF ONE NAME INSIDE TWO YEARS. It also explains the 1901 census hit that looked promising: it is the third family, not the first. *** THE TRAIL PICKS UP AGAIN, 17 September, and it runs through a barracks. *** HE IS IN THE 1901 CENSUS AFTER ALL: FREDERICK CASTLE, SON, 11, at NORTON END with George W and Caroline — RG13/1298 f.49 p.26 sch 192. The earlier 1901 search that came back wrong had found the OTHER Norton End Castle family, three schedules away. AND IN 1911 THERE IS A BALDOCK-BORN FREDERICK CASTLE, AGED 21, SINGLE, AT MEEANEE BARRACKS, COLCHESTER — RG14 piece 10304, schedule 9999, Military Road and Mersea Road. HE WAS A SOLDIER, which is why he is in no Hertfordshire household in 1911. THE AGE IS THE DISCRIMINATOR AND IT IS THIN BUT REAL: 21 at 2 April 1911 means born between April 1889 and April 1890, which fits ours and EXCLUDES the Norton End Fred of the other family (23) and the Orchard Road man of 1887 (24, and he is at Baldock that night). IT IS NOT PROOF. The entry says FREDERICK, not Frederick James, and it rests on one census age and a birthplace. IT IS LABELLED PROBABLE AND NOT MORE. WHAT IT CHANGES: the 1921 census has ONE Baldock-born Frederick Castle in the whole of England and Wales and it is the b.1888 man of the other family, so ours is gone from the country by 1921. A regular soldier of 1911 who is not in Soldiers Died and not in the death index either went abroad and stayed, or died in a service Soldiers Died does not cover. NEXT: the regiment at Meeanee Barracks in 1911, then the medal rolls and the service papers for a Frederick Castle of that regiment. *** THE UNIT IS NAMED, and it took the original image rather than the transcript. *** The Findmypast transcript leaves the occupation column empty. THE IMAGE DOES NOT. Column 5 of the barracks return — 'UNIT, or ARM OF SERVICE' — reads SCOTTISH RIFLES, written once at the head of the sheet and carried down every line by ditto. That is THE CAMERONIANS (SCOTTISH RIFLES), and the surrounding pages of the same return confirm it: Malcolm Campbell, Duncan Sinclair, and men born at Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Dunbartonshire, Ayrshire, Roxburghshire and Kirkcudbright. A Hertfordshire farm labourer's son among them is unusual and is exactly what the regular army did. He is a PRIVATE, 21, single, born Herts Baldock, at MEEANEE BARRACKS, Colchester, on the night of 2 April 1911. AND IT IS STILL LABELLED PROBABLE. The entry says Frederick, not Frederick James, and the identification rests on one age and one birthplace — which is precisely the shape of the three mistakes this archive has made in the last week. WHAT IT UNLOCKS: a named regiment turns an impossible search into an ordinary one. The Cameronians' medal rolls, the medal index cards and the service papers can all be searched for a Frederick Castle, and a service record would carry his NEXT OF KIN — which would name George William Castle and Caroline and settle the whole thing. *** AND THE REGIMENT FOUND THE MAN, the same afternoon. *** BRITAIN, FIRST WORLD WAR CAMPAIGN MEDALS, TNA WO 329/1120: FRED JAMES CASTLE, SERGEANT, SERVICE NUMBER 10061, CAMERONIANS (SCOTTISH RIFLES), previous unit '2nd Sco Rif. 10061 Sgt.', awarded the BRITISH WAR MEDAL AND VICTORY MEDAL. HIS MEDAL INDEX CARD, TNA WO 372/4 (Discovery D1734236), gives the whole career on one line: SERGEANT THROUGHOUT, THREE NUMBERS — 10061 Scottish Rifles, 195568 MACHINE GUN CORPS, and 7815432 Scottish Rifles. THIS MORNING THE IDENTIFICATION RESTED ON ONE CENSUS AGE. IT NOW RESTS ON TWO INDEPENDENT MATCHES ARRIVED AT FROM OPPOSITE ENDS: the medal roll says FRED JAMES, which is exactly how the GRO registered him at Hitchin in 1889; and it says CAMERONIANS (SCOTTISH RIFLES), which is what the 1911 barracks return says in column 5 over Frederick Castle's line. AND THE THIRD NUMBER EXPLAINS EVERY ABSENCE THIS ROW WAS BUILT ON. 7815432 IS AN EIGHT-DIGIT NUMBER AND THE ARMY BEGAN ISSUING THOSE IN 1920. HE WAS STILL A SERGEANT AFTER THE WAR — which is why he is in no 1921 household, no 1939 Register and no English death index. HE WAS A CAREER SOLDIER, and career soldiers of the 1920s were mostly abroad. STILL NOT PROVED, AND THE FILE SAYS SO: the medal roll carries no date of birth and no birthplace, so the link is forenames plus regiment and not a document stating identity. A SERVICE RECORD WOULD STATE IT, because it names next of kin — and next of kin would be George William Castle and Caroline. ONE THING TO CHECK RATHER THAN BELIEVE: he has the War and Victory medals and NO 1914 OR 1914-15 STAR, although the 2nd Battalion went to France in November 1914. Either he was not with them, or he was on home or garrison service until 1916, or the Star roll has simply not been searched. It has not. NEXT: the service papers. A pre-1920 regular's papers are in WO 363/364 if they survived the 1940 fire; a man still serving in 1920 may have a record held to this day by the Ministry of Defence and obtainable by a next-of-kin application.

rows.what: FAMILYSEARCH HOLDS ELEVEN SOUTH AFRICAN RECORD SETS AND THIS ARCHIVE HAS ONLY EVER USED THE INDEX BEHIND ONE OF THEM
rows.note: FOUND 17 SEPTEMBER while running the full-text row, and it is the more useful half of that morning. Searching the ordinary record index rather than the full-text one, surname WEAR, country SOUTH AFRICA, returns 16,156 rows across sets this archive has never touched: SOUTH AFRICA, CIVIL MARRIAGE RECORDS 1801-1974; SOUTH AFRICA, GAUTENG, JOHANNESBURG, CEMETERY RECORDS 1840-2019; SOUTH AFRICA, CHURCH OF THE PROVINCE OF SOUTH AFRICA (ANGLICAN) PARISH REGISTERS 1801-2004; SOUTH AFRICA, WESTERN CAPE, DECEASED ESTATE FILES 1951-2011; SOUTH AFRICA, CAPE, PROBATE RECORDS OF THE MASTER OF THE HIGH COURT 1822-1990; SOUTH AFRICA, PIETERMARITZBURG ESTATE FILES 1846-1950; SOUTH AFRICA, NATAL CIVIL DEATHS 1863-1955 and NATAL CIVIL MARRIAGES 1845-1955; KWAZULU NATAL VITAL RECORDS 1868-1976; CAPE CEMETERY RECORDS 1872-2011; and the Dutch Reformed and Netherdutch Reformed registers. WHAT IT ALREADY PROVED IN TWO MINUTES: BOTH OF LEONARD'S MARRIAGES ARE INDEXED THERE — Rosebank, 7 September 1940 to Phyllis Agnes Robertson, and Johannesburg, 30 October 1951 to Marjorie Eileen Dunlop — in South Africa, Civil Marriage Records. This archive found both the hard way, through court files and a register image. WHAT IT COULD ANSWER NEXT, and these are rows that have been open for a fortnight: the JOHANNESBURG CEMETERY set covers 1840-2019 and WEST PARK IS A JOHANNESBURG CEMETERY, so LEONARD'S BURIAL — and with it the 1973-or-1979 question — may simply be sitting in an index; the WESTERN CAPE DECEASED ESTATE FILES 1951-2011 is the set behind the two Cape Town estates already being asked for by letter; and the ANGLICAN PARISH REGISTERS would carry a Rosebank marriage if it was Anglican rather than Catholic. A DECOY TO WRITE DOWN NOW, BEFORE IT COSTS SOMEBODY A DAY: there is an entirely separate WEAR FAMILY IN DURBAN — Cecil Joseph Wear and Katie, with children baptised at Durban from 1913 to 1931, and Cecil Wentworth Wear who married Doreen Mary James in 1933. They are not ours and they will dominate any surname search. *** WHY THIS IS BLOCKED AND NOT RUNNING: THE FAMILYSEARCH SESSION EXPIRED MID-SEARCH and the site now asks for the password. I do not sign anybody in. David, when you next have a minute, sign in to FamilySearch in the browser and say so, and this goes from blocked to done in an afternoon. *** *** RUN AND CLOSED 17 SEPTEMBER, AND THE ROW UNDERSTATED IT. THERE ARE NOT ELEVEN SOUTH AFRICAN RECORD SETS. THERE ARE THIRTY-TWO. *** All 3,502 FamilySearch collections were enumerated through /service/search/hr/v2/collections and filtered; the list, with ids and counts, is in data/familysearch-south-africa.tsv. Then surname WEAR was matched EXACTLY - q.surname.exact=on, which drops the 16,156 fuzzy rows to 111 - and ALL 111 WERE READ, together with 2 for LUWINSKI and 24 for FIGUEIREDO. THE FINDINGS FILE FIRST SAID FIVE NEW RECORDS AND THE HONEST NUMBER IS TWO. Three of the five were already on this site, one of them far better than the index has it: the Germiston register of Ivone's first marriage has been READ, entry 27 of 1948 before magistrate A. J. Rossouw, and Frances's remarriage to Rolf Eisenhardt on 23 May 1958 has been published on Kurt's page for days. Written down because the error is the useful part: AN INDEX ENTRY AGREEING WITH A PAGE YOU HAVE ALREADY READ IS NOT A DISCOVERY. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW. (1) PHYLLIS AGNES WEAR MARRIED ROBERT SELWYN NORQUOY ON 14 JUNE 1952 AT MALVERN, JOHANNESBURG, aged 37 - ark 1:1:6ZHR-NR73. The archive had her second surname from a court index and no idea where it came from; WLD 790/1957 is Leonard suing a woman who had been remarried for five years, and she remarried seven and a half months after he did. (2) KATHLEEN EDITH WEAR AND JAMES CECIL FOOT, 26 MAY 1945 - the marriage was known from GenDatabase, which is a transcription. THE RECORD IS NEW AND SO IS WHAT IT IS: an ANGLICAN parish register, the first documentary evidence of this family's denomination in South Africa. (3) One further marriage is withheld because the bride may be living; it is in notes/, which is gitignored, and David has the decision. THE DECOY THE ROW PREDICTED WAS REAL: the Durban Wears are the majority of the 111. A SECOND DECOY IS NEW - LEONARD ANTHONY WEAR of the Western Cape, a different man with a different middle name, whose wife's estate file is indexed. AND THE NEGATIVE HELD: Leonard Aubrey Robert Wear appears in FamilySearch's ENTIRE South African holdings EXACTLY TWICE, both marriages, and he is under none of WARE, WEIR, WIER, WEARE, WEARNE or WEARS either.

rows.what: THE SHENTON LINE IS CLOSED — Louisa had one child and he died in the quarter he was born
rows.note: ANSWERED 17 SEPTEMBER, and the answer is no. The Pix Road find opened one specific question: LOUISA SHENTON WAS HENRY ROBERT WEAR'S SISTER, so a descendant of hers would carry the WEAR half of Derrick's ancestry AND NOT THE CASTLE HALF — the independent test this archive has wanted since the segment reading, and the one thing that could separate the couple. No children were in the 1939 household, and the transcript confirms it held EXACTLY THREE PEOPLE with no officially closed records hidden in it. SO THE INDEXES WERE ASKED DIRECTLY. Births, surname SHENTON, mother's maiden name WEAR: ONE RESULT — STANLEY W SHENTON, Q1 1924, HITCHIN. Deaths, surname Shenton, born 1924: STANLEY W SHENTON, Q1 1924, HITCHIN. BORN AND DIED IN THE SAME QUARTER. His mother was forty-one. AND THE MOTHER'S-MAIDEN-NAME TRAP WAS AVOIDED THIS TIME, because it had just caught this archive over Martha Maud: the district was searched as well, surname SHENTON, HITCHIN, 1916 TO 1936, WITH NO MOTHER'S NAME AT ALL. ONE RESULT. THE SAME ONE. Shenton is a Staffordshire surname and there is exactly one Shenton birth in the whole Hitchin district across twenty-one years. THE MARRIAGE: WILLIAM SHENTON married a WEAR at Hitchin in Q3 1918, when Louisa was thirty-five. THE REST OF THE HOUSEHOLD, now traced end to end: WILLIAM SHENTON, born December 1876, 'Incapacitated' in 1939, DIED Q3 1953 at Hitchin. LOUISE S A SHENTON DIED Q4 1967 AT HITCHIN, AGED 84 — and the initials close it, because her birth is registered as LOUISA SARAH A WEAR. AND THAT BIRTH GIVES A PLACE NOBODY HAD: Q1 1883, KINGSTON, SURREY. Robert Wear and Emma Hawkins married at Southwark in 1881 and their son Henry Robert was born at St Olave Bermondsey in 1889 — IN BETWEEN THEY WERE AT KINGSTON. WHAT THIS COSTS: the Wear half can no longer be tested through Louisa. WHAT IS LEFT: Henry Robert's other siblings, and the two Hull half-siblings ALBERT J b.1895 and EDITH M b.1897, who carry Emma's DNA but not Robert Wear's — which is a different and still useful test, because a Hull cousin should match Derrick on the HAWKINS side ALONE.

rows.what: ELECTORAL REGISTERS 1832-1932 — WITHDRAWN AS A NAME SEARCH. The set is page images and indexes no elector at all
rows.note: *** WITHDRAWN 18 SEPTEMBER, THE DAY AFTER IT WAS WRITTEN, AND THE ERROR WAS MINE. *** I wrote here that a search returned NINE ELECTORAL REGISTER ENTRIES FOR WILLIAM WEAR, Surrey and London, 1885 to 1900, and called it the best unworked source for the Bermondsey Wears. I HAD NOT OPENED ONE. Opened, EVERY ROW IN THAT RECORD SET SAYS 'NO NAME ON RECORD' and carries a PDF icon. They are page images of volumes, not entries about people. THREE CONTROLS SETTLE IT. (1) Searching WILLIAM WEAR with no place filter returns 3,478 rows and the locations are DEVON and DURHAM — Weare in Devon and the River Wear in Durham. It is matching a place name, not a surname. (2) Searching JOHN SMITH returns the same kind of nameless rows in Lancashire and Warwickshire, which is not what a name index does. (3) Searching LUWINSKI returns ZERO, and a nonsense name returns zero too — so the fields are not inert, they simply match something that is not an elector. The 'Surrey & London' locations I quoted yesterday came from MY OWN PLACE FILTER, not from any name. WHAT I DID WRONG, AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME IN A WEEK: I read a RESULT COUNT as a FINDING. The Giddins matches, the two archives-index zeroes, and now this. A count is a property of a search box. WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING: the Bermondsey volumes for 1885 to 1900 ARE digitised and ARE browsable page by page, and an electoral register is still an annual address record covering the years that bracket both brothers' deaths in 1890. IT IS AN AFTERNOON OF READING IMAGES, NOT A SEARCH, and it is now filed as that. The caution already attached still stands: before 1918 the franchise is a property franchise, so lodgers and all women are absent and a silence means nothing about a life. || CLOSED 20 SEPTEMBER. The withdrawal was published, the replacement set (1910-1932, name-indexed) was found and worked in row 165, and its limit was established. There is nothing further to do on this row and it should stop appearing as work.

rows.what: ADA MAY CASTLE BECAME ADA MAY SMITH — married surname settled; the death still open
rows.note: FOUND 17 SEPTEMBER while following the one baptism the register did yield. THE TREE THIS ARCHIVE HARVESTED FROM A MATCH HOLDER RECORDS 'Ada May Castle, died Jul 1969, Hitchin'. SHE MARRIED ON Q4 1909 AT HITCHIN, volume 3A page 1171, aged twenty-two. AND THE DEATH INDEX HAS NO SUCH ENTRY: Ada-anything Castle born 1884 to 1890, all England and Wales, returns sixteen rows and NOT ONE is at Hitchin and NOT ONE is in 1969. A WOMAN WHO MARRIED IN 1909 DID NOT DIE A CASTLE IN 1969. This is the CAROLINE JAMES trap in miniature — a tree recording a death under a maiden surname its owner had not used for sixty years — and it is the second time in two days that the same mechanism has hidden a woman from this archive. HER MARRIED SURNAME IS UNKNOWN AND IS NOT GUESSED HERE. Findmypast's MarriageFinder offers THOMAS REDMAN or SIDNEY SMITH; those are page-mates in an index and not a marriage, and this archive has now refused that particular temptation three times in one day. WHAT SETTLES IT: the certificate, 3A/1171, which names the husband and her father on one line and would confirm George William Castle at the same time. AND THE GENERAL LESSON, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN ADA MAY: every married daughter in that tree with a death recorded under CASTLE is now suspect. Agnes Kate married a Brown. Martha Maud married a Wear. Florence and the rest need checking the same way. *** SETTLED 17 SEPTEMBER, AND IT TOOK NO CERTIFICATE. *** THE 1911 CENSUS HAS HER UNDER HER MARRIED NAME: RG14 piece 7595, schedule 300, 27 CHURCHYARD, HITCHIN — ADA MAY SMITH, WIFE, 24, BORN BALDOCK HERTS, MARRIED 1909, YEARS MARRIED 2, ONE CHILD BORN AND ONE LIVING; head AMOS SMITH; her husband SIDNEY SMITH; their son also Sidney. THREE STRANDS ARRIVED AT SEPARATELY AND THEY MEET: the GRO marriage index (Ada May Castle, Q4 1909, Hitchin, 3A/1171), the census household, and MarriageFinder's page-mate suggestion of a SIDNEY SMITH. THE THIRD STRAND WAS WORTHLESS ON ITS OWN AND THIS ARCHIVE SAID SO THREE TIMES TODAY. It counts for something now only because the first two were found without it. HER DEATH REMAINS OPEN AND THE TREE'S VERSION OF IT STILL DOES NOT EXIST. The tree says 'died Jul 1969, Hitchin' under CASTLE; there is no such death under Castle at Hitchin in any year. WHAT THERE IS: ADA MAY SMITH, BORN 1887, DIED Q3 1969 — AT SPILSBY, LINCOLNSHIRE. Q3 IS JULY TO SEPTEMBER, SO THE TREE'S DATE IS RIGHT AND ITS SURNAME AND DISTRICT ARE WRONG, which is what happens when somebody finds a date and fills the rest in from assumption. BUT SMITH IS THE COMMONEST SURNAME IN ENGLAND and Lincolnshire is a long way from Hertfordshire. THIS ARCHIVE IS NOT ASSERTING THAT THE SPILSBY WOMAN IS HER. What is settled is the surname she died under, and it was not Castle. *** WORKED 20 SEPTEMBER AND DEFEATED BY THE SURNAME, WHICH IS WORTH MEASURING RATHER THAN SAYING. *** Ada May Castle married Sidney Smith, and SMITH is where she leaves the record. England and Wales death index, forename ADA MAY, born 1885-1889: THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-ONE CANDIDATES nationally. Narrowed to Hertfordshire with a wildcard on the forename: seventeen Ada Smiths and NOT ONE OF THEM CARRIES THE MIDDLE NAME MAY. The only Hitchin entry is Rose Ada Smith, 1889-1974, who is somebody else. THEN THE 1939 REGISTER, which prints exact dates of birth and would have keyed the death index in one step: TWO Ada Smiths in the whole county in her birth window, neither of them May. AND HER HUSBAND IS GONE TOO - Sidney Smith, born 1879-1889, at Hitchin in 1939: NIL. SO THE SMITHS LEFT HERTFORDSHIRE, and a national search on that surname and that forename is not a search. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK, and neither has been tried: probate, which indexes by exact date of death and address; or the 1921 census, which would give the household ten years after the 1911 entry at 27 Churchyard, Hitchin and might give a destination.

rows.what: A SECOND ELECTORAL REGISTER SET EXISTS AND IT IS NAME-INDEXED — 1910 to 1932, and Hertfordshire Castles are in it
rows.note: FOUND 17 SEPTEMBER, and it partly rescues the row withdrawn this morning. The set this archive tested and withdrew is ENGLAND & WALES, ELECTORAL REGISTERS 1832-1932, which returns page images and indexes no elector: every row says 'No name on record'. THERE IS A SECOND, DIFFERENT SET — ENGLAND & WALES, ELECTORAL REGISTERS 1910-1932 — AND IT CARRIES NAMES. A search for Castle in Hertfordshire returns rows like ARTHUR FREDERICK CASTLE 1929 and 1930, and FREDERICK CASTLE 1919 and 1920. WHAT IT CANNOT DO is the thing the withdrawn row wanted: it starts in 1910, and the question was about BERMONDSEY 1885 TO 1900, which brackets the two Wear brothers' deaths in 1890. For that, the images still have to be read by eye. WHAT IT CAN DO: place the BALDOCK CASTLES year by year from 1919, which is the decade in which Caroline became Caroline James and moved to Letchworth, and in which Frederick vanishes. THE CAUTION FROM THIS MORNING STILL APPLIES IN A NEW FORM: before 1918 the franchise was a property franchise; from 1918 it widens but still excludes women under thirty until 1928. An absence is not a death. *** WORKED 17 SEPTEMBER, AND IT BOTH DELIVERS AND DISAPPOINTS. *** THE SET IS REAL AND IT IS NAME-INDEXED: surname CASTLE at BALDOCK returns 356 ENTRIES across 1919 to 1932, by name and by year and by season — spring and autumn registers separately. That is the annual address record the withdrawn row wanted, and it exists. AND A FREDERICK CASTLE IS ON THE BALDOCK ROLL EVERY YEAR FROM 1919. Thirty-one Fred-form entries in that polling district. *** BUT IT CANNOT TELL US WHICH FREDERICK, AND THAT IS THE DISAPPOINTMENT. *** The transcript was opened — BL/ER/1919/D20, British Library SPR.Mic.P.16/BL.H.57 — and it carries NAME, YEAR, SEASON, POLLING DISTRICT AND CONSTITUENCY AND NOTHING ELSE. NO ADDRESS. NO AGE. Baldock had THREE Frederick Castles — ours born 1889, the 17 Orchard Road man born 10 April 1887, and the Cemetery Road man born about April 1888 — and an index of bare names cannot separate them. THE ADDRESS IS ON THE PAGE IMAGE AND NOT IN THE INDEX, so this is an afternoon of reading images if it is ever to answer. ONE THING IT DOES SAY, THOUGH, AND IT FITS: ERNEST ALBERT CYRIL CASTLE IS NOT ON THE BALDOCK ROLL AT ALL. He was twenty-one in 1925 and should have been, had he still lived there. He does not, WHICH AGREES WITH THE 1921 CENSUS PUTTING HIM AT 9 BOSCOMBE PLACE, LETCHWORTH, as James James's step-son.

rows.what: FREDERICK JAMES CASTLE'S SERVICE PAPERS — not at Kew, because he was still serving; they are the MoD's
rows.note: OPENED AND IMMEDIATELY BOUNDED, 17 September. The service record is the document that would turn a strong identification into a proved one, because AN ATTESTATION FORM NAMES NEXT OF KIN — and next of kin would be GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLE and CAROLINE of Norton End. IT IS NOT AT KEW. All 78 Fred* Castle entries in WO 363 (the 'Burnt Documents') and WO 364 (pension claims) were read: NOT ONE is Scottish Rifles, Cameronians, or number 10061. AND THAT IS THE EXPECTED ANSWER, not a disappointment. Those two series hold men whose service ENDED BY ABOUT 1920; a man still serving kept a live record that never went to the Public Record Office. His medal card gives him 7815432, an eight-digit post-1920 number. THE SERIES CANNOT CONTAIN HIM BY DEFINITION. WHERE IT IS: with the MINISTRY OF DEFENCE, Army Personnel Centre, Glasgow. WHY THIS IS BLOCKED AND OWNED BY DAVID RATHER THAN BY ME: the MoD releases a service record to the NEXT OF KIN, or to anybody on production of a DEATH CERTIFICATE plus a fee, and THIS ARCHIVE HAS NO DEATH FOR HIM AT ALL. So the application needs either a death record this archive has not found, or a next-of-kin claim, and a next-of-kin claim is a statement about who somebody is that only the family can make. I am not filling in a form on anybody's behalf and I am not claiming a relationship for anybody. THE CHEAPER THING TO TRY FIRST, AND IT IS MINE: he is absent from the English death index because he was abroad. A soldier of the 1920s died, married and had children in ARMY REGISTERS — the British Army chaplains' returns and the consular and service registers — and those are indexed separately from the ordinary GRO series. That search has not been run. *** THE CHEAPER THING WAS TRIED FIRST, THE SAME AFTERNOON, AND IT CAME BACK EMPTY. *** BRITISH ARMED FORCES AND OVERSEAS DEATHS AND BURIALS, surname CASTLE forename FRED*: ten results, none of them Scottish Rifles and none of them 10061. The nearest by name is FREDERICK J CASTLE who died in 1917 — PRIVATE 47783, NORTHUMBERLAND FUSILIERS, Roclincourt Valley Cemetery, France. BRITISH ARMED FORCES AND OVERSEAS BANNS AND MARRIAGES, surname CASTLE: ALL FIFTY-NINE READ across three pages and NOT ONE IS A FRED. Those Castles marry at Malta, Kolar, Istanbul, Singapore, Italy, Aldershot and Johannesburg. AND THE CONTROL WAS RUN BEFORE THE NEGATIVE WAS BELIEVED: John Smith in the same marriage set returns 251 results from Lisbon in 1726 onward, so the set is real and was pointed at the right place. WHAT IS LEFT, AND IT IS NARROWER THAN IT WAS: he did not die in the war, he did not die on army service abroad under that name, and he did not marry in an army chapel abroad under it. He is in no English census after 1911, no 1939 Register and no English death index. HE LEFT AND DID NOT COME BACK, and the rest of his life is in a country this archive has not identified. The service record remains the one document that would say which.

rows.what: THE NATIONAL ARCHIVES DISCOVERY CATALOGUE — 219 commits citing Kew, and the catalogue had never been opened
rows.note: RAISED 17 SEPTEMBER, AT DAVID'S PROMPTING, AND IT IS A GAP RATHER THAN A DISCOVERY. This archive has published RG10, RG11, RG12, RG13, RG14, RG15, BT 27, WO 329, WO 372 AND WO 392 — hundreds of references to records held at Kew — AND HAD NEVER ONCE OPENED THE CATALOGUE THOSE REFERENCES BELONG TO. Every one came second-hand through a commercial index's transcript. THE FIRST HOUR PRODUCED FOUR THINGS. (1) EVERY CITATION VERIFIES, and two verify BETTER than they were published: WO 392/15 is specifically 'SECTION 5: SOUTH AFRICA (UNION DEFENCE FORCES)', which is exactly the claim made about Leonard Wear, and WO 329/1120 adds the page range 312-622. (2) WO 372/4/50790 — THE EXACT ITEM REFERENCE for Fred James Castle's medal card, in Kew's own words: 'Scottish Rifles 10061 Serjeant. Scottish Rifles 7815432 Serjeant. Machine Gun Corps 195568 Serjeant.' Findmypast gave only the piece, and PRINTED THE DISCOVERY ID D1734236 ON ITS OWN TRANSCRIPT. This archive had that id for hours and never followed it. (3) DP/12/1/14 and DP/12/1/15, BALDOCK ST MARY THE VIRGIN, Hertfordshire Archives — registers of baptisms 1880-1895 and 1895-1910. The register this archive has been gesturing at all day is now an orderable reference. (4) LUWINSKI RETURNS ZERO across 2,500+ British archives, filed as a bounded negative with the reason a catalogue is not a name index. A REUSABLE TOOL WENT IN WITH IT: tools/tna.py, with a --verify mode that reads a reference back from the catalogue. WHY THIS IS RUNNING AND NOT DONE: the whole back catalogue of citations should be run through --verify, not just the nine tried today; the Hertfordshire registers for NORTON and WESTON have not been found in Discovery at any phrasing and may need HALS asked directly; and the WO 392 South African POW sections should be enumerated so the Leonard Wear identification cites the right volume for each of 1943, 1944 and 1945. *** PUBLISHED 17 September: Discovery is now named on /sources/ with what it verified and what it corrected. *** *** THE FULL SWEEP IS DONE, 17 September. *** Forty-four distinct archival references were extracted from the data files and the pages and each was read back from the catalogue. FORTY-TWO VERIFIED EXACTLY ON THE FIRST PASS. TWO RESOLVED AFTER ONE CORRECTION. NONE WAS WRONG, MISSING OR MISATTRIBUTED. AND THE TWO WERE THE SAME MISTAKE TWICE, AND IT IS NOT REALLY OURS: RG 15/7079 and RG 14/7576 both carry a LEADING ZERO in the piece number, which is how FINDMYPAST PRINTS THEM AND NOT HOW KEW DOES. Without the zero both resolve, and both describe LETCHWORTH (PART) in the Baldock sub-district — exactly what this site says they are. THE CATALOGUE ALSO CONFIRMED THE CONTENT AND NOT MERELY THE EXISTENCE: RG 11/574 is '5K St James Bermondsey' (Jamaica Road), RG 10/641 is '5J St James Bermondsey' (the father's house), HO 107/1560 is 'BERMONDSEY (Street Indexed)', RG 12/1120 is '2C Watford', RG 13/1312 is 'St Albans', RG 14/10304 is 'Colchester South-East' (the barracks), and the three BT 27 pieces are Southampton February-March 1937, London April-June 1939 and London August-October 1939 — Leonard's sailing, his father's and his mother's, in the right ports in the right months. ONE FALSE POSITIVE WAS IN THE EXTRACTION AND NOT IN THE SITE: the pattern pulled 'ED 26' out of a census citation, where it means ENUMERATION DISTRICT 26, and the catalogue matched a Board of Trade series of that name. The site never cited it; the script did.

rows.what: THE BERLINER ADRESSBÜCHER — free, digitised, full-text, annual, and never opened until today
rows.note: RAISED 17 SEPTEMBER out of David's question about the Leibholz and Luwinski families. THE ENTIRE LINE LIVED IN BERLIN AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEVER LOOKED IN THE BERLIN DIRECTORY. The Zentral- und Landesbibliothek Berlin has digitised the Berliner Adressbücher FROM 1799 TO 1970, one volume a year, each 6,000 to 7,500 pages, listing householders by NAME, TRADE AND STREET. It is free, needs no account, and answers a JSON query at digital.zlb.de. tools/zlb.py now wraps it. 1,047 PAGE HITS FOR LEIBHOLZ. 23 FOR LUWINSKI. WHAT CAME OUT FIRST — A SURNAME LEAVING A CITY, MEASURED WITH A CONTROL. Leibholz page hits per annual volume: 24 in 1933, holding between 15 and 24 through the thirties, then 12 in 1940, FIVE in 1941, six in 1942, TWO IN 1943. AND THE CONTROL IS NOT AN IDLE ONE: THIMM — Johanna Thimm of Sauerbaum is Kurt's own great-grandmother, East Prussian and not Jewish — runs 66, 53, 47, 65, 72, 68, 45, 75, 69, 63 AND 75 IN 1943. As common in the last volume as in the first. The scanner did not get worse, the Fraktur did not get harder, the book did not get smaller. Bergmann is flat at around 700. Hirschfeld declines but far less steeply, which this archive cannot explain and does not pretend to. THE LIMITS ARE WRITTEN INTO THE FILE AND THEY MATTER MORE THAN THE NUMBER: a page hit is a page and not a person; twenty-four to two is a small base; and DEPORTATION, EMIGRATION AND ADMINISTRATIVE EXCLUSION FROM DIRECTORIES ALL LOOK IDENTICAL IN A COUNT. Jews were being struck out of German commercial listings from 1938 quite apart from being deported. THE COUNT CANNOT TELL THOSE APART. AND A LEAD: THE LUWINSKIS OF BERLIN ARE IN THE GARMENT TRADE. 1933 and 1936 give ALFRED LUWINSKI, BÜGLER — a garment presser — at N31 PUTBUSSER STRASSE 24 in Wedding; by 1943 an A. Luwinski is a Kraftwagenführer, a lorry driver. LIZZY WAS A DRESSMAKER AND MILLINER. Luwinski is not a common Berlin name — twenty-three pages in a hundred and seventy years of directories — and Joachim Luwinski and Johanna Thimm will have had children besides Auguste. A BROTHER IS THE OBVIOUS GUESS AND IT IS A GUESS, and Putbusser Straße 24 is a checkable address. NEXT, AND THE ORDER MATTERS: read the ALPHABETICAL NAME SECTION rather than the street section for 1924 to 1943 and find JACOB at Meraner Straße 2, Schöneberg, year by year — the year he stops appearing is the year the record of his life in that city stops; find AUGUSTE before 1924 under LUWINSKI and after it under LEIBHOLZ, and after the war under FRICKE; and follow the post-war Luwinskis of 1957 to 1970, because Lizzy lived until 1975. ONE HONEST DIFFICULTY: the OCR is Fraktur and the columns jam, exactly as the South African gazettes did. Counting works; reading a named line needs the page image. *** AND IT IS NOW ON THE SITE RATHER THAN IN A FILE, 17 September. *** The year-by-year table with its Thimm control is published on /leibholz/ under 'A surname leaving a city', with the three limits stated in the same panel — a page hit is not a person, the base is small, and deportation, emigration and administrative exclusion look identical in a count. The Luwinski garment-trade entries are on /east-prussia/, labelled a lead and not a finding. Both sources are now named on /sources/. *** WORKED PROPERLY 20 SEPTEMBER, AND THE FIRST FINDING IS THAT THE METHOD WAS WRONG. *** The page counts in this row - 24 in 1933 falling to 2 in 1943 - COUNTED FOUR SECTIONS AT ONCE. A Berlin volume has Teil I (householders and firms, one entry each), Teil II (the trades index, where one firm recurs), Teil III (institutions) and Teil IV (the street directory, where every tenant recurs). In 1933, twenty-four pages carried LEIBHOLZ AND EXACTLY ONE OF THEM WAS TEIL I. A count across all four measures the book as much as the family, and the Thimm control does not rescue it because it has the same problem. The name section has been read on its own for every volume 1920 to 1943; it is not consistently titled and is identified by position. *** ITEM 9 IS ANSWERED. *** 1933, page 1671, read straight off: "LuwinSki Alfred Bügler N31 Putbusser Str 24" - ALFRED LUWINSKI, A GARMENT PRESSER, A HEAD OF HOUSEHOLD. And that SEPARATES HIM FROM THE AROLSEN ALFRED LUWINSKI BORN 09.09.1917, who would have been sixteen: a boy of sixteen is not a householder and not a qualified presser. Not the same man, and the likeliest reading is father and son. He stays age-compatible with being Lizzy's brother and that is still not proved. LUWINSKI REACHES THE HOUSEHOLDER SECTION IN ONE YEAR OF THE WHOLE RUN. *** AND A THREAD NOBODY HAD PULLED. *** The Leibholz entries in Teil I are not scattered households, they are BUSINESSES, and they are in the clothing trade: Jaques Leibholz & Co., KONFEKTION, W8 Krausenstraße, 1924 to 1934; M. Leibholz, TRIKOTAGEN und WOLLWAREN, C2 Rosenstraße 17, 1929 to 1938; and SAMUEL LEIBHOLZ, "HÜTE EN GROS" - HATS, WHOLESALE. KURT LUWINSKI KEPT A HAT SHOP, THE PICCADILLY HAT, AT 81 ELOFF STREET, JOHANNESBURG. LIZZY WAS A DRESSMAKER AND MILLINER. The trade did not start in Johannesburg. Also in the run: William Leibholz, Generaldirektor and STADTRAT, 1920; Felix Leibholz, herring and anchovies; Louis Leibholz; Leo Leibholz & Co. *** AND HERE IS WHERE IT STOPS, DELIBERATELY. *** From 1939 the only thing the text layer returns under the name is the printer's cross-reference "Leibholz s. a. Leipholz" and a LEIBHOLD Wilhelm, who is a different surname. IT WOULD BE EASY AND WRONG TO PUBLISH THAT AS THE FAMILY VANISHING IN 1939: page 1719 of the 1939 volume comes back as ONE UNBROKEN BLOCK of seventeen thousand characters with the columns interleaved, its running head still says Leibholz, and whether an entry sits under it IS NOT LEGIBLE. ITEMS 7 AND 8 - Jacob at Meraner Straße 2 year by year, and Auguste under three surnames - ARE NOT ANSWERED for the same reason. WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED TOWARDS THEM: the Meraner Straße house block is page 5637 of 1936 and page 5715 of 1938, and in 1936 THE TENANT LIST FOR MERANER STRASSE 1 TO 5 HOLDS NO LEIBHOLZ - so if the 1939 census is right that Jacob, Auguste and Siegfried were at number 2, they arrived after 1936. Two individual Leibholz entries do surface in the street section after the firms stop: a PENSIONÄR in 1938 and a WIDOW in Schöneberg in 1940, neither legible enough to name. Full working in data/berlin-adressbuch-names.tsv. *** AND THEN CORRECTED AGAIN, THE SAME AFTERNOON, ON THE SAME PAGE. *** The reading above — that from 1939 the only thing left under the name is the cross-reference — IS WRONG, and the cause is a typesetting convention rather than the record. IN A GERMAN DIRECTORY ONLY THE FIRST ENTRY OF A RUN SPELLS THE SURNAME AND EVERY ENTRY AFTER IT BEGINS WITH A DASH. Searching for the string 'Leibholz' finds one line in ten. Followed properly, THE 1940 VOLUME HOLDS ELEVEN LEIBHOLZ HOUSEHOLDERS: a master butcher, a police official, a widow, a pensioner, a clerk, an administrator, a bank official, the hat wholesaler, and two Wilhelms. So this row has now measured the wrong thing twice in one day — first by counting four sections of the book as one, then by counting one line of a run as the whole run. THE THIRD READING IS THE ONE TO TRUST AND IT IS IN data/berlin-adressbuch-names.tsv. WHAT CAME OUT OF IT: the identification of Samuel (row 177), the 1938 decree visible in the listing, AND ITEM 8 PARTLY — 'AUGUSTE, Witwe, Schöneberg, BADENSCHE STR 9' in 1940, with a conflict stated rather than smoothed: Jacob Leibholz was not deported until 26 February 1943, so a widow in 1940 is either a different Auguste, an error, or something about that marriage this archive does not know. 1942 AND 1943 ARE NOT COUNTED AT ALL, because the dash run breaks in the text layer and a short run cannot be told from a lost one without the image. *** CLOSED 20 SEPTEMBER ON THE FOURTH READING, FROM THE PAGE IMAGES. *** The text layer was exhausted and this row said so. THE IIIF IMAGES ARE NOT: digital.zlb.de serves every page at full resolution and the Fraktur is perfectly legible at three to four times magnification — the same technique that rebuilt the West Park cemetery registers. ITEM 7 IS ANSWERED. 'Jaques Kaufm Schönebg MERANER STR 2' is in the 1938 volume and the 1939 volume AND NO VOLUME AFTER — and item 7 asked exactly that, because 'the year he stops appearing is the year the record of his life in that city stops'. THE ANSWER IS 1939. He was deported on 26 February 1943; the directory loses him three volumes earlier. Bracketed on the other side: the 1936 street section lists the tenants of Meraner Straße 1 to 5 and no Leibholz is among them, so the household arrived between 1936 and 1938. ITEM 9 was already answered. ITEM 8 IS NOT, and is now precisely bounded: Auguste appears in ONE volume, 1940, as a WIDOW at Badensche Straße 9 in the same borough — and Jacob was alive until 1943, so the archive will not join them. She has never been looked for under LUWINSKI before 1924 or FRICKE after the war. *** AND THE COUNT THIS ROW SPENT THREE READINGS TRYING TO GET RIGHT. *** Householders: 17 in 1938, 11 in 1939, 10 in 1940, 9 in 1941, 6 in 1942, 4 in 1943. BUT THE NUMBER IS NOT THE FINDING; THE NAMES ARE. In 1940 Samuel is listed as 'Israel'. In 1941 two more men carry it and both have lost their trade in one year — a FLEISCHERMEISTER becomes an ARBEITER, a VERTRETER becomes a BAUARBEITER. IN 1942 EVERY NAME CARRYING 'ISRAEL' IS GONE. The four who survive to 1943 are exactly the four who never carried it. THE DIRECTORY MARKS THEM AND THEN LOSES THEM. What the count still cannot do is tell deportation from emigration from erasure — but it is now a list of named households with trades and street numbers, so each can be chased one at a time.

rows.what: THE 1938 NAME DECREE IS NOW ON THE SITE AS A DOCUMENT — and its §2(3) answers half of the Kurt question
rows.note: DONE 17 SEPTEMBER, at David's request for a copy of the decree to show. IT IS THE ZWEITE VERORDNUNG ZUR DURCHFÜHRUNG DES GESETZES ÜBER DIE ÄNDERUNG VON FAMILIENNAMEN UND VORNAMEN, 17 August 1938, promulgated the 18th — REICHSGESETZBLATT 1938, TEIL I, NR. 130, SEITE 1044, signed by Stuckart for the Interior Ministry and Gürtner for Justice. THE PAGE SCAN IS NOW HOSTED ON THE SITE at /rgbl-1938-1044.png, from Wikimedia Commons out of the Austrian National Library's digitised Reichsgesetzblatt. It is PUBLIC DOMAIN as a published German law, which is why it can be shown rather than linked. AND READING IT RATHER THAN PARAPHRASING IT MOVED THE ARGUMENT. THIS ARCHIVE'S STANDING OBJECTION TO KURT CARRYING 'ISRAEL' WAS THAT HE HAD LEFT IN 1933 AND WAS IN JOHANNESBURG BY 1939. § 2 (3) DISPOSES OF IT IN ITS OWN WORDS: 'Hat der Anzeigepflichtige seinen Wohnsitz oder gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Ausland, so ist die im Abs. 2 Satz 1 vorgesehene Anzeige an Stelle der Ortspolizeibehörde DEM ZUSTÄNDIGEN DEUTSCHEN KONSUL zu erstatten.' The decree was written with emigrants in mind, names the consulate as the office you report to, and routes births and marriages registered abroad to Standesamt I in Berlin. A MAN IN JOHANNESBURG IN 1939 WAS INSIDE ITS REACH AND THE MACHINERY FOR REACHING HIM IS SPECIFIED IN THE TEXT. AND § 1 (2) CLOSES THE OTHER DOOR: the decree does not apply to 'Juden, die eine fremde Staatsangehörigkeit besitzen'. KURT HELD NONE. This archive established separately, and for entirely different reasons, that he never naturalised — an alien for thirty-five years who died one in 1968. THE EXEMPTION THAT WOULD HAVE RELEASED HIM IS THE EXACT THING HE DID NOT HAVE. WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT PROVE, AND THE PANEL SAYS SO: it does not establish that Kurt was classed a JUDE rather than a MISCHLING, because the decree says only 'Juden' and leaves the definition to the Reich Citizenship Law — that is still the Geltungsjude question, and the Berlin Gemeinde membership registers are still what would settle it. Nor is there any document showing Kurt personally notified a consul. WHAT THERE IS: a law that reached South Africa, a man it was not exempt from, and the name on his records.

rows.what: AROLSEN — JACOB, AUGUSTE AND KURT ARE ALL ON ONE DOCUMENT, DocID 11214358
rows.note: WORKED 17 SEPTEMBER. It had sat on the sources page under 'identified, not yet worked' since 14 September. THE INDEX IS VISIBLE WITHOUT CONSENTING TO ANYTHING and it holds 213 Leibholz person entries. CONFIRMED FROM A SECOND INDEPENDENT BODY OF RECORDS: JAKOB LEIBHOLZ, 08.08.1884, SCHUBIN — exactly the Gedenkbuch; he appears three times, once French-spelled as JACQUES, which suggests a displaced-persons or tracing document rather than a German one. OSKAR LEIBHOLZ, 13.05.1887, SCHUBIN, four entries. SIEGFRIED LEIBHOLZ, 05.08.1925 — Kurt's brother, to the day. TWO THINGS THAT ARE NEW RATHER THAN CONFIRMING. FIRST, THE COMPULSORY NAME IS ON THE FAMILY'S OWN RECORDS: 'LEIBHOLZ, ISRAEL OSKAR' and 'LEIBHOLZ, GEORG ISRAEL'. The 1938 decree published on /kurt/ today is no longer only a law quoted at these people — here are two of them carrying what it forced on them. SECOND, THERE IS A TRACING CASE FOR OSKAR: T/D no. 52.971, 'LEIBHOLZ, OSCAR born 13.05.1887', FOURTEEN DOCUMENTS. Somebody, after the war, asked the International Tracing Service what had become of him. WHO ASKED IS INSIDE THAT FILE, and the likeliest askers are a brother who got out or a widow who did not. A DISCREPANCY TO CARRY RATHER THAN RESOLVE: Arolsen gives GEORG as born 07.06.1885 where the Gedenkbuch gives 7 June 1884. Same day, same month, different year. AND SAMUEL IS THE ONE ABSENCE — nothing under 'Leibholz Samuel', although Yad Vashem and the Gedenkbuch both have him. Only twenty-five of the 213 entries were read, so HE MAY BE ON A PAGE NOT YET TURNED. Recorded as unfinished, not as a negative. *** AND THEN KURT. *** LUWINSKI, KURT, 11.05.1912 — his date of birth to the day — DocID 11214358, filed under '1 Incarceration Documents / 1.2 Miscellaneous / 1.2.1 DEPORTATIONS AND TRANSPORTS / Part 24: Folder MFN01335', reference 10000375 24, five hundred documents. KURT LEFT IN 1933 AND DIED IN JOHANNESBURG IN 1968. HE WAS NOT DEPORTED. The obvious readings are that he is named INSIDE a document about somebody else — a next of kin, an address, an emigrated son on a form about his father — or that a five-hundred-document folder is simply mixed. THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN WRONG THREE TIMES IN A FORTNIGHT BY READING A GOOD FIT AS A FINDING and it is not doing it again on this subject. *** WHY THIS ROW IS BLOCKED AND OWNED BY DAVID. *** Opening any of these documents requires ticking Arolsen's DECLARATION OF CONSENT — 'I hereby declare my consent to using sensitive personal data in accordance with applicable national laws and provisions.' THAT IS A DECLARATION A NAMED PERSON MAKES ABOUT THEIR OWN CONDUCT. I do not tick it on anybody's behalf; the rule was set at the start of this work and has not changed. Everything harvested above came from the index, which needs no consent. WHAT TO OPEN FIRST IF DAVID CONSENTS, IN ORDER: (1) DocID 11214358, because it is Kurt and nobody knows why he is there; (2) tracing case T/D 52.971 for Oskar, because it names whoever was looking for him; (3) the Jacques-spelled Jacob record, because a French rendering means a particular kind of file. ONE PRIVACY NOTE FOR THE SAME SEARCH: the Luwinski index also returns two post-war births that this archive's own register already omits as LIVING PEOPLE, and they are not named here or anywhere on the site. *** AND THEN IT GOT MUCH BIGGER, THE SAME AFTERNOON. *** A search for AUGUSTE returned somebody this archive did not know was in the persecution records at all: LEIBHOLZ, AUGUSTE, MAIDEN NAME LUWWINSKY, BORN 28.08.1893. THAT IS LIZZY, and the archive had her as 1893-1975 with no date. IT NOW HAS 28 AUGUST 1893. The maiden name is spelt LUWWINSKY with a DOUBLED W — a seventh spelling of this surname, German rather than South African, now added to /names/. THEN THE DOCUMENT IDS WERE COMPARED AND THEY ARE THE SAME ONE. Jacob b.08.08.1884, Auguste b.28.08.1893 and Kurt b.11.05.1912 ALL RESOLVE TO DocID 11214358, folder MFN01335, reference 10000375 24, under Deportations and Transports. THE FATHER WHO WAS DEPORTED, THE MOTHER WHO WAS NOT, AND THE SON WHO HAD BEEN GONE TEN YEARS, ALL THREE NAMED ON A SINGLE SHEET. THIS MORNING'S CHARITABLE GUESS — that Kurt was 'named inside a document about somebody else' — NOW HAS EVIDENCE INSTEAD OF GOODWILL: the somebody else is his father, and his mother is on it too. WHAT IS STILL INFERENCE AND MUST STAY LABELLED: THE SHARED DocID IS A HARD FACT FROM THE INDEX; WHAT KIND OF DOCUMENT IT IS, IS NOT. It could be a transport list, a property declaration, a Gestapo household record or a post-war reconstruction. Nobody here has read it and nobody here will tick a consent declaration on David's behalf to. IT IS THE ONLY WARTIME GERMAN DOCUMENT KNOWN TO CARRY KURT'S NAME, and if David consents to one thing in this archive, this is the one. *** UNBLOCKED AND OPENED 20 SEPTEMBER, David having ticked the consent declaration. *** DocID 11214358 IS A BERLIN POLICE HOUSEHOLD REGISTRATION CARD, printed form Vordruck Nr. 258, nationality 'Pr'. Three rows: LEIBHOLZ, JACQUES — 8.8.84 — SCHUBIN — religion 'mos.'; his wife AUGUSTE GEB. LUWWINSKY — 28.8.93 — SAUERBAUM; and 'Kind: SIEGFRIED — 5.8.25 — Bln-Schöneberg'. THE CARD SPELLS HIM JACQUES, which is the third independent source for the form of his name after the 1938 directory and the Mapping the Lives index, and it gives SAUERBAUM as Auguste's birthplace from a Berlin police file rather than a census card. THE RIGHT-HAND COLUMN IS A DATED LIST OF ADDRESSES running from 1913 into the 1930s, each paired with a landlord's name — Landsberger Str, Barbarossastr 17, Freisinger Str 15 from 1.6.33 — WHICH IS THE FAMILY'S MOVE HISTORY AND HAS NOT BEEN FULLY TRANSCRIBED; the scan is 976 pixels and the hand is Kurrent. The reverse lists the seven other indexed names — Schmidt, Puff, Heinicke, Herzog, Biere, Koch, Nicksch — WHO ARE LODGERS, not family. ONE HONEST GAP: KURT IS INDEXED TO THIS DocID AND IS NOT LEGIBLE AS A ROW ON THE CARD. *** AND THE ROW NAMED ITS OWN NEXT STEP, WHICH IS NOW ALSO UNBLOCKED: *** 'THERE IS A TRACING CASE FOR OSKAR: T/D no. 52.971, LEIBHOLZ, OSCAR born 13.05.1887, FOURTEEN DOCUMENTS. Somebody, after the war, asked the International Tracing Service what had become of him. WHO ASKED IS INSIDE THAT FILE.' THAT FILE CAN NOW BE OPENED. It is the single most promising unopened thing in Arolsen for this family, because a tracing enquiry names the enquirer and their relationship. See the new row.

rows.what: YAD VASHEM NAMES THE TRANSPORT — Jacob went out of Berlin on TRANSPORT 30, 26 February 1943
rows.note: WORKED 17 SEPTEMBER. This archive had used ONE Yad Vashem list — Jews murdered in Auschwitz — and had never searched the database itself. LEIBHOLZ returns 88 VICTIM RECORDS, 3 DATA-SUBMITTER RECORDS and 8 further, across the List of Murdered Jews from Germany (47), the LIST OF DEPORTATION FROM BERLIN (41), PAGES OF TESTIMONY (18) and the Theresienstadt inmate list (8). *** THE TRANSPORT. *** Jacob's record, 13520936, carries a field this archive has never had: 'DETAILS OF TRANSPORT: TRANSPORT 30 FROM BERLIN TO AUSCHWITZ BIRKENAU, EXTERMINATION CAMP, POLAND, ON 26/02/1943.' The date has been on these pages for a fortnight. THE TRANSPORT NUMBER HAS NOT. It also gives his permanent residence as BERLIN and his CITIZENSHIP AS GERMANY. *** AND A SECOND MEMORIAL BOOK NOBODY HERE KNEW THEY WERE STANDING ON. *** That deportation record is sourced NOT to the Bundesarchiv but to the GEDENKBUCH BERLINS DER JÜDISCHEN OPFER DES NATIONALSOZIALISMUS, Freie Universität Berlin, Edition Hentrich, Berlin 1995 — BERLIN'S OWN MEMORIAL BOOK, a different work from the national one cited on every page of this site, and the source of the transport number. IT SHOULD BE CONSULTED DIRECTLY for Auguste, for Siegfried, and for an address. OSKAR, record 13449776: Berlin to THERESIENSTADT 17/03/1943, Theresienstadt to AUSCHWITZ 16/10/1944, DATE OF DEATH 16/10/1944 — the same day the second transport left. A DISCREPANCY RESOLVED IN THE BUNDESARCHIV'S FAVOUR: Yad Vashem gives GEORG as born 1884, agreeing with the Gedenkbuch and DISAGREEING with Arolsen's 1885. Two against one, and the two are the older and better-sourced. LYDIA LEIBHOLZ appears on the LODZ GHETTO list, 1885 and 1886 in two records — which is where this archive already believed Georg's wife Lydia née Perl died, on the same day he did. AND A BERLIN LEIBHOLZ FAMILY THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER ACCOUNTED FOR: WILHELM 1890, ELSE 1889, RUTH 1923, LIESELOTTE 1923, WALTER 1922, CHANA 1938, HEINRICH 1890, ALBERT 1886, MAX 1877, HANS ISRAEL 1912 of Preussisch Friedland — most on the deportation list. WHETHER ANY IS A COUSIN IS UNKNOWN AND IS NOT GUESSED. But Sally Leibholz and Friederike Schmul had more sons than this archive has names for, and a Berlin Leibholz of the right age is where a fifth would show. *** A DECOY WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE IT COSTS SOMEBODY A DAY: 'KURT LEIBHOLZ, 1927, BERLIN, MURDERED'. THAT IS NOT OUR KURT. *** Ours is Kurt LUWINSKI, born 11 May 1912, who left in 1933 and died in Johannesburg in 1968. A Kurt of the same city fifteen years younger, murdered, is exactly the near-match this archive has been caught by three times in a fortnight. TWO OF THE 18 PAGES OF TESTIMONY HAVE NOW BEEN READ — SEE THE ROW BELOW. The remaining sixteen were not, and a Page names WHO SUBMITTED IT — a living relative writing down a dead one. The three data-submitter results (Heinrich Leibholz 1890, Mathilde Binder 1888, Sally Binder 14/01/1884) are not obviously ours but were not run down.

rows.what: TWO NAMED RELATIVES WHO SURVIVED — Irmgard Shtern, Georg's NIECE, and Margot Cox, Elli's COUSIN
rows.note: FOUND 17 SEPTEMBER by opening two of the eighteen Pages of Testimony. A PAGE OF TESTIMONY IS A FORM FILLED IN BY A PERSON WHO KNEW THE DEAD, and it names that person and their relationship. ELLI STRUZIK NÉE LEIBHOLZ, Yad Vashem 13689593, Page item 1819733: born 07/11/1915 at Berlin — which matches this archive's register to the day; FATHER GEORG; MOTHER LYDIA; MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME PERL; married to HARRY; a SECRETARY; twenty-six years old; deported BERLIN to the ŁÓDŹ GHETTO on 01/11/1941 and ŁÓDŹ to CHEŁMNO on 13/05/1942. *** SUBMITTED BY MARGOT COX, COUSIN. *** GEORG LAIBHOLZ, Page item 1684365: born 1883; married LIDIA née PERETZ; of Berlin; PROFESSION FACTORY OWNER. *** SUBMITTED BY IRMGARD SHTERN, NIECE. *** *** WHAT THESE TWO NAMES ARE NOT: KURT'S RELATIVES ON ANY EVIDENCE THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS. *** The position argued at length on /leibholz/ is that GEORG IS NOT JACOB'S BROTHER — Jacob born Schubin in Posen 8 August 1884, Georg born Hammerstein in West Prussia two months earlier, and two men cannot be brothers on those dates. Margot Cox and Irmgard Shtern belong to GEORG'S LINE. *** AND THAT IS PRECISELY WHY THEY ARE WORTH EVERYTHING. IRMGARD SHTERN IS GEORG'S NIECE, SO HER PARENT WAS GEORG'S SIBLING — AND GEORG'S PARENTS ARE THE ONE FACT THAT WOULD SETTLE WHETHER HIS LINE TOUCHES SALLY LEIBHOLZ AND FRIEDERIKE SCHMUL OF SCHUBIN AT ALL. A NIECE IS ONE GENERATION FROM THE ANSWER TO A QUESTION THIS ARCHIVE HAS HAD OPEN SINCE DAY ONE. *** THREE FACTS CONFIRMED THAT WERE ASSERTIONS: Georg's wife WAS Lydia née Perl, and it is on her daughter's Page in a cousin's hand; Elli's death is no longer 'after 13 May 1942' but 13 MAY 1942 AT CHEŁMNO; and Georg was a FACTORY OWNER, which this archive did not know. THREE DISCREPANCIES CARRIED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: Georg's birth year is now 1884 (Bundesarchiv and the Yad Vashem list), 1885 (Arolsen) and 1883 (this Page) — three sources, three years. Lydia's maiden name is PERL on one Page and PERETZ on the other. And Georg's place of death is AUSCHWITZ on his Page but CHEŁMNO via Łódź on the deportation lists; A PAGE OF TESTIMONY IS WRITTEN FROM MEMORY YEARS LATER BY SOMEBODY WHO WAS NOT THERE, so the deportation list wins and this archive keeps Chełmno. NEXT: read the other sixteen Pages, because one of them may be for Jacob, Samuel or Oskar and may be signed by a Leibholz; and search Yad Vashem by SUBMITTER for SHTERN and for COX, because a person who filled in one Page usually filled in several. *** WORKED 20 SEPTEMBER, AND THE WHOLE SURNAME WAS SWEPT RATHER THAN TWO PAGES. *** 99 results in the Shoah Names Database for LEIBHOLZ: 88 about victims, across seven sources — List of Murdered Jews from Germany 47, List of Deportation from Berlin 41, PAGE OF TESTIMONY 18, Theresienstadt inmates 8, List of Persecuted Persons 5, Lodz ghetto inmates 3, Jews Murdered in Auschwitz 2. AND THE REASON TO DO IT TODAY RATHER THAN ANY OTHER DAY is that the 1940 Berliner Adressbuch had just yielded ELEVEN LEIBHOLZ HOUSEHOLDERS, so for the first time the two lists can be laid beside each other. AT LEAST FOUR OF THE ELEVEN ARE IN THE DATABASE: Samuel Israel (identified, by matching street and house number), Wilhelm born 28.12.1890 (murdered, deported from Berlin, Theresienstadt), Albert born 1886 of Berlin, and Heinrich born 1890 of Berlin. THE DATABASE'S OWN PROFESSION FACET AGREES WITH THE DIRECTORY: it lists a BUTCHER, and the directory has two Leibholz Fleischermeister. A city directory and a register of the murdered, describing the same handful of tradespeople. *** AND A NEW LEAD ON THE GEORG QUESTION. *** HANS ISRAEL LEIBHOLZ, BORN 1912 AT PREUSSISCH FRIEDLAND, murdered at Auschwitz. Preussisch Friedland is in KREIS SCHLOCHAU — the same district as HAMMERSTEIN, where Georg was born, and nowhere near Schubin, where Jacob, Samuel and Oskar were born. This does not make Georg a brother. IT MAKES HIM A FAMILY: a second, West Prussian Leibholz line, of which Hans is the first member found besides Georg and Lydia, and of which Irmgard Shtern — who called herself Georg's niece — is a survivor. THE BOUND, STATED FIRST RATHER THAN LAST: three of the four Berlin matches are NAME AND CITY ONLY. Berlin held four million people, this archive has twice published a person built out of two, and a name in two lists is a correspondence until an address or a date of birth joins them. Only Samuel has that. In data/yadvashem-leibholz.tsv. *** TWO MORE OPENED 20 SEPTEMBER, CHOSEN RATHER THAN TAKEN IN ORDER. *** The eighteen Pages of Testimony were filtered and the two picked were the ones the Berlin directory work had already identified a household for. WILLI LEIBHOLZ, item 1067433: 'He was a BUTCHER. Prior to WWII he lived in Berlin.' Born 1893, married, spouse ERNA, PLACE OF DEATH AUSCHWITZ 1943. ERNA LEIBHOLZ, item 1070804: born Berlin, permanent residence NEUKÖLLN, spouse WILLY, place of death AUSCHWITZ. *** AND THE SAME PERSON WROTE BOTH: EVA KHAVA [P.] HAMMER OLSHER, NIECE. *** She is a HAMMER, and Mapping the Lives gives Erna as ERNA NÉE HAMMER — so the survivor who recorded this household came through the wife's family, not the husband's. WHAT IT CLOSES: the Berliner Adressbuch has 'Wilhelm, FLEISCHERMEISTER, Neukölln, LENAUSTRASSE 25' in 1940, 1941 and 1942 and nothing in 1943. Yad Vashem gives the trade, the city, the wife and Auschwitz in 1943. FOUR INDEPENDENT SOURCES NOW DESCRIBE ONE MAN AND THEY AGREE — a directory, the 1939 census database, the name records and a form written from memory by a woman who survived. AND THERE ARE PHOTOGRAPHS: his record lists four documents, two of them of type PHOTOS. ONE INCONSISTENCY KEPT RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: the Page gives his age as 45 against a birth of 1893 and a death in 1943, which does not add up; Pages of Testimony are written from memory and their age fields are the weakest thing on the form. AND THE BOUND: NONE OF THIS CONNECTS WILLI TO KURT'S FAMILY. Jacob, Samuel and Oskar were born at Schubin; nothing here says where Willi was born beyond 'Germany'. FOURTEEN OF THE EIGHTEEN PAGES REMAIN UNOPENED, including one for HEINZ LEIBHOLZ born 1922, who is the son at the same address. *** WORKED AGAIN, LATER ON 20 SEPTEMBER, BY SUBMITTER RATHER THAN BY VICTIM — AND THIS ROW'S CENTRAL ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN. *** The row said: Irmgard Shtern called herself GEORG'S NIECE, so her parent was Georg's sibling, so her other Pages would give GEORG'S PARENTS. She filed SEVENTEEN Pages and three of them settle it. LIDIA LAIBHOLZ b.1884 — father ELIUS, mother MINA. KLARA LEWINZON b.1906 — father YULIUS, mother MINA. EMA MENDELZON b.1892 — father YULIUS, mother MEINE. Elius and Yulius are one name through the Hebrew; so are Mina and Meine. THREE SISTERS, and Irmgard is niece to all three. *** SO GEORG IS THE UNCLE BY MARRIAGE — IRMGARD'S BLOOD IS LYDIA'S FAMILY, NOT THE LEIBHOLZES'. *** Her Pages cannot give Georg's parents and never could, and Georg's own Page (item 1684365) has no father and no mother on it and gives his birthplace as the single word "Germany". The open question is exactly where it was. WHAT THE SEVENTEEN DID GIVE. (a) LYDIA'S PARENTS AND SISTERS — a wife who was a name and a maiden name is now a daughter of Julius and Mina with at least two sisters. (b) GIDEON SHTRUZIK, BORN 1940, marital status "child", of Berlin, MURDERED, father HARRY — almost certainly Elli's son and Georg's grandson, although HIS MOTHER IS NOT NAMED ON THE PAGE. A child this archive did not have. *** AND THE OTHER SUBMITTER SEARCH FOUND A SURVIVOR. *** SUBMITTER LAST NAME = LEIBHOLZ returns three records, all filed by SOPHIE LEIBHOLZ through RELICO, the World Jewish Congress Relief Committee in Geneva, on questionnaires "COMPLETED BY SURVIVORS IN SHANGHAI, 1946". She was looking for her brother SALLY BINDER (b.14.01.1884, tailor, Motzstrasse 13, Neukölln — deported to Auschwitz 1 March 1943 and murdered), his wife MATHILDE, and her brother-in-law HEINRICH LEIBHOLZ (b.16.10.1890 Berlin, tax agent, Hornstrasse 19, wife AGNES) — THE CONTROL CASE, who survived and died in 1948, and whom she did not know was alive. A SECOND SOPHIE LEIBHOLZ, NÉE ROTHENBERG, BORN AT SCHLOCHAU 09.01.1887, was murdered at Auschwitz on the same 1 March 1943 transport and is a different woman; the two are kept apart deliberately. SCHLOCHAU IS THE DISTRICT THAT CONTAINS HAMMERSTEIN, where Sally Leibholz — Kurt's grandfather — was born. In data/yadvashem-leibholz.tsv. STILL OPEN AND NOW A ROW OF ITS OWN: the Relico Shanghai questionnaires as a collection, and Sophie's husband's forename, which is on none of the three forms.

rows.what: THE GREAT-GRANDPARENTS ARE DOCUMENTED — Sali Leibholz and Fridericke Schmul, on an Auschwitz death register
rows.note: FOUND 17 SEPTEMBER, and it is the oldest unsourced claim on the front page of this site finally getting a source. The chart has said 'SALLY LEIBHOLZ & FRIEDERIKE SCHMUL, Hammerstein; married at Szubin, 1874' since day one, ON THE FAMILY TREE'S WORD AND NOTHING ELSE. YAD VASHEM RECORD 5415605, SAMUEL ISRAEL LEIBHOLZ: born 28/06/1877 at SCHUBIN; FATHER'S FIRST NAME **SALI**; MOTHER'S FIRST NAME **FRIDERICKE**; MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME **SCHMUL**; married to **FRIEDA**, which this archive did not know he had; died at AUSCHWITZ on 10/04/1943; CONTENT NOTE 'DOCUMENT NUMBER 18258/1943'; source THE AUSCHWITZ DEATH REGISTERS held by the State Museum Auschwitz-Birkenau. SO THE GREAT-GRANDPARENTS ARE NAMED ON A GERMAN DEATH REGISTER KEPT AT AUSCHWITZ, AGAINST A NUMBERED ENTRY, FOR A MAN BORN AT SCHUBIN IN 1877. The spellings are SALI and FRIDERICKE — what the clerk wrote. It is the first primary source this archive has ever held for that generation. AND A TEST WAS BUILT OUT OF IT AND RUN: Yad Vashem can be searched on MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME. SCHMUL returns people from Berlin to Łódź to Komarów — it is a common name — AND EXACTLY ONE LEIBHOLZ, Samuel. NO BROTHER OF JACOB AND SAMUEL IS RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THAT DATABASE WITH THOSE PARENTS, AND THAT IS A LIMIT OF THE RECORDS RATHER THAN OF THE FAMILY: Jacob's and Oskar's entries come from DEPORTATION LISTS, which have no parents' fields at all. Only a Page of Testimony or a death register carries parents, and of the four brothers only Samuel has one. WHICH ALSO SETTLES THE SHAPE OF THE GEORG QUESTION: he will never be excluded or included by a parents' field in Yad Vashem, because his surviving records do not have one either. IRMGARD SHTERN, HIS NIECE, REMAINS THE ROUTE.

rows.what: Frances's own four marriages - Hostowsky, Berner, Sefton, Luwinski, Eisenhardt
rows.note: NEW 17 SEPTEMBER, and it began as a mistake worth keeping. The FamilySearch index gives Kurt's third wife as FRANCES HOSTOWSKY, BERNER, SEFTON, LUWINSKI, and her 1958 remarriage to Rolf Eisenhardt was written up here as a discovery before Kurt's own page was checked - WHERE IT HAS BEEN PUBLISHED FOR DAYS. So the row is not what it started as. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WORTH DOING: Frances is the only person in this story whose whole adult life is legible in one line of an index - born Hostowsky at Vienna, married Berner, married Sefton, married Kurt on 29 February 1956, married Eisenhardt on 23 May 1958 - AND THE ARCHIVE HAS NEVER LOOKED FOR THE FIRST TWO. Berner and Sefton are two marriages and probably a widowhood, all in South Africa, all in the civil marriage index that has now been mapped. One search each. SHE IS NOT BLOOD AND THE ARCHIVE SHOULD SAY SO PLAINLY: this is about establishing whether the 1956 register's 'widow' is true, because that is the field Kurt's page leans on. || BLOCKED AGAIN 20 SEPTEMBER: THE FAMILYSEARCH SESSION HAS SIGNED OUT for the second time in four days. The search page now says 'Create a free account or sign in to see all available results' and the persona API returns 0 results for a query that returned 111 on 17 September — a zero that means signed out, not absent, which is exactly the kind of false negative this archive keeps catching. I do not sign anybody in. One sign-in in the browser unblocks this row and row 174 together. *** RUN 20 SEPTEMBER, the sign-in restored. *** BERNER AND SEFTON ARE NOT IN THE SOUTH AFRICAN MARRIAGE INDEX. Frances's two marriages before Kurt do not appear under either surname, which fits the 1956 register giving her birthplace as VIENNA — she probably married them in Europe, not here. WHAT DID COME OUT: the Western Cape Archives Records version of her 1958 marriage to Rolf Eisenhardt GIVES A PLACE THE CIVIL MARRIAGE INDEX DOES NOT — WYNBERG, CAPE PROVINCE. So after Kurt she left Johannesburg for the Cape. Her age is given as 43 in both versions. The row closes: her whole traceable South African life is three entries, and the two earlier husbands are a European problem.

rows.what: The WLD number for Kurt versus Frances, 1957
rows.owner: the National Archives of South Africa — NAAIRS is down
rows.note: NEW 17 SEPTEMBER. Kurt's page carries '1957 - files for divorce again, Kurt Luwinski versus Frances, formerly Sefton, formerly Berner, born Hostowsky' AND data/litigation.tsv HAS NO REFERENCE FOR IT. Eight court files are tabulated there and that action is not one of them. It must exist: Frances married Rolf Eisenhardt on 23 May 1958 and Kurt did not die until 1968, so the marriage was ended by a court and not by a death. FIND THE NUMBER. It is a Witwatersrand Local Division file of 1957 or 1958, in the same series as WLD 1950/1948, WLD 497/1951, WLD 2368/1951 and WLD 2542/1957. NAAIRS, when it is back, under LUWINSKI, LUWINSKY and LUWENSKI - the last of which hid WLD 2545/1950 for weeks. AND NOTE THE NEIGHBOUR ALREADY IN THE TABLE: WLD 2542/1957, Standard Bank versus K. Luwinski, sits in the same window. Whatever 1957 was for him, it was happening in more than one court. || BLOCKED 20 SEPTEMBER: NAAIRS has stopped answering altogether — not 503 as on 17 September but no response at all, portal and search service alike, four days running. See row 179. This row cannot move until it comes back, and marking it 'next' overstated what this archive can do.

rows.what: The Transvaal estate-file DEATH NOTICES - re-check whenever FamilySearch publishes more
rows.owner: FamilySearch — until it publishes more of the set
rows.note: NEW 17 SEPTEMBER, and it is the best future prospect this archive has for the question it exists to answer. "South Africa, Transvaal, Estate Files, 1950-1993", collection 2144007, is in its own words IMAGES OF COPIES OF DEATH NOTICES from probate estate files at the National Archives in Pretoria. A South African death notice NAMES THE DECEASED'S PARENTS, and the title spans Kurt in 1968, Henry Robert in 1969, both of Leonard's candidate years, and Martha Maud in 1986. ITS WAYPOINTS - read from /service/cds/recapi/collections/2144007/waypoints - SAY IT IS PUBLISHED FOR 1955 TO 1960 ONLY. Seven of them. The collection page says "This collection is being published as images become available". THE CONTROL SAYS THE REST EXISTS: the Orange Free State equivalent, collection 1407787, has fifty-seven waypoints running 1951 to 2006 and 3.9 million images. So the Transvaal gap is a publishing schedule and not a destroyed record. CHECK THE WAYPOINT COUNT PERIODICALLY. It is one HTTP request and the answer is a number.

rows.what: THE HAT TRADE, BERLIN TO ELOFF STREET
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER out of the Berlin directory, and it is the first thing that connects Kurt's working life to his mother's family rather than to Johannesburg. SAMUEL LEIBHOLZ IS LISTED IN THE BERLINER ADRESSBUCH AS "HÜTE EN GROS" - HATS, WHOLESALE - in the householder-and-firms section from 1929 to 1938, at SW19 and then SW68. KURT LUWINSKI RAN THE PICCADILLY HAT AT 81 ELOFF STREET, JOHANNESBURG, FROM 1941 TO 1952, and gave his occupation as dress designer in 1933 and again in 1956. AUGUSTE 'LIZZY' LUWINSKI WAS A DRESSMAKER AND MILLINER. And the other Leibholz firms are Konfektion and Trikotagen - ready-made clothing and knitwear. THE WHOLE FAMILY IS IN THE RAG TRADE, ON BOTH SIDES OF THE EQUATOR. WHAT THIS IS NOT, YET: proof that Samuel the hat wholesaler is Samuel Israel Leibholz of the Auschwitz death register, document 18258/1943, whose father was Sali and mother Friderike née Schmul. It is the same uncommon surname in the same city in the same decade, which is a candidate and not a finding - the Bloom mariner rule. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the Adressbuch gives the firm's street and number, and Samuel Israel Leibholz's address is recoverable from the 1939 census the way Jacob's was. TWO ADDRESSES, ONE COMPARISON. *** CLOSED THE SAME DAY IT WAS OPENED, AND IT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A CANDIDATE. *** The row asked for two addresses and one comparison. THE ADDRESSES MATCH. The Berliner Adressbuch gives SAMUEL LEIBHOLZ, HÜTE EN GROS, at JERUSALEMER STRASSE 5/6 in 1933 and at KOMMANDANTENSTRASSE 29 from 1936 onward. The Bundesarchiv Gedenkbuch gives SAMUEL LEIBHOLZ, born Schubin 28.06.1877, residence Berlin (KREUZBERG), and this archive's own Leibholz page has carried the street for days: KOMMANDANTENSTR. 29, KREUZBERG. SAME STREET, SAME NUMBER. The wholesale hatter is Samuel Israel Leibholz of the Auschwitz death register. *** AND THE 1940 VOLUME LISTS HIM UNDER THE NAME THE LAW GAVE HIM. *** Not 'Samuel Leibholz' but '—Israel Hüte SW68 Kommandantenstr 29'. THE 1938 DECREE, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY SHOWS AS A DOCUMENT ON KURT'S PAGE, OPERATING IN A TELEPHONE BOOK: the forename gone and the imposed one in its place. A second man on the same page is listed as 'A. Israel'. *** AND KURT LIVED AT THE SHOP. *** The atlas gives four Berlin addresses for Kurt and one of them is Kommandantenstr. 29. A SECOND of the four is Waghäuseler Str. 9/10 — which the 1936 and 1937 directories give as the address of OSKAR LEIBHOLZ, Kaufmann, Wilmersdorf, matching the Gedenkbuch's Wilmersdorf for Oskar. TWO OF KURT'S FOUR BERLIN ADDRESSES ARE LEIBHOLZ BUSINESS ADDRESSES. He grew up in the family's trade and took it to Eloff Street. ONE THING WITHDRAWN: the reading that Samuel 'moved postal district between 1936 and 1938' is an artefact — SW19 was renumbered SW68 and the street never changed. *** AND THEN PART OF IT WAS WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY. *** The sentence 'AND KURT LIVED AT THE SHOP', and the claim that two of Kurt's four Berlin addresses are Leibholz business addresses, ARE CIRCULAR AND ARE WITHDRAWN.
