Those four addresses are not Kurt's — they are the four Leibholz households in the CENSUS OF 17 MAY 1939, carried on the atlas under a loosely worded pin. Saying the directory agrees with them is saying the same thing twice, and it went into a commit message before it was checked. WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS STILL THE ANSWER THIS ROW WANTED: the identification of Samuel is sound, because the NEW fact is not the address but the TRADE — the Gedenkbuch gives a man at Kommandantenstr. 29 and the directory gives a WHOLESALE HAT BUSINESS there. And the directory does the same for the other three: JACOB traded as JAQUES and the firm 'Jaques Leibholz & Co, KONFEKTION' printed directly beneath him is his; OSKAR was a Kaufmann; GEORG RAN A LAUNDRY at Michaelkirchstraße 26. Four men who had four addresses and no occupations now have occupations. THE HAT THREAD TO JOHANNESBURG IS STILL REAL AND IS NOW PROPERLY STATED: Kurt's mother was a dressmaker and milliner, her husband's family firm was ready-made clothing, his brother sold hats wholesale, and Kurt opened a hat shop in Eloff Street. THAT IS A FAMILY TRADE, NOT A SHARED DOORWAY.

rows.what: AUGUSTE UNDER HER OTHER TWO SURNAMES — Luwinski before 1924, Fricke after the war
rows.note: THE REMAINING HALF OF ITEM 8, carved off so it stops hiding inside a closed row. The Berlin directory has now been read properly under LEIBHOLZ and Auguste appears in exactly one volume, 1940, as a widow at Badensche Straße 9. SHE HAS NEVER BEEN LOOKED FOR UNDER HER OTHER NAMES. Before her marriage to Jacob she was AUGUSTE LUWINSKI — and the Luwinski surname reaches the Berlin householder section in only one year of the whole run, 1933, so that search is small and quick. After the war she was AUGUSTE FRICKE and she lived until 22 June 1975, which is inside the digitised run: the ZLB has the volumes to 1970. A post-war Berlin address for Kurt's mother would be the first record of her own later life this archive has ever had, and the volumes are free. ALSO WORTH ONE QUERY: whether the 1940 widow is her at all. Jacob was not deported until 26 February 1943 and the archive will not join a 1940 widow to a man alive in 1943 without something more. *** WORKED THE SAME DAY, AND HALF OF IT IS ANSWERED. *** FIRST, A CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN PREMISE: the digitised run under the collection this archive had been querying STOPS AT 1943, and 1944 to 1954 return nothing. The claim that ZLB has 1799 to 1970 in one series is wrong. BUT THE POST-WAR BOOKS ARE THERE UNDER OTHER IDENTIFIERS — 34117222 for the Namenteil volumes of 1955 to 1970, 15849358 for the telephone books to 1980 — AND THEY ARE SET IN ANTIQUA, so the text layer reads them perfectly and no page images are needed. *** FRICKE: ONE CANDIDATE. *** 1957 Namenteil page 518: 'Fricke Auguste Rentn Chlb 1 Kais-Friedr-Str 79' — AUGUSTE FRICKE, A PENSIONER, CHARLOTTENBURG, KAISER-FRIEDRICH-STRASSE 79. Lizzy was born 28 August 1893 and died 22 June 1975, so in 1957 she was sixty-four and 'Rentnerin' is exactly right. She is the only Auguste Fricke in the Berlin name sections of 1955 to 1980. IT IS A CANDIDATE AND NOT A FINDING: Fricke is a common North German surname and Auguste a common forename for that generation, and one name in one directory is how this archive got the Bloom mariner wrong. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT is her death registration of 22 June 1975, which would carry an address to compare. *** AND THE POST-WAR LUWINSKIS, WHICH THE ROW DID NOT ASK FOR AND WHICH MATTER MORE. *** MANFRED LUWINSKI, Schlosser, Tegel, Egellsstraße 16, in 1957, 1959 and 1961 — the register holds Manfred Joachim Luwinski, born 14 November 1933. JOACHIM LUWINSKI, Ofensetzer, Berlin 65, Ramlerstraße, in 1967 — the register holds Joachim Luwinski, born 30 November 1940. AND KURT LUWINSKI, POSTFACHARBEITER, BERLIN 21 (MOABIT), STEPHANSTRASSE, in 1964, with a telephone in the 1970-71 book. *** THAT LAST ONE SOLVES A STANDING BUILD PROBLEM. *** Every check-evidence run reports that 'KURT LUWINSKI' matches two register entries and is therefore left unlinked — Kurt Israel of Johannesburg who died in 1968, and a Kurt who died in 1995. THE SECOND KURT IS NOW PLACED: Berlin, the post office, Moabit, a telephone in 1970. The two are separated by city, trade and decade instead of by a death date alone. STILL UNDONE: Auguste under LUWINSKI before 1924. The surname reaches the householder section in only two pre-war years, 1909 and 1933, and the 1909 page has not been opened — it would be her father's generation. *** THE LUWINSKI HALF IS NOW CLOSED, AND FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON RATHER THAN A SEARCH. *** Auguste married Jacob in 1924, so before that she was AUGUSTE LUWINSKI — but she was born in 1893 and UNMARRIED WOMEN ARE NOT HOUSEHOLDERS. The Berliner Adressbuch's Teil I lists heads of household and registered firms; a woman in her twenties living at home or in service does not appear in it. AND THE SURNAME CONFIRMS IT: across 1900 to 1943 LUWINSKI reaches the householder section IN ONE YEAR ONLY, 1933, with Alfred the presser and Oskar the master tailor. There is no Luwinski household in Berlin for her to be part of before 1924. The apparent 1909 exception was opened and is a mirage — the page runs LÖWENTHAL to LÖWISOHN and the search fuzzes LU to LO. SO THERE IS NOTHING TO FIND HERE AND THE ROW SHOULD STOP IMPLYING THERE IS. *** THE FRICKE HALF STANDS AS ONE CANDIDATE: *** Auguste Fricke, Rentnerin, Charlottenburg 1, Kaiser-Friedrich-Straße 79, in the 1957 Namenteil — the only Auguste Fricke in the Berlin name sections of 1955 to 1980, and the right age. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT is her death registration of 22 June 1975, which would carry an address to compare with Kaiser-Friedrich-Straße 79. That is a German civil record and it is David's to order. *** THE FRICKE HALF SWEPT PROPERLY, 20 SEPTEMBER, WITH THE SOLR API FOUND IN THE TEIL IV WORK. *** A phrase search for "Fricke Auguste" across ALL FORTY POST-WAR VOLUMES — 27 Namenteil 1949-1970 and 13 telephone books 1969-1980 — returns THREE PAGES, AND THEY ARE TWO WOMEN. 1957 Namenteil p.518: "FRICKE AUGUSTE RENTN CHLB 1 KAIS-FRIEDR-STR 79", the candidate this row already had. 1963 street section p.850 and 1970 p.287: "FRICKE AUGUSTE PUTZFRAU" and "FRICKE AUGUSTE" — THE SAME BUILDING BOTH YEARS, among Fröhlich, Kaldenbach, Luckow and Stinka. A WORKING CLEANER IN 1963 IS NOT THE SEVENTY-YEAR-OLD PENSIONER OF 1957. Two different women, and the Charlottenburg pensioner appears in NO OTHER VOLUME OF THE RUN AND IN NO TELEPHONE BOOK. Four Fricke blocks were also opened directly — 1952, 1954, 1963, 1970 — and none holds an Auguste under her own name or on the dash. *** WHAT THE SHAPE MEANS IF THE 1957 WOMAN IS LIZZY: she was in Berlin in 1957 and gone by 1959 — AND SHE WAS STILL IN BERLIN TWO YEARS AFTER HER MOTHER DIED AT ZEUTERN ON 30 OCTOBER 1955. *** She did not go to Baden to nurse her mother; she went afterwards, and died at Kraichtal, the same town, in 1975. THE IDENTIFICATION IS STILL UNPROVED AND NOTHING HERE CHANGES THAT — one line, no age, no birth date, no maiden name. What the sweep buys is the difference between "there is a candidate in 1957" and "there is a candidate in 1957 AND IN NO OTHER YEAR". BOUND STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the dash convention means a phrase search cannot find a dashed "—Auguste", and twenty-three volumes were not opened by hand. The row stays blocked on her 1975 Kraichtal death registration. In data/berlin-postwar-luwinski.tsv.

rows.what: THE 1909 LUWINSKI HOUSEHOLDER — Lizzy's father's generation, one page image away
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER, and it is one page. Sweeping the Berliner Adressbuch householder section for LUWINSKI across 1900 to 1943 returns the name in EXACTLY TWO YEARS: 1909, on page 1662 of 'I. Einwohner Berlins und seiner Vororte', and 1933, on page 1671, which is Alfred the presser at Putbusser Straße 24. THE 1909 PAGE HAS NOT BEEN OPENED. Auguste 'Lizzy' Luwinski was born on 28 August 1893, so in 1909 she was sixteen and cannot be the householder — WHOEVER IS ON THAT PAGE IS OF HER PARENTS' GENERATION, and this archive has never had a name for them. Luwinski is rare enough in Berlin that a single householder in 1909 is worth the four minutes: the page image is at digital.zlb.de/viewer/api/v1/records/34115495_1909/files/images/00001662.png and the Fraktur reads cleanly at three to four times. ONE HONEST CAUTION BEFORE ANYBODY GETS EXCITED: a Luwinski in Berlin in 1909 is not automatically her father. The family was East Prussian and the name appears in Posen and West Prussia too. *** STRUCK WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE PAGE WAS OPENED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN ABOUT HIM. *** THERE IS NO LUWINSKI ON PAGE 1662 OF THE 1909 VOLUME. The page runs 'LÖWENTHAL — 1639 — LÖWISOHN' and is full of a completely different set of families: Semu LOWINSKI of Barnimstraße 50, Dr Julius LOWINSKIS of Brunnenstraße 196, WILLY LOWINSKY Ingenieur G.m.b.H., R. LOWINSKY Nachfolger Dampf-Waschanstalt, and a page of Löwenthals and Löwisohns. THE ZLB SEARCH FUZZES LU- TO LO- AND Ö-, and this archive had written a whole work-list row about Lizzy's father's generation before looking. IT TOOK FOUR MINUTES TO CHECK AND IT WOULD HAVE TAKEN A DAY TO UNPICK. *** WHAT OPENING IT DID PRODUCE, because the same doubt then had to be turned on the finding that IS published: *** the 1933 entry was re-verified on its own page image, and page 1671 runs LUTZ to LUX, which is the right alphabetical place, and the line reads 'Luwinski Alfred Bügler N31 Putbusser Str 24'. IT HOLDS. AND THERE IS A SECOND LUWINSKI ON THAT LINE'S DASH WHICH THE TEXT LAYER HAD HIDDEN: '—Oskar Schneidermstr W35 Steglitzer Str 7' — OSKAR LUWINSKI, A MASTER TAILOR. See the new row.

rows.what: OSKAR LUWINSKI, MASTER TAILOR, STEGLITZER STRASSE 7 — a name this archive did not have
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER, found by re-verifying a published finding rather than by looking for him. The 1933 Berliner Adressbuch householder page carries TWO Luwinskis, not one: ALFRED, Bügler (a garment presser), N31 Putbusser Straße 24 — already published — and immediately beneath him on the dash, 'OSKAR SCHNEIDERMSTR W35 STEGLITZER STR 7'. OSKAR LUWINSKI, A SCHNEIDERMEISTER — A MASTER TAILOR — with his own business in Schöneberg. HE WAS LOST TO THE DASH CONVENTION, the same fault that hid four Leibholz households this morning: the text layer spells the surname only on the first line of a run. Twice in one day. WHY HE MATTERS. Luwinski reaches the Berlin householder section in ONE YEAR of the whole 1900-1943 run, so there were two Luwinski households in the city and BOTH WERE IN THE GARMENT TRADE — a presser and a master tailor. AUGUSTE 'LIZZY' LUWINSKI WAS A DRESSMAKER AND MILLINER, and her son opened a hat shop in Johannesburg. WHAT TO DO WITH HIM: he is not in this archive's register under any spelling. Look for Oskar Luwinski in the 1939 census via Mapping the Lives, in Arolsen, and in the post-war volumes beside Manfred, Joachim and Kurt. AND STATE THE OBVIOUS CAUTION: a rare surname and a shared trade is a reason to look, not a relationship. *** THE FIRST THING THIS ROW ASKED FOR WAS DONE THE SAME HOUR, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. *** Mapping the Lives — the memorial database built on the 1939 census supplementary card, which is where this archive's four Leibholz addresses came from — returns TWO PEOPLE for the surname LUWINSKI IN ITS ENTIRE HOLDING. One is Auguste née Luwinski at Meraner Straße 2, who is Lizzy. THE OTHER IS NEW AND IS NOT OSKAR. *** ANTON LUWINSKI, BORN 16 OCTOBER 1919, AT SCHINDEKOPSTRASSE 7, LEHRWERKSTATT OSTPREUSSISCHES BAUGEWERBE, KÖNIGSBERG (PR.) *** — a twenty-year-old at the East Prussian building trade's TRAINING WORKSHOP in Königsberg. THIS ARCHIVE HAS AN EAST PRUSSIA PAGE AND HAS NEVER HAD A TWENTIETH-CENTURY LUWINSKI IN EAST PRUSSIA. Note also that Arolsen holds an ALFRED LUWINSKI BORN 09.09.1917 — two young Luwinski men born two years apart, both in persecution databases. SO: OSKAR LUWINSKI THE MASTER TAILOR IS NOT IN THE DATABASE, AND NEITHER IS ALFRED THE PRESSER. For a database built on the census card that recorded Jewish descent, that absence is itself informative and this archive will put it no more strongly than that. WHAT IS LEFT OF THIS ROW: Oskar in Arolsen, and Oskar in the post-war volumes. *** AROLSEN CHECKED 20 SEPTEMBER, AND OSKAR IS NOT IN IT. *** Nine records under LUWINSKI in the whole Arolsen index and he is not one of them. Nor is he in Mapping the Lives. So the Schneidermeister of Steglitzer Straße 7 appears in ONE SOURCE — a single line in the 1933 Berliner Adressbuch — and in no record of Nazi persecution at all. THAT IS CONSISTENT WITH A MAN WHO WAS NOT PERSECUTED, and it is one absence in two archives, which is not proof of anything. WHAT IS LEFT AND CANNOT BE DONE FROM HERE: the post-war Berlin volumes have been read and hold Manfred, Joachim and Kurt but no Oskar; the 1939 census would have a card for him and Mapping the Lives does not index it, which means the card either does not survive or was never flagged. The row is parked rather than closed, because a second directory year would cost four minutes if anyone wants it. *** AND THE POST-WAR HALF OF THIS ROW IS NOW DONE TOO, THOUGH NOT FOR OSKAR. *** The whole post-war Berlin run was searched by surname for the first time. LUWINSKI RETURNS TEN PAGES IN EIGHT VOLUMES and THREE MEN, all three already in the tree and all three dead: MANFRED, Schlosser then MODELLSCHLOSSER, Tegel, EGELLSSTRASSE 16, in 1957, 1959, 1961, 1963, 1964, 1967 and 1970 — and MODELLSCHLOSSER IS MODEL FITTER, the exact trade on the 1965 ICEM emigration roll, which also names a MARQUARDT, and the tree holds Helga Erna Marquardt née Luwinski. Three sources, one man. JOACHIM, OFENSETZER — a stove-fitter — at RAMLERSTRASSE 15, Wedding, in 1967 and 1970: a trade and an address the tree does not have for him at all. KURT, Postfacharbeiter at Stephanstraße 7 in 1964 and Peter-Vischer-Straße 25 in 1967, and in the 1970-71 TELEPHONE BOOK as "LUWINSKI KURT 4 12 25 12 · BEAMTER · 52 WALDSTR. 60". *** NOT DERRICK'S FATHER, who died in Johannesburg in 1968 — this is the tree's other Kurt, Leo's son, recorded as dying in 1995 with no birth date, place or trade. A correspondence and not an identification. *** *** OSKAR LUWINSKI, THE MASTER TAILOR OF 1933, IS IN NONE OF THE FORTY POST-WAR VOLUMES. *** He does not reappear after the war under Luwinski, and LUWINSKY returns nothing in the run at all. The row stays parked on one source for him, and the sweep that would have unparked it has now been run and come back empty.

rows.what: ANTON LUWINSKI, KÖNIGSBERG, BORN 16 OCTOBER 1919 — the first twentieth-century Luwinski in East Prussia
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER, out of a search that was looking for somebody else. Mapping the Lives holds exactly two Luwinskis: Lizzy, and ANTON LUWINSKI, BORN 16 OCTOBER 1919, recorded at SCHINDEKOPSTRASSE 7, LEHRWERKSTATT OSTPREUSSISCHES BAUGEWERBE, KÖNIGSBERG — the training workshop of the East Prussian building trade. WHY IT MATTERS: the Luwinskis are an East Prussian family and this archive's East Prussia page is built on nineteenth-century parish entries from Ermland and Masuria. ANTON IS THE FIRST TWENTIETH-CENTURY LUWINSKI THE ARCHIVE HAS FOUND IN EAST PRUSSIA, and he is in a persecution database, at an address that is an institution rather than a home. WHAT TO DO: read his full record for the source it came from and for any parents; check Arolsen for him; and set him beside ALFRED LUWINSKI BORN 09.09.1917, whom Arolsen holds — two young men born two years apart. THE CAUTION: Luwinski is rare but not unique, Königsberg is four hundred miles from Berlin, and NOTHING HERE CONNECTS HIM TO LIZZY except a surname and a province. That is a reason to look, not a relationship. *** RECORD OPENED THE SAME HOUR, AND IT CORRECTS THIS ROW'S OWN PREMISE. *** ANTON LUWINSKI was born at DEUTHEN, KREIS ALLENSTEIN — in the ERMLAND, the Catholic corner of East Prussia, and about twenty miles from SAUERBAUM, KREIS RÖSSEL, WHERE LIZZY WAS BORN. His card reads "Race": NNNN and "Basis of persecution: UNKNOWN". SO HE WAS NOT PERSECUTED, and this row's sentence calling Mapping the Lives "a persecution database" and drawing an inference from his being in it IS WRONG: the database indexes surviving 1939 census supplementary cards, and presence in it is not evidence of anything except that a card survives. WHAT IS LEFT, AND IT IS BETTER THAN WHAT WAS CLAIMED: two Luwinskis from two Ermland villages twenty miles apart, one of them Kurt's mother. Still a reason to look and still not a relationship. *** AROLSEN CHECKED 20 SEPTEMBER, AND ANTON IS NOT IN IT EITHER. *** Which adds nothing, and the reason it adds nothing is worth writing down: his own 1939 card already reads "Race: NNNN" and "Basis of persecution: unknown", so a persecution archive SHOULD NOT hold him, and it does not. The two sources agree and neither takes him further. WHAT HE STILL IS: a Luwinski born at DEUTHEN, KREIS ALLENSTEIN, twenty miles from Lizzy's Sauerbaum, both in the Ermland — the first twentieth-century Luwinski this archive has placed in East Prussia. WHAT WOULD TAKE HIM FURTHER is the same thing that would take Lizzy further: the Kreis Allenstein and Kreis Rössel parish registers, which are the undigitised films of the Groß Bössau row. HE IS NOW PART OF THAT ROW'S CASE RATHER THAN A SEPARATE LEAD.

rows.what: LIZZY'S OWN 1939 CENSUS CARD — Sauerbaum, NNNN, and a mixed marriage
rows.note: OPENED 20 SEPTEMBER, and it is the single most informative document this archive has found about Kurt's mother. Mapping the Lives, from the Reichssippenamt census card of 17 May 1939, Bundesarchiv R 1509. *** (1) HER BIRTHPLACE. *** AUGUSTE LEIBHOLZ née LUWINSKI, born 28.08.1893 IN SAUERBAUM / RÖSSEL / OSTPREUSSEN — and this archive already knew that village, because JOHANNA THIMM OF SAUERBAUM is Kurt's great-grandmother and was used as the non-Jewish East Prussian CONTROL when counting Berlin directory pages. Lizzy was born where her grandmother came from. *** (2) "RACE": NNNN. *** The card recorded the ancestry of all four grandparents; N is nicht-jüdisch. FOUR N's. THE GERMAN STATE CLASSIFIED LIZZY AS NOT JEWISH, ON ITS OWN FORM, IN 1939. *** (3) "BASIS OF PERSECUTION: COLLECTIVE". *** The term for someone persecuted as part of a household rather than for their own recorded ancestry — A MISCHEHE. It is the standard reason Jacob was not taken until 26 February 1943, the Fabrikaktion. The category is on the record; the inference is not asserted. *** (4) AND IT GIVES JACOB A PLACE OF DEATH. *** The record's family block reads 'Leibholz, Jacob [Jakob], * 08.08.1884 in Szubin (Schubin), † before 08.05.1945 IN AUSCHWITZ'. The Bundesarchiv Gedenkbuch entry this archive holds says 'not documented' for both death date and death place. THE PLACE IS NOW NAMED. The date is not. *** AND THE QUESTION IT SHARPENS. *** Kurt was born in 1912, Lizzy married Jacob in 1924, so Kurt is her son by another man and Jacob was his stepfather. IF LIZZY WAS NNNN THEN KURT'S CLASSIFICATION AS A JEW — he carried the imposed name ISRAEL out of Germany in 1933 — CANNOT HAVE COME FROM HER. It came from the father whose surname he does not carry, and this archive has no name for that man. In data/mappingthelives-leibholz.tsv.

rows.what: GROSS BÖSSAU, KREIS RÖSSEL — Lizzy's parish register, and the two films that are not online
rows.owner: a Family History Centre, or the Olsztyn archives
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER and it is the most precisely defined open task this archive has. The 1939 census card gives Lizzy's birthplace as SAUERBAUM, KREIS RÖSSEL, OSTPREUSSEN. The FamilySearch catalogue names the parish in its own words, record koha:15497: 'Parish register of baptisms and deaths for GROSS BÖSSAU, Ostpreußen, now BIESOWO, Olsztyn, Poland. Also includes Kunzkeim, SAUERBAUM, Willims, and Kleisak (Kreis Rössel).' The series runs 1690 to 1897 on NINE FILMS. *** EIGHT OF THE NINE ARE NOT DIGITISED. *** The two that matter both return 'Film number not found' in the viewer while signed in: FILM 7948905, TAUFEN 1793-1890, which would hold JOACHIM LUWINSKI'S 1865 BAPTISM AND NAME HIS PARENTS — a generation this archive does not have; and FILM 7769256, GEBURTEN (KOPIE) 1881-1958, which would hold LIZZY'S BIRTH OF 28 AUGUST 1893. Film 7948906 holds HEIRATEN 1700-1895, which would hold Joachim's marriage to Johanna Thimm. THE ONE FILM THAT IS ONLINE, 102682510, WAS OPENED AND CHECKED: 683 images, and at image 591 the camera photographed the film's own title board reading 'GROSS-BÖSSAU / KRS.RÖSSEL / 1798-1847 / ✝'. Right parish, wrong years — its baptisms stop in 1792. THREE ROUTES, IN ORDER OF COST: order 7948905 and 7769256 at a Family History Centre, where undigitised films can be viewed; write to the Archiwum Archidiecezji Warmińskiej at Olsztyn, which holds the Ermland originals; or re-check the two film numbers periodically, which is one request each. AND A WARNING FOR WHOEVER GOES: THE VIEWER FILES THIS CATHOLIC PARISH UNDER 'GERMANY, LUTHERAN BAPTISMS, MARRIAGES AND BURIALS'. The catalogue says Katholische Kirche and the Ermland was Catholic; the title board settles it. Anyone trusting the collection label would conclude these are the wrong registers and go home. In data/ermland-sauerbaum.tsv.

rows.what: AROLSEN HOLDS KURT HIMSELF — and six more Luwinskis from this family
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER, found while checking Arolsen for somebody else. THE WHOLE SURNAME RETURNS NINE RECORDS AND SEVEN OF THEM MATCH THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN REGISTER BY EXACT DATE OF BIRTH. *** KURT IS ONE OF THEM. *** LUWINSKI, Kurt, 05/11/1912 — DocID 11214358, '1 Incarceration Documents / 1.2.1 DEPORTATIONS AND TRANSPORTS / Part 24: Folder MFN01335', five hundred documents. THAT IS THE SAME DocID THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD FOR JACOB AND AUGUSTE, so the three of them are in one folder, and Kurt's index date of birth matches the register to the day. The archive knew the DocID; it did not know Kurt was indexed under his own name in it. THE OTHERS, IN FOUR DIFFERENT DOCUMENT CLASSES: FELIX (19.02.1923) in the Allied registration of foreigners and persecutees, DocID 69931515; MANFRED (14.11.1933) AND HELGA (01.05.1934) SHARING ONE DocID, 81709354, in '3.1.3 EMIGRATIONS — correspondence and nominal rolls'; ALFRED (09.09.1917) in post-war evaluations, DocID 130648701. Two further entries are a name-variant card and a surname with no forename. TWO MORE ARE PEOPLE FLAGGED LIVING IN THE FAMILY TREE AND ARE NOT NAMED — the build's own guard would stop them. *** WHY THIS IS BLOCKED AND OWNED BY DAVID. *** Every document behind these entries requires the consent declaration to be ticked, and I do not tick declarations on anybody's behalf. Name, date of birth, DocID and archival path are all Arolsen shows without it, and all of them are now recorded. ONE TICK BY DAVID OPENS FIVE DOCUMENTS, and the one that matters most is not Kurt's — it is 81709354, an EMIGRATION file naming two Luwinskis born a year apart, which is the only document in any archive that might say where the Berlin Luwinskis went. In data/arolsen-leibholz-luwinski.tsv. *** OPENED 20 SEPTEMBER, THE SAME DAY, AND IT IS THE BEST DOCUMENT OF THE WEEK. *** DocID 81709354 is an INTERGOVERNMENTAL COMMITTEE FOR EUROPEAN MIGRATION NOMINAL ROLL, headed MELBOURNE, numbered BGO 65/135, marked "AUSTRALIAN GOVERNMENT FINANCIALLY ASSISTED", stamped SEPTEMBER 1965, filed under "3.1.3 EMIGRATIONS — transport by airplane". Lines 85 to 88 are one family: MANFRED LUWINSKI, born 14.11.33, aged 32, of BERLIN, occupation MODELL FITTER; HELGA, born 1.05.34, aged 31, of Berlin; and TWO CHILDREN AGED TEN AND THREE WHO ARE FLAGGED LIVING AND ARE NOT NAMED. Forwarding address: c/o Mr H. MARQUARDT, HACKETT, CANBERRA ACT — and the family tree carries Manfred's wife as HELGA ERNA MARQUARDT Wagner. HER FAMILY WAS ALREADY IN AUSTRALIA AND BROUGHT THEM OUT. THE BERLIN DIRECTORY LINES UP EXACTLY: Manfred is a SCHLOSSER at Egellsstraße 16, Tegel, in 1957, 1959 and 1961 and vanishes after 1961. Schlosser and model fitter are the same trade. HE VANISHES BECAUSE HE LEFT THE COUNTRY. AND THE TREE ALREADY KNEW WHERE HE ENDED UP WITHOUT KNOWING HOW: Manfred Joachim Luwinski, died 20 SEPTEMBER 2012 AT BRISBANE. This document is the journey between Berlin and Brisbane. In data/luwinski-emigration-1965.tsv.

rows.what: THE TREE'S ALFRED GENERATION IS INTERNALLY IMPOSSIBLE
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER, and it is a fault in the family tree rather than a gap in the records. The MyHeritage export makes ALFRED LUWINSKI, BORN 9 SEPTEMBER 1917, the father of MANFRED born 14 November 1933 and JOACHIM born 30 November 1940 — and gives Alfred's wife as MARTHA SCHUENKE, WHO IT SAYS DIED IN 1930. SO THE FATHER WAS SIXTEEN AT THE FIRST BIRTH AND THE MOTHER HAD BEEN DEAD FOR THREE YEARS. It cannot stand as written. AND IT MEETS THE SAME PROBLEM FROM THE OTHER SIDE: the 1933 Berliner Adressbuch has ALFRED LUWINSKI, BÜGLER, A HEAD OF HOUSEHOLD at Putbusser Straße 24, which fits a man old enough to father a child that year and does not fit a boy of sixteen. THREE READINGS AND THE ARCHIVE SHOULD NOT PICK ONE: (a) the 1917 birth date belongs to a different Alfred and has been attached to the wrong man; (b) there are two Alfred Luwinskis, father and son, and the tree has collapsed them; (c) Martha Schuenke's 1930 death is the error. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: Manfred's own birth registration of 14 November 1933 at Berlin, which names both parents and their ages. Berlin Standesamt records of 1933 are not open, but Manfred emigrated to Australia in 1965 and DIED AT BRISBANE IN 2012 — an Australian death certificate names the deceased's parents, and Queensland registrations of that date are obtainable. THAT IS A CHEAPER ROUTE TO ALFRED THAN ANYTHING IN GERMANY, and it is in David's own state. *** ANSWERED WITHIN THE HOUR, FROM THE DOCUMENT THE TREE ITSELF CITES. *** Arolsen DocID 130648701 is a registration card of the Berlin 'Amt für die Erfassung der Kriegsopfer', and every field on it contradicts the tree. ALFRED LUWINSKI, born 9.9.17, Geburtsort a POLISH place; Beruf LANDWIRT; religion KATH.; nationality POLN.; *** FAMILIENSTAND: LEDIG — SINGLE *** ; INHAFTIERT SACHSENHAUSEN; 'gestorben 11.7.42 15:20, Herz- und Kreislaufschwäche', death certificate 1924/42. The reverse gives his home: 'wohnhaft PRZASNYSZ, PIŁSUDSKIEGO 117' — Masovia, north of Warsaw. SO HE IS A POLISH CATHOLIC FARM LABOURER WHO DIED AT SACHSENHAUSEN AT TWENTY-FOUR AND NEVER MARRIED. HE IS NOT THE FATHER OF ANYBODY BORN IN 1933 OR 1940. AND THE TREE CITES THIS EXACT URL as its source for Manfred's 1933 birth AND for Martha Schuenke's 1930 death. THE CARD CONTAINS NEITHER FACT AND NEITHER PERSON. Reading (b) of the three offered above is the right one: there are two Alfreds and the tree has collapsed them — or rather three, because the 1933 Berliner Adressbuch's ALFRED LUWINSKI, BÜGLER, PUTBUSSER STRASSE 24, a head of household, is a third man and is now THE ONLY CANDIDATE THIS ARCHIVE HAS for Manfred's actual father. WHAT FOLLOWS: MANFRED AND JOACHIM'S FATHER IS UNKNOWN. The Queensland death certificate suggested above is still the cheapest way to a name. In data/alfred-luwinski-sachsenhausen.tsv.

rows.what: KURT IS BURIED AT THE CHEVRA KADISHA — the one cemetery this archive ruled out
rows.note: NOTICED 20 SEPTEMBER while reading the tree against the Arolsen documents, and it is an exclusion this archive made for a good reason and never revisited. Row 77 swept every Wear in the Johannesburg municipal cemetery registers and stated its bounds honestly, including: 'it does not cover the Chevrah Kadisha, which is a separate database — A WEAR WOULD HAVE NO BUSINESS IN A JEWISH CEMETERY but the exclusion is stated rather than assumed.' THAT IS RIGHT ABOUT THE WEARS AND WRONG ABOUT KURT. The family tree gives his burial as CHEVRA KADISHA, JOHANNESBURG. He was registered as a Jew in Germany, carried the imposed name Israel out of it, and the tree says he was buried by the Johannesburg Jewish burial society. THE CHEVRAH KADISHA MAINTAINS ITS OWN BURIAL DATABASE and it is not in FamilySearch's municipal collection. ONE ENQUIRY WOULD GIVE A DATE OF DEATH, A PLOT AND USUALLY THE NAME OF WHOEVER ARRANGED THE BURIAL — which is the question row 57 could never answer for his family. AND IT MAY SETTLE A DISCREPANCY THIS ARCHIVE IS CARRYING: the work list says Kurt died on 15 DECEMBER 1968 and the tree says 15 DECEMBER 1969, with an estate numbered 7584/1969. The day and month agree and the year does not. *** STRUCK THE SAME DAY, AND THE ROW WAS WRONG BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN. *** THIS ARCHIVE HAS ALREADY CONSULTED THE JOHANNESBURG CHEVRAH KADISHA BURIAL REGISTER. It is the source of the FIRST entry in data/corrections.json and of the third: 'Kurt Israel Luwinski, died: was Dec 15 1969, now 15 DECEMBER 1968 — Johannesburg Chevrah Kadisha burial register: died 15.12.1968, buried 16.12.1968, WESTPARK BLOCK L GRAVE 211, Yahrzeit 24 Kislev 5729, which is itself 15 December 1968'; and 'Morris Isaac Salkow ... Westpark block U grave 2469'. SO EVERYTHING THIS ROW ASKED FOR IS ALREADY HELD: the date, the plot, and the Hebrew date cross-checking the civil one. IT ALSO SETTLES THE DISCREPANCY THE ROW RAISED, in the opposite direction to the one I assumed: the tree says 1969, the burial register says 1968, AND THE CORRECTION HAS BEEN IN THE FILE ALL ALONG. And one thing worth carrying away rather than losing with the row: KURT IS BURIED AT WEST PARK — block L, grave 211, in the Jewish section. THE SAME CEMETERY AS HENRY ROBERT AND MARTHA MAUD WEAR, who are in grave 56045, section E.C. Derrick's biological father's parents and the man who raised his mother's household lie in one ground. THAT IS THE THIRD TIME TODAY I have raised as new something this archive already had. The pattern is worth naming: I have been reading the work list and the page text and not corrections.json, which is where the hardest-won facts are.

rows.what: ALFRED LUWINSKI OF PRZASNYSZ — found by mistake, and kept
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER. He was opened because a family tree said he was somebody's father, and he was not. HE IS RECORDED HERE ANYWAY, because the archive found him and dropping him because he is not useful would be the wrong instinct. ALFRED LUWINSKI, BORN 9 SEPTEMBER 1917 in Poland, a CATHOLIC FARM LABOURER, SINGLE, of PRZASNYSZ, PIŁSUDSKIEGO 117, in Masovia about a hundred kilometres from the East Prussian border. Imprisoned at SACHSENHAUSEN. DIED THERE ON 11 JULY 1942 AT TWENTY PAST THREE IN THE AFTERNOON; the card gives 'Herz- und Kreislaufschwäche', heart and circulatory failure, which is the standard camp formula and is not a cause of death. Death certificate 1924 of 1942. The Polish diplomatic mission and the I.R.O. were notified after the war and a later hand has dated the card 16.5.72 — somebody was still asking about him thirty years on. ONE THING WORTH NOTING AND NOT OVERREADING: Przasnysz is Masovian and the archive's other Luwinskis are East Prussian and Posen. The surname is thinly spread across all three, which is why it is traceable at all and why it keeps putting the wrong man in the right slot.

rows.what: AN AROLSEN INDEX ENTRY IS A POINTER, NOT A FACT — two of the tree's Luwinskis are misattached records
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER, after opening four Arolsen documents with David's consent and finding TWO MISATTRIBUTIONS IN THE FAMILY TREE, both of the same shape. (1) ALFRED LUWINSKI, born 9.9.1917: the tree makes him Manfred and Joachim's father and cites his Arolsen record. THE CARD SAYS POLISH, CATHOLIC, FARM LABOURER, *LEDIG* — SINGLE — SACHSENHAUSEN, DIED 11 JULY 1942 AGED TWENTY-FOUR, of Przasnysz in Masovia. He fathered nobody. (2) FELIX LUWINSKI, born 19.2.1923: the tree gives his birthplace as GRAFENAU, GERMANY and cites Arolsen. THE DOCUMENT GIVES NO BIRTHPLACE — it is a Form 11 return of the Landrat Grafenau dated 19 AUGUST 1946, an Allied listing of foreigners in the American Zone, and its nationality field reads RUSSLAND. THE PLACE OF REGISTRATION HAS BECOME THE PLACE OF BIRTH. *** THE RULE, AND THIS ARCHIVE SHOULD APPLY IT TO ITSELF BEFORE ANYONE ELSE. *** An Arolsen index entry gives a name, a date of birth and a DocID. EVERYTHING ELSE IS ON THE DOCUMENT. Until the document is opened, any place, relationship, occupation or fate attached to that entry is somebody's guess — and once it is written into a tree it gets cited back as though the archive had said it. FOUR DOCUMENTS OPENED, TWO MISATTRIBUTIONS. WHAT TO DO: the remaining Arolsen entries this archive has recorded WITHOUT opening the document — the 191 Leibholz index entries in data/arolsen-leibholz-luwinski.tsv — should be treated as pointers and nothing more until somebody opens them, and the file should say so. *** THE AUDIT WAS RUN, 20 SEPTEMBER, AND IT IS NOW A TOOL RATHER THAN A ONE-OFF: tools/audit-tree.py. *** 164 PEOPLE, 59 CITED FACTS, THREE HOSTS. (A) AROLSEN: SEVEN CITED FACTS AND ALL SEVEN POINT AT THE SAME DOCUMENT — DocID 130648701, Alfred Luwinski's Sachsenhausen card. ONE of the seven is supported by it, his own birth date. THE OTHER SIX ARE FALSE: two parents' 'birth of son', Alfred's fatherhood of Manfred, Martha Schuenke's 1930 death and her 'birth of son', and Manfred's 1933 birth. The card names no parents, no wife and no children and says LEDIG. (B) FAMILYSEARCH: FORTY-SIX CITED FACTS AND ONLY TWO ARE WRONG — 7 exact, 25 where the record is one to forty-five days after the event, 9 with no record date to check against. AND THE FIRST PASS OF THIS AUDIT SAID THIRTY-THREE WERE WRONG, WHICH WAS ITSELF THE ERROR: those 25 are PARISH REGISTERS, where the record is the BAPTISM or the BURIAL and the tree correctly holds the birth or the death. Stanilaus born 27 September 1810 and baptised 14 October; Valentin dead 12 July 1878 and buried on the 15th. A crude date comparison calls every one of those a mismatch. THE TWO THAT ARE REAL ARE THE SAME ERROR TWICE: Ivone's and Johannes de Witt's marriage of 2 FEBRUARY 1948 both cite the record of KURT AND IVONE'S MARRIAGE OF 19 JUNE 1948 — the wrong husband, 138 days out. The right record is already in hand from 17 September: ark 1:1:6ZCM-J38T, Germiston. (C) NAAIRS: six citations, NONE VERIFIABLE — they are URLs with session tokens that would not resolve even if the service were up, and it has not answered since 16 September. (D) INTERNAL IMPOSSIBILITIES: THREE IN 164 PEOPLE, found by arithmetic alone. Two are Martha Schuenke, dead in 1930 with sons born 1933 and 1940. THE THIRD IS NEW AND PAYS FOR THE AUDIT: JOHANNES ANTONIE OELOFSE DE WITT, born December 1923 at Johannesburg, has a SON OF THE SAME NAME born CIRCA 1923 AT PRETORIA, and both die at SASOLBURG. ONE MAN, SPLIT IN TWO — and the duplicate is carrying a fact the original lacks: DEATH 2 APRIL 1963 AT SASOLBURG. SO IVONE'S FIRST HUSBAND HAS A DATE OF DEATH, AND IT WAS HIDDEN INSIDE A DUPLICATE. The split also invented a phantom wife and a spurious half-sister relationship. *** AND THE RULE THAT COMES OUT OF IT. *** The FamilySearch citations are good BECAUSE EACH ONE CARRIES THE RECORD'S OWN DESCRIPTION IN ITS TEXT, so a wrong one can be caught without opening anything. The Arolsen citations are bare URLs with nothing to check against, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY SIX WRONG ONES SURVIVED. A citation that cannot be falsified from its own text is not much of a citation. In data/tree-audit.tsv.

rows.what: IVONE'S FIRST HUSBAND DIED AT SASOLBURG ON 2 APRIL 1963 — and the tree has him twice
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER, out of the tree audit, and it is both a correction and a gain. The tree holds JOHANNES ANTONIE OELOFSE DE WITT twice: record 9500005, born December 1923 at Johannesburg, son of Frederik Petrus Johannes de Witt and Delina Johanna Oelofse who married at Burgersdorp on 3 October 1921, with a death place of SASOLBURG and NO DATE; and record 9500160, 'his son', of the SAME NAME, born CIRCA 1923 AT PRETORIA, DIED 2 APRIL 1963 AT SASOLBURG. A father aged nought, and both men dying in the same small Free State town. THEY ARE ONE MAN. *** SO IVONE'S FIRST HUSBAND DIED ON 2 APRIL 1963, AGED THIRTY-NINE, AT SASOLBURG *** — a date this archive did not have, sitting inside the duplicate. WHAT THE SPLIT ALSO CREATED: a phantom wife, 'Unknown de Witt' (9500161), who exists only to be the duplicate's mother, and a 'half sister' relationship for Delina de Witt that is an artefact rather than a fact about anybody. WHAT TO DO: this is the MyHeritage export and this archive's rule is that the charts draw the export as given — so the fix belongs in data/corrections.json as a was/now correction, not as an edit to the harvest. AND ONE CHECK BEFORE IT GOES IN: a South African death index or estate file for de Witt at Sasolburg in 1963 would confirm the date independently, and Sasolburg is in the Free State, so it is the Orange Free State estate files — a set FamilySearch has fully digitised, 1951 to 2006, on 57 waypoints. *** DONE 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND THE ESTATE FILES WERE NOT NEEDED. *** The row proposed browsing 57 waypoints of unindexed Orange Free State estate images. THE NATIONAL DEATH REGISTRATION INDEX COVERS 1953-1967 AND HAS HIM: "South Africa, Civil Death Registration, 1953-1967", Entry for JOHANNES ANTONIE OELOFSE DE WITT, 2 APRIL 1963, SASOLBURG, ORANGE FREE STATE, AGED 40, BORN 1923 AT PRETORIA (ark 1:1:DD9Y-PLT2). The duplicate's date is confirmed from outside the tree, and the duplicate's BIRTHPLACE is confirmed too — Pretoria, which is the half 9500005 disagreed with. *** AND THE SAME SEARCH FOUND A SECOND MARRIAGE NOBODY HAD: *** JOHANNES ANTONIE OELOFSE DEWITT and ELSIE MARIE GEYER, 25 FEBRUARY 1950, groom aged 27 (ark 1:1:6ZHR-NVYN). Ivone's first husband remarried two years after she left him and outlived that marriage by thirteen years. THE ONE THING IT UNSETTLES: three officials recorded his age — 25 in Feb 1948, 27 in Feb 1950, 40 in Apr 1963 — and the three ranges overlap at APRIL 1922 TO FEBRUARY 1923. The tree's "December 1923" is outside all three. Declared ages are not proof; three of them agreeing is recorded, not asserted. Written up in data/dewitt-confirmed.tsv, on the Ivone page, and into corrections 9500005 and 9500160. THE ESTATE FILE IS STILL THERE if anyone ever wants the de Witt line itself, which is not this family's.

rows.what: T/D 52.971 — somebody asked the Tracing Service what became of Oskar Leibholz, and the file names them
rows.owner: the Arolsen Archives — a letter is drafted
rows.note: CARVED OUT OF ROW 170 ON 20 SEPTEMBER, BECAUSE THE CONSENT THAT BLOCKED IT IS NOW TICKED AND IT DESERVES ITS OWN LINE. The Arolsen index holds a TRACING AND DOCUMENTATION CASE, T/D NO. 52.971, for 'LEIBHOLZ, OSCAR born 13.05.1887' — FOURTEEN DOCUMENTS. A T/D file is opened when a PERSON ASKS THE INTERNATIONAL TRACING SERVICE what became of somebody, and IT NAMES THE ENQUIRER AND THEIR RELATIONSHIP TO THE MISSING PERSON. Oskar was deported to Theresienstadt in March 1943 and murdered at Auschwitz on 16 October 1944; his wife Gertrud died on 27 February 1943. SO WHOEVER ASKED WAS NEITHER OF THEM, AND WAS ALIVE AFTER THE WAR AND KNEW HIM WELL ENOUGH TO ASK. This archive's whole difficulty with the Leibholz generation is that it has no survivor to anchor it: Margot Cox and Irmgard Shtern came from Pages of Testimony and are attached to GEORG's family, which the archive argues is a different family altogether. A NAMED ENQUIRER ATTACHED TO OSKAR — who IS Jacob's brother, both born at Schubin — WOULD BE THE FIRST SURVIVOR ON KURT'S OWN SIDE. Fourteen documents, and the consent is already given. *** WORKED 20 SEPTEMBER, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE CONSENT DOES NOT REACH IT. *** The topic page for 06030302.0.052.971 serves METADATA AND NO IMAGES — no document list, no DocIDs, no viewer, and the row expander opens nothing — and it carries its own explanation: 'UNDER CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES, PARTS OF THE FILE ARE NOT DISPLAYED FOR DATA PROTECTION REASONS. In such cases, please contact the Arolsen Archives.' THE DECLARATION OPENS DEPORTATION LISTS, REGISTRATION CARDS AND POST-WAR REGISTRATIONS AND STOPS AT THE CORRESPONDENCE, which is consistent with what a T/D file is. ONE THING THE METADATA DOES GIVE: creation date 1949 TO 2002. The enquiry was opened in 1949 and the file was still being added to fifty-three years later. SO THE ACTION IS A LETTER AND IT IS DRAFTED, NOT SENT: requests/29-SEND-THIS-to-arolsen.txt, which asks for the enquirer's name and relationship, accepts that part may stay closed, and asks whether the 2002 activity means a second person asked. *** AND THE HUNT PRODUCED SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY, WHICH IS IN THE NEW ROW. ***

rows.what: RUTH-TRUDE TABORI-HAMMER WROTE FROM PALESTINE IN 1946 LOOKING FOR THE LENAUSTRASSE FAMILY
rows.note: FOUND 20 SEPTEMBER while failing to open T/D 52.971. A DIFFERENT AROLSEN SERIES IS SERVED WITHOUT RESTRICTION: 6.3.1.1, 'Searching for missing persons — TRACING INQUIRIES 1945-1946'. Searching LEIBHOLZ there returns 43 topics, including a 'Personal file of LEIBHOLZ, ROSA' — a forename this archive has never seen — and 'Personal file of LEIBHOLZ, WILLI and of further persons', five documents, WHICH WERE READ. *** IT IS A JEWISH AGENCY FOR PALESTINE SEARCH BUREAU FOR MISSING RELATIVES FORM, JERUSALEM, QUESTIONNAIRE NO. 2, DATED 23 MAY 1946, FILE 50764. *** THE PERSON SOUGHT: LEIBHOLZ, WILLI, aged 55, BORN AT STOLP IN POMMERN; last information MARCH 1943 FROM BERLIN; last address BERLIN-NEUKÖLLN, LENAUSTRASSE 25; occupation BUTCHER. With him: ERNA, 48, born HAMMER, wife; HEINZ, 23, son; AND RUTH, 22, DAUGHTER — A CHILD THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE. THE PERSON WHO ASKED: TABORI-HAMMER born NACHUM, RUTH-TRUDE, of BENEI-BRAQ, JEHOSHUASTRASSE, PALESTINE, born 9 SEPTEMBER 1899 AT HAMBURG, last address abroad BERLIN-MOABIT, TURMSTRASSE 59, relationship 'BROTHER IN LAW AND HIS FAMILY', signed in her own hand. The ITS answered her on 8 December 1947 through the Jewish Agency and closed the case on 22 December. *** AND IT SETTLES THE QUESTION I LEFT OPEN THIS MORNING. *** I wrote then that 'nothing here says where Willi was born beyond Germany'. STOLP IN POMMERN IS NOT SCHUBIN IN POSEN — two hundred and fifty miles and a different province — SO THE LENAUSTRASSE LEIBHOLZES ARE DOCUMENTED AS NOT KURT'S FAMILY rather than merely unproven. TWO HAMMERS SURVIVED AND BOTH WENT LOOKING: Ruth-Trude in 1946, and EVA KHAVA HAMMER OLSHER, niece, who wrote Willi's and Erna's Pages of Testimony later. BOTH COME THROUGH ERNA'S FAMILY, NOT WILLI'S. THE HONEST DISAPPOINTMENT: the row wanted a survivor on KURT'S side, and the file that would give one is the closed one.

rows.what: THREE MORE TRACING FILES OPEN AND UNREAD — Heinz, Rosa, and Oskar's other four records
rows.note: DONE 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, all three, and the third one was the prize. (1) T/D 755.334 FOR HEINZ IS RESTRICTED. Tested, not assumed: reference 06030302.0.755.334, creation date 1959-1988, eleven documents, the same data-protection sentence Oskar's file carries, and NO DocID, NO IMAGE, NO DOCUMENT LIST. The consent declaration does not reach the T/D repository, and 755.333 ERNA and 755.335 RUTH stand beside it — three consecutive case numbers for the Lenaustraße household. (2) THE ROSA FILE IS ONE SHEET OF PAPER. DocID 86338329, a cross-reference slip in red: "AJDC-Berlin · Leibholz, Rosa · X-Reference = Silbermann, Heinz; ", Else; ", Inge". No date, no place, so it cannot be tied to this family or ruled out; what it gives is a route, because her papers were filed under SILBERMANN. (3) OSKAR'S OTHER RECORDS — AND THEY CARRY HIM OUT OF THERESIENSTADT. The Theresienstadt central card file (1.1.42.2, DocID 5055941) holds a Czech card: "Leibholz Oskar · 13.5.1887 · DEPORTACE NA VÝCHOD: Číslo Er 606, dne 16.X.1944 · (původní transportní číslo: 11025-I/90)". THE ORIGINAL TRANSPORT NUMBER IS THE BERLIN TRANSPORT'S OWN DESIGNATION — the Gestapo list of 17 March 1943 names itself "(I/90)" in its scope note. The two ends of the journey name each other. The AJDC card (1.2.1.2, DocID 11243228) gives SCHUBIN/BROMBERG in full, the deportation address BERLIN W 50 MARBURGERSTR. 13, the filing "49/30999 II — 4.gr.Alterstrsp. 17.3.43", and "Ehefrau: (Sa) GERTRUD geb. LEIBKE 13.7.94 Berlin". The Berlin registration card (1.2.1.5, DocID 11214364) puts Oskar and Gertrud on one form with CONSECUTIVE KENNKARTE NUMBERS, A 442 462 and A 442 461. ON "Verw.Abz." THE ROW'S INSTRUCTION STANDS AND IS NOT BROKEN: the abbreviation is still not expanded here. What was learned is what kind of column it sits in — the same column carries "Geltungsjude", "Ehepaar", "Pflegekind" and "Sohn von Nr. 69", so it is a column of exemption and relationship categories. That narrows it and does not settle it. Written up in data/oskar-leibholz-theresienstadt.tsv and data/arolsen-tracing-files.tsv. *** RE-TESTED LATER ON 20 SEPTEMBER AFTER DAVID TICKED THE CONSENT AGAIN, AND NOTHING CHANGED. *** T/D 52.971 still serves fourteen documents' worth of metadata and no DocID, no image, no list; T/D 755.334 the same with eleven. THE RESTRICTION IS ON THE SERIES, NOT ON THE USER — which is now tested twice rather than assumed. The declaration was never the obstacle; it is what opens the SERVED collections, and it has been open all day, for Oskar's four records, Jacob's transport list, Gertrud's Zählkarte, the Shanghai CLI card and the Willi file. HEINZ'S FILE HAS BEEN ADDED TO LETTER 29 rather than sent as a second letter, and the letter now says plainly that both were tested twice with the consent in place.

rows.what: ADD THE 1874 SZUBIN MARRIAGE TO THE BYDGOSZCZ THREAD — it names both sets of parents
rows.owner: David — to send on the open Bydgoszcz thread
rows.note: *** SUPERSEDED 22 SEPTEMBER 2026 — DO NOT SEND THIS ONE. *** The draft at requests/30-SEND-THIS-to-bydgoszcz.txt asked Bydgoszcz for the 1874 Szubin marriage because it names both sets of parents. IT WAS NEVER SENT, AND IT NO LONGER NEEDS TO BE: the archive answered the 14 September letter on 22 September by pointing at genealogiawarchiwach.pl, and the marriage was read at the image the same hour — akt nr 9 of 24 November 1874, USC Szubin Miasto sygn. 141 scan 10. It gives Sally Leibholz as born and resident at Hammerstein, aged twenty-seven, son of the Kaufmann JACOB LEIBHOLZ and WILHELMINE GEB. POLLNOW. THE DOCUMENT THIS ROW EXISTED TO OBTAIN IS NOW READ AND PUBLISHED. The letter's own fallback question — whether Bydgoszcz holds the Szubin Jewish community records — is the one thing in it still worth asking, and it has been lifted out into its own draft at requests/36, which is row 266. NEW 20 SEPTEMBER, out of David's question about the SCHMUL family, AND IT IS THE CHEAPEST UNWORKED THING ON THIS LIST because the letter is already sent and acknowledged. The front-page chart says SALLY LEIBHOLZ & FRIEDERIKE SCHMUL, 'Hammerstein · married Szubin 1874'. FRIEDERIKE IS NOT IN FAMILYSEARCH'S POSEN CHURCH BOOKS — all 33 exact SCHMUL records there were read and she is not among them — AND SHE WOULD NOT BE, because those are CHURCH books and a Jewish marriage is not in one. PRUSSIAN CIVIL REGISTRATION BEGAN ON 1 OCTOBER 1874, so a Szubin marriage that year is either a Jewish community register entry or a STANDESAMT SCHUBIN entry. EITHER WAY IT IS AT THE ARCHIWUM PAŃSTWOWE W BYDGOSZCZY — the same archive this archive wrote to on 15 September for Standesamt Schubin 1884, Jacob's birth, and which acknowledged with a warning that complex queries take over a month. ADD THE MARRIAGE TO THAT THREAD RATHER THAN OPENING A NEW ONE. WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE BIRTH CERTIFICATE: A PRUSSIAN MARRIAGE CERTIFICATE OF 1874 NAMES BOTH SETS OF PARENTS with ages and occupations. It would give FRIEDERIKE SCHMUL'S FATHER AND MOTHER and SALLY LEIBHOLZ'S — the generation ABOVE the top of the chart, which this archive has never reached on any line of the German side. ONE THING TO SAY IN THE LETTER: the chart says the couple were 'of Hammerstein' and married at Szubin, and Hammerstein is in WEST PRUSSIA while Szubin is in POSEN. If the 1874 record is not at Bydgoszcz it may be at the state archive holding Hammerstein, and correction 5 — which rests on Georg being born at Hammerstein and Jacob at Schubin — WOULD NEED RE-EXAMINING, because a family with both places in it is exactly what that correction assumes is impossible. *** DRAFTED THE SAME DAY: requests/30-SEND-THIS-to-bydgoszcz.txt, in Polish with an English translation beneath, in the house style used for Koszalin. NOT SENT. *** It is written as a REPLY ON THE EXISTING THREAD rather than a new enquiry, so it lands against the same file, and the note at the top says so — the archive has not recorded which address was used on 15 September and THE LETTER DOES NOT INVENT ONE; the sent mail has it. WHAT IT ASKS: the 1874 Szubin marriage of SALLY (Sali, Salomon) LEIBHOLZ, born at Czarne 1847, and FRIEDERIKE born SCHMUL. It raises the 1 OCTOBER 1874 boundary itself rather than letting them discover it, asks them to check BOTH the Standesamt books AND the Szubin Jewish community register, and says that even an answer naming the right series would be worth having. IT ALSO TELLS THEM WHICH TO DO FIRST IF THEY CAN ONLY DO ONE: the 1874 marriage, not the 1884 birth, because Jacob's parents are known and his grandparents are not. And it gives them the reason it has become urgent — KOSZALIN ANSWERED ON 16 SEPTEMBER that the 1884 Czarne books are not available and that they do not know what became of them. SALLY WAS BORN AT CZARNE IN 1847. If those books are gone, the Szubin marriage may be the only surviving document that names his parents.

rows.what: ZEUTERN IS PART OF KRAICHTAL — mother and daughter died in the same town
rows.note: NOTICED 20 SEPTEMBER while answering David's question about the Thimms, and it is a join this archive already had the pieces for. The East Prussia page records JOHANNA THIMM as dying on 30 OCTOBER 1955 AT ZEUTERN NEAR BRUCHSAL, and AUGUSTE 'LIZZY' LUWINSKI as dying on 22 JUNE 1975 AT KRAICHTAL. IT LISTS THEM AS TWO PLACES. ZEUTERN IS A DISTRICT OF KRAICHTAL. Mother and daughter died in the same small Baden-Württemberg town, twenty years apart — out of the Ermland, through Berlin, and into the west. THE PAGE SHOULD SAY SO IN ONE LINE. AND IT BEARS ON THE FRICKE CANDIDATE RAISED THIS MORNING: Johanna's own addresses include RICHARD-WAGNER-STRASSE 42, CHARLOTTENBURG, from 24 July 1932, and the 1957 directory candidate is 'Fricke Auguste, Rentnerin, Charlottenburg 1, Kaiser-Friedrich-Straße 79' — THE SAME DISTRICT. That does not confirm it, and Lizzy ending at Kraichtal where her mother died pulls the other way. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT IS ONE RECORD: Lizzy's death registration of 22 June 1975 at Kraichtal, which is a Baden-Württemberg Standesamt entry and is David's to order. It would also confirm or break the Charlottenburg address. *** DONE 20 SEPTEMBER 2026. *** The East Prussia page now says it in three places: the two entries in the key-value list, and a panel. ZEUTERN IS ONE OF THE NINE VILLAGES AMALGAMATED INTO KRAICHTAL IN 1971-75, which is why the 1955 death is registered under the village and the 1975 death under the town; Johanna's last address, Besingstraße 110 at Zeutern, is a Kraichtal street. The same edit carried a second thing found the same day: DocID 11214358, opened at last, gives AUGUSTE'S BIRTHPLACE AS SAUERBAUM IN HER OWN HOUSEHOLD'S HAND — a second independent source for what had rested on the 1939 census card alone — and gives SIEGFRIED'S BIRTHPLACE AS BERLIN-SCHÖNEBERG, which nothing else did. THE FRICKE CANDIDATE IS NOT ADVANCED BY ANY OF THIS and stays where it was.

rows.what: SALLY LEIBHOLZ WAS BORN AT HAMMERSTEIN — which complicates correction 5 rather than settling it
rows.note: NOTICED 20 SEPTEMBER while drafting the Bydgoszcz follow-up, and it deserves stating because it cuts against something this archive has published. CORRECTION 5 in data/corrections.json disputes Georg Leibholz's brotherhood on exactly this ground: 'Born Hammerstein, West Prussia, 7 June 1884; Jacob born Schubin, Posen, 8 August 1884. Two months and two hundred kilometres apart.' THE ARGUMENT TREATS HAMMERSTEIN AS A PLACE THIS FAMILY HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH. IT IS NOT. The front-page chart says the great-grandparents were 'Hammerstein · married Szubin 1874', and the Koszalin letter of 15 September asked that archive for 'Standesamt Hammerstein 1884 — Georg; AND SALLY, 1847'. SO SALLY LEIBHOLZ, JACOB'S OWN FATHER, WAS BORN AT HAMMERSTEIN. The family had people in both towns. THAT DOES NOT MAKE GEORG A BROTHER — two sons of one mother cannot be born two months apart, and that arithmetic is untouched — BUT IT REMOVES THE GEOGRAPHY FROM THE ARGUMENT. A Leibholz born at Hammerstein in 1884 is no longer a stranger who happens to share a surname; he is a Leibholz born in the town Jacob's father came from, which is what a COUSIN looks like. Open question 5 asks 'Is Georg a brother or a cousin?' and this makes cousin the stronger reading rather than 'a different Leibholz family'. WHAT TO DO: the correction's wording should be revisited — not reversed, because the dates still rule out brotherhood, but its stated REASON is now half wrong. And the 1874 marriage record, if Bydgoszcz finds it, would name Sally's parents and make the cousin test answerable. *** FIXED THE SAME DAY — AND THE ROW OVERSTATED ITS OWN NOVELTY, WHICH HAS TO BE SAID. *** The Leibholz page's NEXT PANEL, 'A likelier reading', has carried the right answer since the start: 'Sally Leibholz was himself born at Hammerstein, on 7 JULY 1847, and married at Szubin on 24 NOVEMBER 1874. So the family had people in both towns... Georg belonged to the Hammerstein branch Sally came from — a nephew or a cousin of Jacob's, not a brother', with his status given as 'right surname, RIGHT FAMILY, wrong generation'. And open question 5 is already headed 'Is Georg a brother or a cousin?'. SO THE ARCHIVE HAD THE READING. What was wrong was narrower and sharper than this row claimed: TWO PLACES CONTRADICTED IT. (1) corrections.json entry 5 said 'disputed — A DIFFERENT LEIBHOLZ FAMILY' and gave as its reason 'two hundred kilometres apart'. (2) The Leibholz page, one paragraph ABOVE the panel that says the opposite, said 'These are two Leibholz families. Ours is the Schubin one.' BOTH ARE NOW REWRITTEN. The correction reads 'NOT A BROTHER — the dates forbid it. Probably a cousin or nephew of the same family', and rests on SIXTY-TWO DAYS rather than on the distance; the page says in as many words that it used to claim two families and that this was wrong. AND THE FIX PAID FOR ITSELF: the panel also gave the MARRIAGE DATE, 24 NOVEMBER 1874, which is SEVEN WEEKS AFTER Prussian civil registration began on 1 October. The Bydgoszcz letter drafted an hour earlier raised that boundary as an open question. It no longer speculates — it gives the date, says the record should be an ordinary 1874 Standesamt Szubin entry, and keeps the Jewish community register only as a fallback. FOURTH TIME TODAY. The cause is the same one named this morning: I read the work list and the top of a page, and the answer was further down it.

rows.what: WAS GERTRUD ON THE SAME TRANSPORT AS OSKAR? The list has 1,200 names and only one page has been looked at
rows.note: Oskar is line 54 of page 161 of the “4th Large Transport of the Elderly” (I/90), 17 March 1943, reference 15510042, FIFTY-ONE DOCUMENTS and 1,200 listed people. HIS WIFE GERTRUD SARA LEIBHOLZ NÉE LEIBKE, born Berlin 13 July 1894, IS NOT ON THAT PAGE, and Oskar's line carries no “Ehepaar” bracket although the same sheet uses one for other couples. That is suggestive and it is not an answer — she could be on any of the other fifty sheets. She has FOUR Arolsen person records of her own, mirroring Oskar's four, so the index knows where she is; the work is to open them and see which series they sit in. This matters because the site currently gives her death as 27 February 1943 in Berlin, which is BEFORE the 17 March transport — so if she is on the list, something has to give. *** ANSWERED THE SAME DAY IT WAS WRITTEN, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. *** DocID 12663551, in 1.2.4 Various Organizations, is a KULTUSVEREINIGUNG BERLIN ZÄHLKARTE for Gertrud: "Leibholz geb. Leibke · Gertrud · 13.7.94, Berlin · verh." and, in the column headed ZIELLAND — country of destination — "VERSTORBEN 27/2.43". Household address MARBURGERSTR. 13, written Berlin 8 March 1943, stamped Kataster-Verwaltung, serial 015881, with an ITS stamp "CARDED ON 6 OCT 1947" and a pencilled cross-reference to T/D 52.972 on the back. SHE DIED EIGHTEEN DAYS BEFORE THE TRANSPORT LEFT, so she cannot be on any page of it, and Oskar's line carries no "Ehepaar" bracket because by then there was no pair. IT ALSO DOCUMENTS A DATE THE SITE HAD ONLY FROM THE GEDENKBUCH — a compilation — and puts it on a contemporary card written nine days later by the office that knew her. THE FORM IS AN EMIGRATION CARD WITH "EMIGRATING" CROSSED OUT AND A DEATH WRITTEN INTO THE BOX FOR THE COUNTRY SHE WAS GOING TO. No cause of death is on it and none is inferred here, although 27 February 1943 in Berlin was the day of the Fabrikaktion. The other fifty sheets of the transport list stay unread and there is no longer a reason to read them for her.

rows.what: The address column on the Leibholz registration card is untranscribed Kurrent
rows.note: DocID 11214358, image 001. The right-hand “Wohnungen” column carries a dated run of Berlin addresses from the 1910s onward — the household's whole moving history on one card, and the thing the Berlin directories can only sample at one household per year. IT HAS NOT BEEN READ. The scan is a grey microfilm frame 976 pixels wide and the hand is Kurrent; enlargement recovers the dates and not the street names. Two routes: ask the Arolsen Archives whether a better scan exists, or put the crop in front of somebody who reads Kurrent. Recorded as unfinished rather than as read — see data/leibholz-registration-card.tsv. *** TRIED PROPERLY ON 20 SEPTEMBER AND IT IS BLOCKED ON THE IMAGE, NOT ON THE EFFORT. *** Two processing passes were run on the crop: median-filtered denoise with five-times LANCZOS upscaling and light contrast, and a seven-times pass with an unsharp mask. THE SHARPENING AMPLIFIES THE FILM GRAIN INTO THE HAND and destroys it; the gentle pass leaves words that can be guessed at and not read. *** AND THERE IS ONLY ONE SCAN TO WORK FROM. *** Six URL variants were tested against collections-server.arolsen-archives.org — the H, V and L partitions, a _big suffix and a .tif — and every alternative returns 404. The 976-pixel frame is all the server has. WHAT WAS RECOVERED, AND IT IS ONLY THIS: the column carries a dated run BEGINNING IN 1913 — entries reading 18.13, 19.13, 21.13 and 23/4.15 — and the latest annotation on the card is Auguste's 18.1.44. THE STREET NAMES ARE NOT READABLE AND NONE IS PUBLISHED. TWO ROUTES REMAIN AND NEITHER IS THIS ARCHIVE'S TO TAKE ALONE. (1) ASK THE AROLSEN ARCHIVES whether a higher-resolution scan of DocID 11214358 exists — they hold the film, the web copy is a derivative, and they answer written requests. (2) PUT THE CROP IN FRONT OF SOMEBODY WHO READS KURRENT. Re-owned to David-or-Arolsen and marked blocked rather than next, because nothing further can be done from this end.

rows.what: GERTRUD MEYER NÉE LEIBHOLZ, born 09.03.1899 — a sister nobody has
rows.note: Found in the 43-topic Leibholz sweep: “Tracing and documentation case no. 161.094 for MEYER, GERTRUD born 09.03.1899”, indexed under the MAIDEN NAME LEIBHOLZ. The Schubin siblings this archive has are Samuel 1877, Georg 1884, Jacob 1884 and Oskar 1887. A Leibholz daughter born 1899 would fit the same family and there is no sister in the tree at all. THE CASE IS IN THE RESTRICTED T/D REPOSITORY, so the lead is an index entry and a married surname. The reachable test is her person records and the Berlin directories under MEYER — and the Schubin civil registers, which is the same Bydgoszcz thread as request 30. *** TESTED AND KILLED THE SAME DAY. *** Her second person record gives a PLACE OF BIRTH and it is GLOWITZ — Główczyce in Pomerania, KREIS STOLP. STOLP IS WHERE WILLI LEIBHOLZ WAS BORN, on the 1946 Jewish Agency questionnaire read earlier the same day. She is a Pomeranian Leibholz, not a Schubin one, and she is not Jacob's sister. THE NEGATIVE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE HYPOTHESIS WAS: the two Leibholz families are now separable by place — Schubin in Posen against Stolp in Pomerania — and that is the only thing that will ever separate them. Her fate is on the record too: DocID 127212709, "Wave 48 — 34th OSTTRANSPORT TO CC AUSCHWITZ, 4 MARCH 1943", thirteen days before Oskar's Alterstransport to Theresienstadt and a different kind of list altogether. Struck rather than done, because the row asked a question whose premise turned out to be wrong.

rows.what: Three names inside the Levetzowstraße tracing run that the 1939 census does not have
rows.note: T/D cases 90.465 to 90.474 are one enquiry about one household: ALFRED 04.12.1887, ELSE 20.07.1889, MARIANNE 26.04.1921, LISELOTTE and KURT match Mapping the Lives at Levetzowstraße 13 to the day. HANS (90.465), GERHARD (90.466) and WALTER (90.473) sit in the same run and are NOT in the census record for that flat. Older children already out of the house, or relatives named in the same enquiry — not asserted either way. Also here: T/D 90.474 IS NOT DERRICK'S FATHER. It is Alfred's son Kurt, born 04.11.1927, and the note is written down so a later reader does not repeat the mistake. NOT ON THE CRITICAL PATH — this is the Levetzowstraße family, not Schubin — but it is the largest single Leibholz household in the archive and it is one search away. *** DONE 20 SEPTEMBER, BY SEARCHING THE 1939 CENSUS DATABASE ON STREET AND HOUSE NUMBER INSTEAD OF ON NAME — AND ONE OF THE THREE WAS THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN MISS. *** LEVETZOWSTRASSE 13 HOLDS SIX LEIBHOLZ, NOT FIVE: Alfred 04.12.1887 † 08.08.1942 · Else née Seelig 20.07.1889 † 17-19.08.1943 · Marianne 26.04.1921 · *** WALTER 20.09.1922 † before 08.05.1945 *** · Lieselotte 16.11.1923 † 06.12.1943 · Kurt 04.11.1927 † before 08.05.1945. T/D 90.473 WALTER is the fourth child and data/mappingthelives-leibholz.tsv simply did not list him; that file now carries the correction. HANS (90.465) AND GERHARD (90.466) ARE NOT AT THAT ADDRESS. The only Gerhard in the database is Dr Uri Gerhard Leibholz, born 15.11.1901, who DIED AT GÖTTINGEN IN 1982 — a survivor, and on the public record the constitutional lawyer. *** AND THE ONLY HANS TURNED OUT TO BE WORTH THE WHOLE ROW. *** HANS LEIBHOLZ, born 25.01.1912 IN PREUSSISCH FRIEDLAND / SCHLOCHAU / POMMERN, "Race" JJJJ, at DANCKELMANNSTRASSE 44 CHARLOTTENBURG on census night, DEPORTED 12 JANUARY 1943 AND DEAD AT AUSCHWITZ ON 22 FEBRUARY 1943. That is the "Hans Israel Leibholz born 1912 at Preussisch Friedland" the Yad Vashem sweep found and could not place. His flat holds three more: his mother ELSE née ROTHENBERG b.23.10.1884 IN SCHLOCHAU (no death recorded), his sister LISELOTT b.22.10.1920 in Preussisch Friedland † Auschwitz, and LAURA née ROTHENBERG b.23.09.1884 — a second Rothenberg woman of 1884 at the same address. The T/D run 8.891/8.892/8.893 is this flat, with two crossovers recorded rather than tidied. *** AND IT IS THE FIRST BERLIN LEIBHOLZ HOUSEHOLD FROM OUR OWN KREIS. *** Schlochau and Preussisch Friedland are KREIS SCHLOCHAU, and so is HAMMERSTEIN, where SALLY LEIBHOLZ was born on 7 July 1847. Every other household placed so far is Schubin, Stolp or Berlin. A KREIS IS NOT A FAMILY and this is not claimed as kinship — what it does is say where to look, and the answer is the Hammerstein and Preussisch Friedland civil registers, which are the same Bydgoszcz-region books as the Szubin letter. IT ALSO NAMES A STOLPERSTEIN: the Danckelmannstraße 44 stone, listed here for a week as belonging to "other Leibholz families", commemorates this household.

rows.what: SOPHIE LEIBHOLZ OF SHANGHAI — find her husband, and read the Relico collection
rows.note: FOUND 20 SEPTEMBER: the first Leibholz survivor this archive has a name for. She filled in three Relico questionnaires in SHANGHAI in 1946 — for her brother SALLY BINDER, his wife MATHILDE, and her brother-in-law HEINRICH LEIBHOLZ. Sister to a Binder and sister-in-law to a Leibholz makes her SOPHIE NÉE BINDER, married to a brother of Heinrich. *** HER HUSBAND'S FORENAME IS ON NONE OF THE THREE FORMS. *** THREE THINGS TO DO. (1) The Berlin directory: Heinrich Leibholz is at HORNSTRASSE 19 on her form and at Neukölln, Leinestrasse 32 in the 1938-42 volumes — two addresses for one man, and the volumes will name his brothers as householders. (2) The RELICO COLLECTION ITSELF, "Questionnaires used for the search for relatives by Relico, the World Jewish Congress Relief Committee in Geneva, completed by survivors in Shanghai, 1946" — a source this archive has never used, and one that by definition records people who were ALIVE. Search it for LUWINSKI as well as LEIBHOLZ. (3) The Shanghai ghetto emigrant lists, which are held at Arolsen. THE BOUND, STATED FIRST: NOTHING TIES SOPHIE OR HEINRICH TO KURT'S FAMILY. Heinrich was born in Berlin in 1890, not at Schubin. This is a lead about a Berlin Leibholz family, and it is the first one with a living person in it. *** ANSWERED THE SAME DAY, AND THE HUSBAND HAS A NAME. *** Mapping the Lives has an EMIGRATION PLACE field. Surname LEIBHOLZ with emigration place SHANGHAI returns two people: Charlotte Abrahamsohn née Leibholz b.18.09.1889, and *** ALBERT LEIBHOLZ, BORN 17.05.1886 *** — who is the "Albert, Antiquitäten, Halensee" of the 1938 Berliner Adressbuch. Arolsen then gives him twice over. (1) DocID 131698324, a CENTRAL LOCATION INDEX card, index no. L 337909: "LEIBHOLZ · ALBERT · died 8.18.44 · 5.17.86 · Berlin · German · J · dealer · last known address SHANGHAI, 12.14.45", and under OTHER MEMBERS OF THE FAMILY ABROAD: "SOPHIE · REL. TO NO. 1: W · 6.19.87 · BERLIN". *** W IS WIFE. SOPHIE LEIBHOLZ NÉE BINDER WAS BORN AT BERLIN ON 19 JUNE 1887 AND SHE WAS ALBERT'S WIFE. *** The card also gives the journey — "arr. 6.27.39 from Berlin" — and a third person looking for them: CURT STERNGAST, c/o Silman, Rambam Str. 39, Rehavia, JERUSALEM. (2) DocID 78827389, the H.I.A.S. "lists concerning Jewish nationals who died and were buried in SHANGHAI during 1939-1948", page 24: "LEIBHOLZ, ALBERT · 5/17/86 · 8/18/44 · PARALISIS PROGRESSITIS", file L-142. SO: Berlin antiques dealer, out on 27 June 1939, dead in Shanghai on 18 August 1944, his widow still there in December 1945 and filling in relief forms in 1946. AND IT SEPARATES THE TWO SOPHIES FOR GOOD — née BINDER born Berlin 19 June 1887 and alive, against née ROTHENBERG born Schlochau 9 January 1887 and murdered. STILL AN INFERENCE AND THE ONLY ONE LEFT: that Heinrich is Albert's brother. Sophie called him her brother-in-law and she married a Leibholz; nothing yet says the two men were brothers rather than cousins. In data/leibholz-shanghai.tsv. A clean negative came with it: LUWINSKI returns nothing at Yad Vashem, victim or submitter, against a control of 66 for LEIBHOLZ.

rows.what: STRUCK — THE HAMMERSTEIN REGISTERS WERE ASKED FOR ON 14 SEPTEMBER AND ANSWERED ON THE 16th
rows.note: WRITTEN 20 SEPTEMBER OUT OF ROW 200, AND IT SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN. The row proposed writing to Poland for the Hammerstein registers — Sally Leibholz's birth of 7 July 1847, and Georg's of 7 June 1884 — and said to check first which archive branch holds Człuchów. *** IT WAS CHECKED, AND ASKED, AND ANSWERED, SIX DAYS EARLIER. *** A letter went to Archiwum Państwowe w Koszalinie on 14 SEPTEMBER, thread 1a0a1a01f08ce480, asking for exactly those two records and the synagogue books. It was ANSWERED ON 16 SEPTEMBER, reference O-S.6342.406.2026, signed by Krzysztof Skrzypiec, Head of the Słupsk Branch: the holdings contain NO registers of Standesamt Hammerstein FOR 1874 TO 1899 and NO SYNAGOGUE-COMMUNITY BOOKS FOR CZARNE AT ALL, and no information about what became of either. It was acknowledged on 17 September as requests/28-SEND-THIS-to-koszalin.txt. All of that is in site/src/data/letters.json and in row 88. *** WHAT TODAY'S WORK ADDS IS ONE LINE OF CORROBORATION AND NOTHING ELSE. *** The public finding aid says the same thing independently: szukajwarchiwach holds fond 27/364/0, "Standesamt Hammerstein [Czarne]", at ARCHIWUM PAŃSTWOWE W KOSZALINIE ODDZIAŁ W SŁUPSKU, 127 units all digitised — and its own date facet reads 1900+ : 128, 1800-1899 : 0. A search for "Synagogengemeinde Hammerstein" returns nothing, against a control of 127 for "Standesamt Hammerstein". So the branch's written negative is confirmed by its own catalogue, which is worth having and is not worth a row. FamilySearch was checked too and has filmed Jüdische Gemeinde Matrikel for Stuhm, Flatow, Marienwerder, Rosenberg, Marienburg and Frauenburg — AND NOT FOR HAMMERSTEIN. *** THE CAUSE, BECAUSE IT IS THE SIXTH TIME TODAY. *** The row was written off the back of a finding without reading letters.json or the requests directory. The finding was real; the action proposed for it was already closed. THE CHEAPEST ROUTE TO THE GENERATION ABOVE SALLY IS UNCHANGED AND IS ALREADY DRAFTED: the SZUBIN MARRIAGE OF 24 NOVEMBER 1874, which names the parents of both spouses, in requests/30-SEND-THIS-to-bydgoszcz.txt, unsent.

rows.what: TREUCHTLINGER STRASSE 4 — Spier named, the house dated, and the move bounded at both ends
rows.note: NEW 20 SEPTEMBER, out of the transport list. Jacob Leibholz is on the 30th Osttransport of 26 February 1943 at TREUCHTLINGERSTR. 4, Berlin-Schöneberg, and the AJDC card adds "b/SPIER" — lodging with a family called Spier. THE 1939 CENSUS HAS HIM AT MERANER STRASSE 2 WITH AUGUSTE AND SIEGFRIED. Something happened in between and this archive does not know what. THREE THINGS ARE REACHABLE WITHOUT ANYBODY'S HELP. (1) MAPPING THE LIVES BY ADDRESS — the method that found the Danckelmannstraße household. Search street TREUCHTLINGERSTR, number 4, and the whole flat comes back, SPIER INCLUDED. (2) THE BERLINER ADRESSBUCH for Treuchtlingerstraße 4, 1939 to 1943, which gives the householder — and if the householder is Spier, that settles whose flat it was. (3) The same two questions for AUGUSTE: her registration card carries an annotation dated 18.1.44 giving a street and a number that has not been read, so where she went after he was taken is also on a document. WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: it does not change a date or a name in the register. It is the last stretch of Jacob's life and it is the only part of it that is still blank. *** PARTS 1 AND 2 DONE WITHIN THE HOUR, AND PART 1 ANSWERED MORE THAN IT ASKED. *** TREUCHTLINGER STRASSE 4 ON CENSUS NIGHT HELD SEVENTEEN PERSECUTED PEOPLE FROM ELEVEN FAMILY NAMES — Brück, Cohn, Eisenberg, Eisenberger, Kaphan, Kochanowska, Löwenheim, Podbielski, Rosenstock, Sundheimer and SPIER. The Spiers are named: MAX b.12.04.1864 † 26 MARCH 1941, HANS b.02.12.1894, ALICE née WOLLSTEIN b.03.11.1899, the last two dead before 8 May 1945. The "b/Spier" on Jacob's card is a household with three names in it, and by the time he was lodging there the eldest was already dead. Eleven surnames at one address in May 1939 is not an ordinary apartment block; Jacob was moved into a house that was already full. He is not in the 1939 list for it because that night he was still at Meraner Straße 2. *** AND THE SAME SEARCH ON MERANER STRASSE 2 SOLVED SOMETHING ELSE. *** Fourteen people at that address, and one of them is ANNA PUFF, BORN 1 JUNE 1895 — who is one of the eleven names indexed on DocID 11214358, the Leibholz registration card. SO THE SECOND IMAGE OF THAT DocID IS THE HOUSE LIST FOR MERANER STRASSE 2, which is exactly what the stamp on the first image says: "Lt. Hausliste 1945 n. erfaßt". One exact match out of seven unplaced names, and the other six would not be in a database of persecuted people if they were not Jewish — a strong reading, not a proof, and recorded as such. It also gives Kurt's name on that sheet a reason: an absent son written against his parents' flat. THIRD ACCOUNT THIS ARCHIVE HAS GIVEN OF THAT DocID, offered as the best one and flagged as the third. PART 3 REMAINS: Auguste's 18.1.44 annotation is in the same unreadable Kurrent as the address column, so it is blocked with row 198. || 21 SEPTEMBER, AND MOST OF IT IS ANSWERED. The 1941 volume, Teil IV printed page 1615, gives the house: owner *** EISENBERG, G. SARA, WW. *** — a widow carrying the compulsory Sara — with tenants including STEPHAN, H. ISRAEL, ROSENSTOCK, L., and *** SPIER, H., HANDELSVERTRETER. *** THAT IS THE SPIER OF THE TRANSPORT LINE: Jacob's deportation address reads "Treuchtlingerstr. 4 b/Spier", bei Spier, and here is Spier in the building two years earlier, with a trade. A Jewish-owned house filling with Jewish tenants in 1940 is what a Judenhaus was, and the directory shows it without using the word. *** AND JACOB IS NOT IN THE 1941 ENTRY *** — that volume was compiled in the autumn of 1940, so he had not been moved there yet. THE WINDOW IS NOW BOUNDED AT BOTH ENDS: Meraner Straße 2 on the census of 17 May 1939, absent from Treuchtlinger in autumn 1940, at Treuchtlinger 4 b/Spier on 26 February 1943. WHAT IS LEFT is the 1942 and 1943 volumes, and the OCR will not give up those two pages — a fuzzy street search returns only cross-references from neighbouring streets and a combined EISENBERG + SPIER search returns nothing in either volume. They must be found by eye. *** PUT TO THE BERLIN DIRECTORIES 22 SEPTEMBER AND NOT FOUND. *** “Spier” AND “Treuchtlinger” returns 3 pages and on none of them is a Spier AT that address: the Spiers are a Konfitüren-Geschäft in W 30, a Fritz Spier of Schöneberg, and a Friedrich and Liselotte Spier of Dianastraße. THE CO-OCCURRENCE IS PAGE-LEVEL, NOT ADDRESS-LEVEL — the same trap as the two Lutherstraßen. The Spier household Jacob lodged with is not reachable by full text and needs the street section read at the image.

rows.what: GENETEKA IS ANSWERED AND IT IS STRUCTURALLY EMPTY FOR THIS FAMILY
rows.note: OPENED AND CLOSED IN ONE SITTING, 20 September. Geneteka was searched earlier the same day, returned nothing for LEIBHOLZ, and the KOWALSKI control ALSO returned nothing — so the negative was correctly withheld and the row left hanging. *** THE CAUSE IS ONE CHARACTER. *** Geneteka's province codes are positional: 01ds dolnośląskie, 02kp KUJAWSKO-POMORSKIE, 03lb lubelskie, 04ls LUBUSKIE. The query used w=04kp, which is not a code at all, so the select fell back silently to dolnośląskie. A SECOND TRAP IN THE SAME SITE: the results table is filled by AJAX, so a plain fetch of the search URL returns the page shell with an EMPTY TABLE that reads exactly like a zero. The rows exist only in a rendered browser. WITH THE CODE FIXED THE CONTROL PASSES and the answers are: LEIBHOLZ zero in kujawsko-pomorskie and zero in wielkopolskie, births and marriages. SCHMUL eighteen marriages in wielkopolskie, all fuzzy variants, NONE AT SZUBIN. *** AND THE STRUCTURAL REASON, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL ANSWER: *** Szubin IS in Geneteka — parish 13066, from 1715 — but it is THE CATHOLIC PARISH. Geneteka marks Jewish registers "(mojż.)" and KUJAWSKO-POMORSKIE HAS NO (mojż.) PARISH AT ALL, across all 358 entries in its list. A Jewish or civil marriage at Szubin in 1874 cannot be in this index however it is searched. STRUCK RATHER THAN DONE: the route was never going to work, and the only route to the 1874 marriage remains requests/30-SEND-THIS-to-bydgoszcz.txt, drafted and unsent. In data/schmul-and-thimm.tsv.

rows.what: THE SZUBIN 1874 MARRIAGE FILM — found, filmed, online, AND RESTRICTED TO A FAMILYSEARCH CENTRE
rows.note: FOUND 20 SEPTEMBER, after Geneteka was proved structurally incapable of holding Jewish Szubin records. *** THE 1874 CIVIL REGISTERS OF SZUBIN ARE FILMED AND THE FILM IS ONLINE. *** Archiwum Państwowe w Bydgoszczy holds them in three fonds — 6/1792/0 SZUBIN MIASTO 1874-1935 with marriages from 1874 AND SKOROWIDZE (alphabetical indexes) FOR 1874-1878, 6/1795/0 Wieś I and 6/1796/0 Wieś II. FamilySearch filmed them from Bydgoszcz: catalogue koha:402152, Standesamt I, film note "Geburten, Heiraten, Tote 1874-1876", *** DIGITAL FILM 007998644, 1,121 IMAGES ***; and koha:402191, Standesamt II, 1874-1875, *** DIGITAL FILM 008016003, 1,160 IMAGES ***. BOTH OPEN IN THE VIEWER WITH NO RESTRICTION. NEITHER IS IN THE FULL-TEXT INDEX — /service/search/fulltext/search/groupNumber returns an empty id list for both — so they cannot be searched by surname and must be browsed. WHY IT IS TRACTABLE: Prussian civil registration began on 1 OCTOBER 1874, so the 1874 volumes cover THREE MONTHS. The marriage book should hold a few dozen entries and the skorowidz a single page. The target is SALLY (SALI, SALOMON) LEIBHOLZ and FRIEDERIKE SCHMUL, 24 NOVEMBER 1874. WHICH STANDESAMT IS NOT SETTLED: the town is the likelier, but Standesamt I's catalogue title says 1875-1876 while its own film note says 1874-1876 — the title and the film disagree and the film is what was photographed. BOTH must be checked. *** AND IT CHANGES REQUEST 30, WHICH HAS BEEN UPDATED. *** The letter now cites the three fond references so Bydgoszcz does not have to find them. If the browse succeeds the letter is only needed for a certified copy, if at all. In data/szubin-civil-registers.tsv. *** WITHDRAWN WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE ERROR IS MINE. *** This row first said "BOTH OPEN IN THE VIEWER WITH NO RESTRICTION". THEY DO NOT. The claim came from the viewer reporting a page count and NOT FROM LOOKING AT THE PAGE. With the browser pane displayed, EVERY THUMBNAIL IN THE FILMSTRIP CARRIES A PADLOCK, and opening one returns FamilySearch's own notice: "IMAGE RESTRICTED. Image access is typically determined by local laws or the custodian who has the original document. To view these images do one of the following: ACCESS THE SITE AT A FAMILYSEARCH CENTER." *** THE LESSON IS GENERAL: AN IMAGE COUNT IS NOT AN IMAGE. *** FamilySearch serves a film's length to everybody, restricted or not; the padlocks exist only in the rendered page. Availability cannot be read from metadata. WHAT SURVIVES: the registers exist, they are at AP Bydgoszcz in three named fonds, the town fond has SKOROWIDZE FOR 1874-1878, and the films are 007998644 and 008016003. Only the viewing is blocked, and by the CUSTODIAN rather than by FamilySearch. *** AND IT GIVES DAVID A FREE ROUTE THIS ARCHIVE CANNOT TAKE. *** The restriction lifts inside a FAMILYSEARCH CENTRE OR AFFILIATE LIBRARY, of which there are several in Brisbane, and access is free. Film 007998644, the 1874 skorowidz, the marriage of SALLY (SALI, SALOMON) LEIBHOLZ and FRIEDERIKE SCHMUL on 24 NOVEMBER 1874 — an afternoon at a terminal. Re-owned to David and marked blocked. REQUEST 30 TO BYDGOSZCZ IS THEREFORE NECESSARY AFTER ALL, and it is a better letter for citing the three fond references. *** AND THE POLISH SIDE WAS CHECKED TOO, SO THE PICTURE IS COMPLETE. *** Film 008016003, Standesamt II, IS PADLOCKED AS WELL — the restriction is on the Szubin material, not on one reel. And SZUKAJWARCHIWACH HAS NO SCANS OF IT EITHER: the portal returns the three USC Szubin fonds AT FOND LEVEL ONLY, with no unit rows, no inventory and no scan counts, across four differently-worded searches. THE CONTROL THAT MAKES THAT A FINDING: the same search box returns 127 UNIT-LEVEL ROWS WITH "Number of scans" for "Standesamt Hammerstein" at Koszalin/Słupsk. The portal does show units and scans when they exist; it has neither for Szubin. SO: THE REGISTERS EXIST AND NOBODY CAN SEE THEM FROM A DESK. Two routes remain and both need a person — a free terminal inside a FamilySearch Centre in Brisbane, or the letter to Bydgoszcz.
