rows.what: JOSEPH LUWENSKI OF ALLENSTEIN, 1874 — the first record the Polish block has ever touched
rows.note: FOUND 20 SEPTEMBER in the Geneteka spelling sweep David asked for. Standesamt OLSZTYN-ALLENSTEIN, birth entry no. 11 of 1874: *** MARTHA LUWENSKI, FATHER JOSEPH, MOTHER ELISABETH BILITEWSKI. *** Entry eleven of a registry that opened on 1 October 1874. JOACHIM LUWINSKI WAS BORN AT ALLENSTEIN ON 21 OCTOBER 1865. A Joseph of this surname registering a daughter in that town in 1874 is the right place, the right registry and the right generation to be HIS FATHER OR HIS ELDER BROTHER — and the family tree already holds a JOSEPH LUWINSKI with no dates and no place, inside the hundred-name Polish block this archive has always called a surname index rather than a descent. NOT PROVED AND NOT ASSERTED. What makes it worth a row is that it is the FIRST TIME that block has touched an actual record. WHAT TO DO: the Allenstein Standesamt registers are at ARCHIWUM PAŃSTWOWE W OLSZTYNIE. Birth no. 11 of 1874 would name Joseph's age, trade and residence; and if Joachim's own birth of 21 October 1865 is in the Catholic register of Allenstein before civil registration, it would name his parents outright. Also search BILITEWSKI, which is a rarer name than Luwinski and may carry the family further. AND ONE MORE GENETEKA PASS IS OWED: only the surname was swept. The forenames JOACHIM and JOSEPH, and the maiden name BILITEWSKI, have not been.

rows.what: THREE LOWINSKI BIRTHS AT STANDESAMT RÖSSEL, 1876-1884 — Sauerbaum's own registry
rows.note: FOUND THE SAME WAY. RESZEL-RÖSSEL USC: 1876 no. 68 FRANZ LOWINSKI · 1881 no. 31 ALBERT LOWINSKI · 1884 no. 9 BERNHARD LOWINSKI. The Geneteka index does not carry their parents. *** KREIS RÖSSEL IS THE DISTRICT SAUERBAUM IS IN. *** Johanna Thimm was born there in 1871 and Auguste Luwinski in 1893. A household of this surname is registering children in that district from 1876, which is between those two dates. NOT KIN ON ANY EVIDENCE HELD. What it does is tell the Olsztyn archive exactly which three entries to pull, and those entries carry the father's name, age, trade and village — which would say at once whether this is Joachim's family or a different Lowinski.  NOTE THE SPELLING: the same registry spells one woman LOWINSKI in four years and LUWINSKI in two. The forms are not different families and must not be treated as such.

rows.what: NAA: A2559, 1965/86/85-88 — the Australian half of the 1965 emigration roll
rows.note: NINE FOLIOS, CANBERRA, PAPER, NOT DIGITISED, access status "not yet examined". This is the same nominal roll Arolsen holds: BGO 65/135 lines 85 to 88 against the NAA control symbol 1965/86/85-88. IT ALREADY CORRECTED THIS ARCHIVE ONCE — its title says the family came by SHIP, the FLAVIA, ex Bremerhaven, arriving 17 September 1965, and this archive had published that they flew. *** THE FREE MOVE FIRST: *** an ACCESS EXAMINATION request to the National Archives of Australia costs nothing and is made by email. It does not produce a scan, but it opens the item and it is the step that has to happen before any copy can be ordered. Ask for examination of item ID 5435314, and at the same time for A714 18/8913, A435 1944/4/1672 and A1478 EPCP63.

rows.what: JOACHIM PETER LEIBHOLZ of Melbourne — died Toorak 1971, and the index names his parents
rows.note: SIX NAA FILES, none scanned. Born Berlin 20 August 1903; landed Melbourne per ANCHISES 12 June 1939 with Tilde (or Hilde) and a child; naturalised 27 July 1944 at South Yarra, Victoria, PREVIOUS NATIONALITY STATELESS. *** AND ONE OF HIS FILES IS ABOUT PROPERTY INSIDE POLAND: *** A1478 EPCP63, "German property taken over by the Polish Government - Leibholz J P Mr", 1947, with a claim following at A1458 EPCH18 and German currency bonds at A1444 EPC164 — the last of those filed under the spelling LAIBHOLZ. OUR LEIBHOLZES ARE FROM SCHUBIN IN POSEN. This is the first document ever found that puts a Leibholz, a Berliner and Polish property in one sentence. NOT KIN ON ANY EVIDENCE HELD, and kept as its own lane. The cheap test is the Victorian death index and the Melbourne Chevra Kadisha, both of which would give his parents. || DONE 21 SEPTEMBER, on the free Victorian historical index. *** REG. 26252/1971: "LEIBHOLZ, Joachim Peter, Death, mother NANETTE, mother's family name at birth NETTER, father LEIBHOLZ WILLIAM, place of birth BERLIN GERMANY, place of death TOORAK, age at death 68." *** He stayed: landed 1939, naturalised at South Yarra 1944, died thirty-two years later two suburbs away, aged 68 and consistent to the year with a birth on 20 August 1903. AND THE ARCHIVE HAS ALREADY MET A WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ OF BERLIN — the 1920 directory has "WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ, GENERALDIREKTOR and STADTRAT", and the 1913 name section has "William, Kaufm., W15 Kurfürstendamm 169", the only William on that roll. STRONG, NOT PROOF; the Victorian death certificate carries the parents in full and is the thing that would settle it. IT DOES NOT CONNECT HIM TO THIS FAMILY — ours are Konfektion merchants from Schubin and William is a managing director on the Kurfürstendamm. The Melbourne lane stays a lane. THE SWEEP WAS DONE PROPERLY: the index takes a wildcard, so L*HOLZ was run across births, deaths and marriages 1900-1995 and returns exactly this one record — with the honest limit that Victorian birth indexes close about 1922 and marriages about 1942, so the child off the Anchises could not appear whatever happened.

rows.what: THE LOWINSKYS OF SOUTH AFRICA — a second family of the name, in print eleven years before Kurt landed
rows.note: FOUND BY RUNNING LOWINSKI, WHICH HAD NEVER BEEN RUN. Eight documents in the South African Government Gazette: THOS. H. LOWINSKY 1922 · LOWINSKY, M. 1939 · MARK LOWINSKY 1944 and 1961 · RUPERT ESMOND LOWINSKY, retired, of Riebeek, District Maclear, deceased estate 671/55 with a first and final account advertised 30 September 1955 · 3747/84/3A in 1985. *** NOT OURS, AND THE REASON IS A DATE: *** Thos. H. Lowinsky is in print in 1922 and Kurt Luwinski did not reach South Africa until 1933. PARKED, NOT PURSUED. It is on the register of lines so that nobody rules it out a second time. If the two names ever have to be separated properly, estate 671/55 names his heirs.

rows.what: AUSTRALIAN ELECTORAL ROLLS 1965-1980 — blocked, and the reason is worth recording
rows.note: Item 8 of the twenty. THE ROLLS FOR THOSE YEARS ARE BEHIND A SUBSCRIPTION. FamilySearch's free Australian electoral rolls stop at 1949 and the family did not land until 1965; the 1903-1980 set is Ancestry's, and an Ancestry subscription is a purchase this archive does not make. NOT A NEGATIVE RESULT — an unopened instrument. The free substitutes are the NAA files at row 208, the Queensland death certificate, and Australian telephone directories at the State Library of Queensland.

rows.what: TROVE — attempted 20 September 2026 and the site refused this browser
rows.note: Item 6 of the twenty. The search application hung on "Loading...", and its own configuration endpoint then began answering "No API key found in request" to this client. NOT A RESULT EITHER WAY: nothing was searched, so nothing is ruled out. *** AND NOTE WHAT TROVE IS ACTUALLY FOR HERE: *** copyright closes Australian newspapers at 1954 and this family landed in 1965, so the newspapers cannot hold them. THE GAZETTES CAN — the Commonwealth of Australia Gazette runs on past 1954 and carried naturalisations. Retry, restricted to the Gazette category, across every spelling. || RETRIED 21 SEPTEMBER, A DAY LATER, AND IT IS THE SAME. The application loads, the search box takes text, Return and the submit button both register — and "Search results for:" stays blank and no search request is ever sent. REPRODUCIBLE ACROSS TWO DAYS AND TWO SESSIONS. *** THE HONEST BLOCKER, NAMED: *** Trove's own endpoints answer "No API key found in request" to this client, and a Trove API key is free but requires REGISTERING AN ACCOUNT, which this archive does not do on David's behalf. So this is not an instrument that is down; it is one that needs a key, and getting the key is David's to do in about two minutes. Everything else about item 6 stands: it is the Commonwealth Gazette that matters, not the newspapers, because copyright closes those at 1954 and this family landed in 1965. *** 22 SEPTEMBER — IT WORKED, AND IT CORRECTED THIS ROW. *** No fix, no workaround: the application simply rendered. The one obstacle was a CULTURAL ADVICE overlay, closed rather than permanently dismissed. *** AND THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG. *** It said Australian newspapers close at 1954 so only the gazettes could hold this family. THE CANBERRA TIMES IS DIGITISED 1926 TO 1995, and every Luwinski hit Trove returns is a Canberra Times article from after 1954. LUWINSKI returns NINE in Newspapers & Gazettes and nothing in the other categories. *** THE THREE PREVIEWED ARE ALL WITHHELD: *** they concern a Canberra household of the surname in the 1970s and 80s, one of them a court report, and at least one names a LIVING person this archive is instructed never to name. Nothing from them is published — not the names, not the address, not the substance. The remaining six were not opened, because the three that were read establish the set is about living people. The living-persons guard was run against the built site as a check on this archive: nine guarded names, none present.

rows.what: THE RYERSON INDEX — the only free instrument that reaches a 2012 Brisbane death
rows.note: A free index to DEATH, FUNERAL AND PROBATE NOTICES in Australian newspapers, running to the present, where the Queensland state index stops at 1996. MANFRED DIED AT BRISBANE ON 20 SEPTEMBER 2012 and a Courier-Mail funeral notice would NAME THE SURVIVORS. Attempted four times on 20 September 2026 and the server answered "Server Overloaded" every time. NOTHING WAS SEARCHED, SO NOTHING IS RULED OUT. Retry across all seven spellings, and separately for MARQUARDT and WAGNER, which are the surnames Helga carried. || RETRIED AGAIN 20 September, late: "Server Overloaded" for the eighth time. Not searched. || RETRIED 21 SEPTEMBER AND THE DIAGNOSIS IS SHARPER. The SEARCH PAGE NOW LOADS — the form, the fields, the notice that Ryerson is free. SUBMITTING IT RETURNS "Server Overloaded" EVERY TIME, on three attempts with pauses, and a further page load then failed the same way. So the site serves and the search backend does not, which is different from what was recorded yesterday and worth having: the block is on the query, not the host. It is an intermittent public service with no workaround available here. STILL THE ONLY FREE INSTRUMENT THAT REACHES A 2012 BRISBANE FUNERAL NOTICE. Left to the scheduled retry. *** 22 SEPTEMBER — FOUR MORE REFUSALS, AND THE FIRST REAL ANSWER. *** search.php returned “Server Overloaded” four more times, about fourteen across three days. NOTHING SEARCHED, NOTHING RULED OUT. BUT THE DIAGNOSIS IS NOW EXACT: THE REST OF THE SITE SERVES PERFECTLY — home page, coverage tables and per-newspaper detail pages all load. It is search.php ALONE that refuses, so this is a throttled endpoint and not a dead archive. *** AND THE COVERAGE QUESTION WAS SETTLED WITHOUT SEARCHING: *** BRISBANE COURIER MAIL is indexed from 28 August 1933 to the present, six days a week, 377,328 records, last updated 19 September 2026 — with DEATH NOTICES from 22 February 1943 (92,248) and FUNERAL NOTICES over the same span (247,302). Manfred died at Brisbane on 20 September 2012, in the middle of both. The instrument covers the newspaper, the year AND the notice type that names survivors. The only thing in the way is a search box that will not answer.

rows.what: QUEENSLAND DEATH CERTIFICATE FOR MANFRED — and the entitlement question that comes first
rows.note: A Queensland death certificate NAMES THE PARENTS, and Manfred's parents are what the family tree gets worst: it makes him the son of Alfred Luwinski of Przasnysz, who died at Sachsenhausen in 1942 and was a Polish Catholic farm labourer. *** BUT THE FREE HISTORICAL INDEX STOPS AT 1996 AND HE DIED IN 2012, *** so this is not an index search — it is an application for a recent record, and Queensland issues those only to people with a recognised entitlement. BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: is there one? Manfred is not proven kin to Kurt, so a family relationship may not exist to claim. The cheap alternative that needs no entitlement at all is the Ryerson Index at row 213 and the funeral notice it points to.

rows.what: MR H. MARQUARDT OF HACKETT, CANBERRA — a shortlist at last, and the best candidate is ruled out as a brother
rows.note: Item 10 of the twenty. The 1965 emigration roll forwards the family c/o Mr H. MARQUARDT at Hackett, ACT, and Manfred's wife was HELGA ERNA MARQUARDT: the sponsor is almost certainly her family, already out. A keyword sweep of the NAA for MARQUARDT, 1950 to 1966, returns 83 items and THIRTY-ONE WITH AN H FORENAME. *** THE BEST FIT IS HARRY WALTER MARQUARDT, born 22 MARCH 1934, German, out on the ANNA SALEN in March 1955 — A2478 MARQUARDT HW and A2571 MARQUARDT HARRY. *** AND THE SAME LINE RULES OUT THE OBVIOUS READING: Helga Erna was born 1 MAY 1934, forty days later. They cannot have the same mother, so brother and sister is precisely what this pair of dates forbids. Cousins or no relation are both still open. WHAT DECIDES IT IS AN ADDRESS — the A2478 selection document carries the sponsor's, and the electoral rolls would too if they were not behind a subscription. ALSO RECORDED: two other Helga Marquardts already in Australia before ours, one naturalising in South Australia in 1960 and one Lithuanian off the General Stuart Heintzelman in 1949. Neither is ours and both are the kind of near-match that swallows an afternoon. || 21 SEPTEMBER: RECLASSIFIED AS BLOCKED, BECAUSE IT IS NOT MINE TO FINISH. The shortlist is built and cannot be narrowed without an ADDRESS, and there are exactly two places an address lives: the A2478 selection document at the National Archives of Australia, which is in the access-examination letter and therefore David's to send; and the Australian electoral rolls for 1965-80, which are behind a subscription this archive does not buy. NOTHING FURTHER CAN BE DONE HERE. Leaving it as "next" for this archive would misdescribe who is holding it up.

rows.what: THE ENTSCHÄDIGUNGSAKTEN — they moved to the Landesarchiv on 1 May 2026 and nobody has asked
rows.note: Items 1, 2 and 3 of the twenty, and the plan had the addressee wrong: it put these files at the Landesarchiv in B Rep. 025. UNTIL THIS YEAR THEY WERE NOT AT AN ARCHIVE AT ALL — they belonged to the ENTSCHÄDIGUNGSBEHÖRDE, a department of LABO, a live authority. *** ON 1 MAY 2026 THE LANDESARCHIV BERLIN TOOK THE WHOLE OF IT: about 280,000 proceedings, FIFTEEN KILOMETRES OF PAPER, stem files and subsidiary files together. *** The question is four and a half months old. The archive's stated minimum to ask is the name and the LIFE DATES, and this archive has those for Kurt (11.05.1912 - 15.12.1968), Auguste (28.08.1893 - 22.06.1975) and Siegfried (05.08.1925). About four weeks from enquiry to reading, with a Schutzfristverkürzungsantrag likely. AND RELATIVES MAY HAVE TEN FILES A YEAR DIGITISED FREE — the letter states the relationship exactly as the records state it, that Derrick is Kurt's son on every document, and leaves the status to them, because this archive has published its own doubt about that paternity and will not claim round it. Drafted as a SUPPLEMENT to the 14 September thread, not a new letter.

rows.what: THE BUNDESZENTRALKARTEI — the prior question, asked nationally, for all four at once
rows.note: AN INSTRUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEVER HEARD OF, named on the Landesarchiv's own page: a NATIONAL card index of Bundesentschädigungsgesetz claims, held by the Bezirksregierung Düsseldorf at bzk@brd.nrw.de, with a Merkblatt at brd.nrw.de/document/20230201_1_15_BZK_Merkblatt_deutsch.pdf. *** WHY IT COMES BEFORE BERLIN: *** every western Bundesland ran its own compensation authority and § 185 BEG decided which was competent. Kurt left Berlin in 1933 and died in Johannesburg in 1968; Auguste died in Baden-Württemberg in 1975; Siegfried lived in Potsdam, on the other side of the wall. THREE PEOPLE, THREE POSSIBLE JURISDICTIONS, and a Berlin-only enquiry can return nothing while a file sits in Stuttgart. The BZK answers whether a claim was ever filed at all and where. One letter covers Kurt, Auguste, Siegfried and the heirs of Jacob.

rows.what: THE WIEDERGUTMACHUNGSÄMTER FILE ON JAQUES LEIBHOLZ & CO
rows.note: Item 3 of the twenty, and it rides on row 216 rather than needing its own letter yet. "JAQUES LEIBHOLZ & CO, KONFEKTION, W8 KRONENSTRASSE 59.60" is in the 1938 Berliner Adressbuch and gone from every volume after it. A liquidated Jewish firm generates a property file at the WIEDERGUTMACHUNGSÄMTER VON BERLIN naming the owners, the value, the purchaser who took it and THE POST-WAR CLAIMANTS — and the claimants are the surviving family, which is the single list this archive most wants. Asked as the second half of the Landesarchiv supplement. If they answer that it is a separate holding with its own procedure, it becomes its own letter.

rows.what: THE MARRIAGE OF JOACHIM LUWINSKI AND JOHANNA THIMM — the one line that would name his parents
rows.note: Item 17 of the twenty, and the reasoning is the Bydgoszcz reasoning. A MARRIAGE RECORD NAMES THE PARENTS OF BOTH PARTIES. Johanna's are known — Anton Thimm b. 16 July 1840 and Elisabeth b. 15 March 1845. JOACHIM'S ARE KNOWN TO NOBODY, and they are the oldest generation reachable on this side of the family. He was born at Allenstein 21 October 1865, she at Sauerbaum 25 March 1871, and their daughter Auguste at Sauerbaum on 28 August 1893 — so the marriage falls between about 1888 and 1893, at USC Biesowo or USC Reszel. The letter asks for that first and for the four indexed entries of rows 206 and 207 second. IT ALSO GETS THE PRE-1874 PROBLEM RIGHT: Prussian civil registration began on 1 October 1874, so the births of Joachim in 1865 and Johanna in 1871 are CHURCH records — St Jakobi Allenstein and the Catholic parish of Gross Bössau, whose register runs 1690 to 1897 and names Sauerbaum expressly — and the letter asks whether those books are at Olsztyn or at the Archiwum Archidiecezji Warmińskiej. Every spelling is listed for them: LUWINSKI, LUWINSKY, LOWINSKI, LOWINSKY, LUWENSKI, LUWWINSKY.

rows.what: KURT'S BIRTH ENTRY NUMBER — FOUND. Standesamt Berlin VIII, 1912, Nr. 963
rows.note: DONE, 20 September 2026. *** LUWINSKI · KURT MYSZISLAUS · 963 *** — the May block of the L section, page 75 of P Rep. 523 Nr. 1395, the name index to the birth register of STANDESAMT BERLIN VIII for 1912. Twenty-one candidate volumes became one: Schöneberg was excluded by reading its whole 1912 L section (entries 14 to 1119, no Luwinski), the 1913 directory gave Chodowieckistraße 32, and the Berliner Adressbuch's own street index — whose first column is headed STANDESAMT — gives houses 23 to 32 as office 8. FOUR THINGS AGREE: the surname, the forename, the month, and a district arrived at independently. AND THE ARITHMETIC CHECKS — entry 963 of a register that passes 2561 by December is 37.6 per cent through it, and 11 May is 36 per cent through the year. Every L page of 1912 was read: exactly one Luwinski in the whole year. A second forename nobody has ever seen: MYSZISLAUS, a German clerk's spelling of Mieczysław.

rows.what: THE 1924 MARRIAGE ENTRY — FOUND. Standesamt Schöneberg II, Nr. 6 — and the index records the Mischehe
rows.note: DONE, 20 September 2026. *** "LEIBHOLZ · mos. · verheiratet mit LUWINSKI · kath. · Nr. 6" *** and the same entry again under her name, on page 221 of P Rep. 161 Nr. 271, the marriage index of STANDESAMT SCHÖNEBERG II. The family tree gives the wedding as 5 January 1924; a register restarts at 1 each January and the entries above are 1, 2 and 4, SO THE SIXTH MARRIAGE OF THE YEAR IS A MARRIAGE IN THE FIRST WEEK OF IT — date and number agree without either being derived from the other. *** AND THE CLERK WROTE THE RELIGIONS: *** Jacob mos., Auguste kath. Her Catholicism had been inferred from the Ermland, from Sauerbaum and from a census card; here a registrar writes it at her own wedding, in the same line as her husband's Judaism. FOUND BY ELIMINATION: Berlin VIII's January 1924 L block (P Rep. 523 Nr. 1054 p.34) and Schöneberg I's opening 1924 L block (P Rep. 160 Nr. 1036 p.210) were read first and hold neither name. AND IT DATES THE MOVE: they were in eastern Schöneberg by January 1924, nineteen months earlier than any document previously showed.

rows.what: THE DOUBLE-ENCODING TRAP AT THE LANDESARCHIV, recorded as method
rows.note: A finding that was about to be published and was false. Three queries for Schöneberg returned nothing and a sweep of all 142 offices put Schöneberg, Neukölln, Köpenick and Weißensee in the empty column. *** EVERY OFFICE NAME WITH AN UMLAUT RETURNED ZERO AND EVERY NAME WITHOUT ONE RETURNED ROWS. *** The site's database stores the names DOUBLE-ENCODED — the stored string is literally "Standesamt KÃ¶penick" — and the match is on the whole string, so the CORRECT spelling finds nothing and the MANGLED one finds seventeen volumes. Schöneberg has more online than almost anywhere: births 1874-1913 and deaths year by year to 1994. WHAT CAUGHT IT was not cleverness but noticing that all four failures shared a property and none of the successes did. Kept as a standing check: when a set of negatives has a common character, suspect the character before believing the negatives.

rows.what: CHODOWIECKISTRASSE 32 AND 31 IN 1912 AND 1914 — a one-year tenancy in a brand-new house
rows.note: DONE. Both volumes found by mapping each year's Teil III pagination onto its image numbers rather than by searching for the name, which is what the row said would be needed. *** 1912: NUMBER 32 IS A NEUBAU *** — "32 Neubau. E. Berl. Terrain-Gesellschaft", owned by the developer, no tenants at all. AND NO LEIBHOLZ AT 31 EITHER: the 1912 run goes Köhler, Koettlitz, KRINKE, Liebenhagen, where 1913 reads Köhler, Koeltlitz, LEIBHOLZ, Liebenhagen. *** 1914: THE LUWINSKIS ARE GONE AND GEORG LEIBHOLZ IS STILL THERE *** — number 32's alphabetical list runs Landow, Michaelis with nothing between, and 31 still carries "Leibholz, G., Kfm." SO THE LUWINSKI TENANCY IS ONE VOLUME WIDE: into a brand-new building during 1912, out again before the autumn of 1913. AND IT QUALIFIES THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN CLAIM — the birth-entry file counted the district as one of four agreeing facts, but the address dates from the autumn of 1912 and the birth was in May, and the family had moved that year. Three agree outright, one partly. The entry itself is untouched: the register index was read.

rows.what: WHICH STANDESAMT SERVED CHODOWIECKISTRASSE IN 1912
rows.note: The thing that now stands between this archive and Kurt's birth entry number. Row 220 enumerated twenty-one candidate 1912 birth-index volumes because the district was unknown. IT IS NO LONGER UNKNOWN — a Luwinski household was at Chodowieckistraße 32, PRENZLAUER BERG, POSTAL N 55, in the year he was born. Which of the old Roman-numeral Berlin registry offices covered that street in 1912 is NOT established and is deliberately not guessed at. The Berliner Adressbuch's own front matter lists the Standesämter with their districts; so does the Landesarchiv. One of those settles it, and settling it cuts twenty-one volumes to one or two. || *** ANSWERED THE SAME DAY: STANDESAMT 8. *** The Berliner Adressbuch's second part carries an alphabetical street index whose first column is headed "Standesamt". Chodowieckistraße: houses 1-10 → 8, 11-20 → 8, 21-22 → 10c, 23-32 → 8. Number 32 is office 8, and so is number 31 where the Leibholz lived. THE INSTRUMENT IS GENERAL: that table gives the registry office for every street in Berlin, and this archive will need it again.

rows.what: LEIBHOLZ, G., OF CHODOWIECKISTRASSE 31 — he is GEORG, and Jaques is four lines below him
rows.note: DONE the same day, from the name section of the same volume: "— GEORG, KAUFM., NO 55, CHODOWIECKISTR. 31 II." A merchant, second floor, next door to the Luwinskis at 32. This archive already holds a GEORG LEIBHOLZ, born at Hammerstein, who cannot be Jacob's brother and has his own lane; WHETHER HE IS THIS MAN IS NOT ESTABLISHED, though the 1913 volume lists exactly one Georg Leibholz in Berlin. *** AND FOUR LINES BELOW HIM: "— JAQUES, KAUFM., W 62, LUTHERSTR. 34 II." *** The man Auguste married eleven years later, in the same column of the same page — and TWENTY-FIVE YEARS EARLIER than the archive's previous earliest address for him. The 1913 Berlin Leibholz roll is transcribed in full in the evidence file. AND AN EIGHTH SPELLING, printed by the directory itself: "LEIPHOLZ, s. a. LEIBHOLZ", never searched anywhere.

rows.what: ORDER THE CERTIFICATE — Standesamt Berlin VIII, Geburtsregister 1912, Nr. 963
rows.note: THE ONE TO SEND FIRST OF EVERYTHING DRAFTED TODAY. A single document by its exact register number: no searching, no name to match, no protection period to argue — births are open after 110 years and 1912 was 114 years ago. *** WHAT IT WILL CONTAIN: *** Auguste Luwinski's age, occupation and ADDRESS ON 11 MAY 1912, which this archive has never had; THE FATHER'S COLUMN, whether filled or empty, and either answer is worth having; the informant; and SAMTLICHE RANDVERMERKE — the marginal notes. Auguste married Jacob Leibholz on 5 January 1924, and if Kurt was legitimised then, the note is in that margin. It is a copy order and will cost something; the letter asks for an estimate first and does not request a certified copy.

rows.what: LEIPHOLZ — an eighth spelling, printed by the Berliner Adressbuch itself, never searched
rows.note: The 1913 directory's own cross-reference reads "LEIPHOLZ, s. a. LEIBHOLZ" — the compiler treating the two as one name. THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER RUN IT: not at Arolsen, not at the Gedenkbuch, not at Mapping the Lives, not at the NAA, not at gazettes.africa, not in the Berlin indexes. Every bounded negative recorded for LEIBHOLZ · LAIBHOLZ · LEIBHOLTZ · LEIBBHOLZ is one spelling short until this is run. The 1925 volume repeats the same cross-reference, so it is not a one-year quirk. || STARTED THE SAME DAY. It is a real Berlin surname, present in every Adressbuch volume sampled from 1913 to 1943, and THE CROSS-REFERENCE RUNS BOTH WAYS — 1913 and 1924 print "Leipholz, s. a. Leibholz", 1940 prints "Leibholz s. o. Leipholz". *** AND ONE MAN MAY BE PRINTED UNDER BOTH: *** ADOLF, police officer, NO18 Friedenstraße — Leipholz in 1924 at no. 30, Leibholz in 1940 at no. 47, in the eleven-householder run this archive has already published. TEXT LAYER ONLY, NOT VERIFIED AT THE IMAGE: three crops of the 1924 page returned a different column because that page's ALTO coordinates do not map onto the served image. NAA: nothing. Gazettes.Africa: nothing. STILL TO RUN — Arolsen, the Gedenkbuch, Mapping the Lives, Yad Vashem, Queensland, Geneteka, and the Landesarchiv name indexes. Seven recorded negatives stay provisional until they are. || *** MAPPING THE LIVES RUN, AND THE RULE HAS PRODUCED A PERSON: WEILER, ELISABETH NÉE LEIPHOLZ, BORN 1 JANUARY 1891, BERLIN *** — exactly one, with LEIBHOLZ as the control on the same screen returning the hundred-capped list the archive already holds. She is in none of this archive's files under any spelling. NOT KIN ON ANY EVIDENCE HELD. Six instruments left: Arolsen, the Gedenkbuch, Yad Vashem, Queensland, Geneteka, and the Landesarchiv name indexes. || GEDENKBUCH RUN: LEIPHOLZ returns NOTHING, with LEIBHOLZ returning fifty as the control. Five instruments left. || *** YAD VASHEM RUNS IT AND THE RULE IS PROVED ON NAMED PEOPLE: *** WILLI LEIPHOLZ b.1887 Berlin and JENNY LEIPHOLZ b.1893 Berlin, both murdered, both with a Page of Testimony — AND THE GEDENKBUCH'S FIFTY CONTAIN "Leibholz, Wilhelm Willi (* 30.12.1887 in Berlin)" and "Leibholz, Jenny (* 11.02.1893 in Loosen)". The same couple, spelt with a B by a German federal archive and with a P by a Jerusalem memorial. That supersedes the unverified Adolf-the-policeman reading. Four instruments left: Arolsen, Queensland, Geneteka, the Landesarchiv name indexes. || QUEENSLAND: nothing. GENETEKA: the empty-parameter trap caught the archive a second time — both spellings first returned an empty table with province and record type left blank, and the Kowalski control with them filled in returned rows at once. RE-RUN PROPERLY, *** LEIPHOLZ FINDS WHAT LEIBHOLZ CANNOT IN OUR OWN PROVINCE: *** kujawsko-pomorskie births give Leibholz "Brak danych" and Leipholz one hit — Gottlieba Leipholz, mother, Runowo Krajeńskie 1905. AND A WARNING TO GO WITH THE RULE: warmińsko-mazurskie returns an 18th-century PROTESTANT Leipholz family at Orzysz-Arys in Masuria, which is not a Jewish family from Posen by any reading. Leipholz is also a surname in its own right. THE RULE WIDENS THE SEARCH; IT DOES NOT WIDEN THE FAMILY. Two instruments left: Arolsen and the Landesarchiv name indexes. || *** AROLSEN COMPLETES IT, WITH A THIRD PROOF: *** LEIPHOLZ returns BODIN, ELSE, maiden name LEIPHOLZ, born HAMMERSTEIN 12.08.1884, and LEIPHOLZ, HEINZ, plus three T/D cases. The Gedenkbuch's fifty contain "Bodin, Else (* 12.08.1884 in Hammerstein)" under LEIBHOLZ. A THIRD INSTITUTION, A THIRD PERSON, THE SAME TWO SPELLINGS — and this one is Hammerstein-born, which is where Sally Leibholz was born and where five of the fifty were born. NINE INSTRUMENTS SWEPT IN ONE EVENING. The rule produced FIVE PEOPLE the archive did not have — Elisabeth Weiler, Willi, Jenny, Heinz and Gottlieba — a Masurian Protestant family that must be kept out, and three separate demonstrations of the equivalence. DONE.

rows.what: LUTHERSTRASSE IS NOT MARTIN-LUTHER-STRASSE — checked, and the guess is dead
rows.note: ANSWERED THE SAME DAY IT WAS RAISED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. Berlin's MARTIN-LUTHER-STRASSE in Schöneberg has carried that name SINCE 28 DECEMBER 1899; its only earlier names were Heinrich-Kiepert-Straße (1893-1899) and Rostocker Straße (1884-1893). It was never a Lutherstraße. The only Lutherstraße in Berlin today is in STEGLITZ, formerly Grabenstraße. Source: berlin.kauperts.de. *** AND THE REFUTATION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE GUESS WAS: *** Jaques Leibholz's 1913 address is postal district W 62, which is BERLIN PROPER, and Schöneberg was a separate city until 1920 with its own postal districts. HE WAS NOT LIVING IN SCHÖNEBERG IN 1913 AT ALL. The family's arrival there is a move, not a continuity. Raised at 21:0x, struck within the hour, and the speculation never reached a narrative page in an unqualified form.

rows.what: SUPPLEMENT TO THE LANDESARCHIV — drafted in the mailbox, on the thread, not sent
rows.note: Sits in Gmail drafts as a reply on thread 1a0a19a926964a01, one click from going. It supplies what the 14 September letter could not: the exact register numbers. *** STANDESAMT BERLIN VIII, GEBURTSREGISTER 1912, NR. 963 *** for that letter's point 3, and *** STANDESAMT SCHÖNEBERG II, HEIRATSREGISTER 1924, NR. 6 *** for its point 2, each with the finding-aid page it came from and the reasoning for the identification. It leaves point 1 — Gertrud's death entry — and the divorce question standing untouched. AN ATTEMPT TO SEND IT DIRECTLY WAS REFUSED by this session's permission mode, which is why it is a draft; the archive did not work around that.

rows.what: WHERE WAS LUTHERSTRASSE, W 62 — Charlottenburg, and the reason this archive gave was wrong
rows.note: ANSWERED 21 SEPTEMBER, and it corrects this archive twice over. The Teil III heading, printed page 534 of the 1913 volume, reads *** "W. 62 LUTHERSTR. · A.G. CHARLOTTB. — L.G. III. · (GEH. Z. CHARLOTTENBURG)" *** — the street BELONGED TO CHARLOTTENBURG, an independent city until 1920 exactly as Schöneberg was. Last night this archive published that W 62 was BERLIN PROPER and reasoned from it; the conclusion (he was not in Schöneberg) survives and the reasoning does not. IT ALSO EXPLAINS A PUZZLE: the Berlin Straßenverzeichnis, whose first column is the Standesamt and which found Kurt's birth office, has NO Lutherstraße — its L column runs Lustgarten, Lutherbrücke, Lütticher with nothing between. That index lists Berlin's own streets and this was not one. *** SO JACOB'S 1913 REGISTRY OFFICE IS ONE OF STANDESAMT CHARLOTTENBURG I, II, III OR IV *** — all four have name indexes in the Landesarchiv's free online set, so the next step is mechanical. AND THE GEOGRAPHY IS WORTH STATING: Kurt was registered in May 1912 at Berlin VIII, Prenzlauer Berg, where the Luwinskis were; Jacob was at the far west end, nine kilometres and two municipalities away. Not an argument against his paternity and not one for it.

rows.what: WHERE WERE THE LUWINSKIS IN MAY 1912, AND WHERE DID THEY GO IN 1913
rows.note: Chodowieckistraße 32 was a NEUBAU in the 1912 volume and holds no Luwinski in the 1914 one. The household is caught by exactly one book. SO THERE IS AN ADDRESS BEFORE IT AND AN ADDRESS AFTER IT, and the one before it is where Kurt was born on 11 May 1912. The 1911 and 1912 volumes' NAME sections are the place to look — Teil I, under Luwinski, which the archive has swept for householders across 1900 to 1943 and found the name in 1933 only. THAT SWEEP NEEDS REDOING AGAINST THE TENANT LISTS RATHER THAN THE HOUSEHOLDER SECTION: J. Luwinski of Chodowieckistraße 32 is a TENANT in Teil III and does not appear in the Teil I householder index at all, which is exactly why forty-four years of sweeping missed him. || 21 SEPTEMBER: RECLASSIFIED, AND THE ANSWER IS ALREADY ORDERED. The row proposed re-sweeping the Teil I householder index against the tenant lists. That cannot work at the scale involved: J. Luwinski is a TENANT, tenants appear only in the street section, and finding one tenant in the 1911 or 1912 street section means reading a volume of six thousand pages with an OCR that mangles Fraktur. *** AND THERE IS NO NEED. *** Kurt's birth entry — Standesamt Berlin VIII 1912 Nr. 963, requested in letter 35 — CARRIES THE MOTHER'S ADDRESS ON THE DAY. The question this row asks is answered by a document already asked for, and chasing it another way would be work done twice.

rows.what: ELISABETH WEILER NÉE LEIPHOLZ — born Neustettin, and she got out to Palestine
rows.note: Found by running LEIPHOLZ at Mapping the Lives, which the archive had only ever searched as LEIBHOLZ. Exactly one person, surfaced through the maiden-name field. A Berlin woman born 1 January 1891 — the generation of Jacob (1884), Samuel (1877) and Oskar (1887). NOT KIN ON ANY EVIDENCE HELD and not asserted to be. WHAT WOULD TEST IT: her record page gives an address and a source, and Mapping the Lives is built on the 1939 census card, which names birthplaces. If she was born in SCHUBIN the question answers itself; if she was born in Berlin to a Leipholz household already in the directories, she belongs to the separate Leipholz line and goes on the register of lines as one. Either way she is the first thing the eighth spelling has produced and the reason the other six sweeps matter. || RECORD OPENED 21 SEPTEMBER. Born 1 JANUARY 1891 at NEUSTETTIN, Pommern — Szczecinek today; residence Berlin; basis of persecution racial; *** EMIGRATION: PALESTINE. *** Source: the Bundesarchiv Residents' List of Jewish Residents of the German Reich 1933-1945, ID 1166673. SHE IS NOT IN THE GEDENKBUCH BECAUSE SHE SURVIVED. Two things follow. First, NEUSTETTIN is the same Pomeranian belt as Tämpelburg, Zettin and Bärwalde among the Gedenkbuch's fifty, and about sixty kilometres from Hammerstein — a fourth independent point in the same corner, and the first attached to somebody who lived. Second, a caution: 1 JANUARY is the commonest placeholder in these lists for a year known without a day and must not be read as a birthday. NOT KIN ON ANY EVIDENCE HELD.

rows.what: THE SCHUBIN BRANCH IS A HAMMERSTEIN FAMILY — and the lanes were kept apart for a reason that has gone
rows.note: Of FIFTY Leibholz in the Bundesarchiv Gedenkbuch, EXACTLY THREE were born at Schubin, and they are Jacob, Samuel and Oskar. The other forty-seven cluster in Pomerania and West Prussia within about sixty kilometres of Schlochau: GLOWITZ 6, HAMMERSTEIN 5, KARWEN 5, SCHLOCHAU 3, BÄRWALDE 2, PREUSSISCH FRIEDLAND 2, TEMPELBURG 2, plus Zettin, Dammen, Loosen and Danzig. *** AND SALLY LEIBHOLZ, JACOB'S FATHER, WAS BORN AT HAMMERSTEIN ON 7 JULY 1847 AND MARRIED AT SZUBIN IN 1874. *** The archive has held both facts for days without drawing the line. The register of lines keeps "Hammerstein — Georg's" and "Kreis Schlochau" apart from ours because Georg was born at Hammerstein and our three at Schubin — BUT SO WAS OUR OWN GREAT-GREAT-GRANDFATHER. The lanes stay separate because no document joins them; the REASON for expecting them to be separate has gone. What would join them: Sally's own birth entry at Hammerstein in 1847, which would name his parents and put them beside Georg's. || 21 SEPTEMBER, AND THE TEST THIS ROW PROPOSED IS ALREADY CLOSED. The row said "what would join them: Sally's own birth entry at Hammerstein in 1847". *** ARCHIWUM PAŃSTWOWE W KOSZALINIE ANSWERED THAT ON 16 SEPTEMBER, reference O-S.6342.406.2026: *** no registers of the German civil registry at Czarne for 1874-1899, and NO SYNAGOGUE-COMMUNITY BOOKS FOR CZARNE AT ALL, and no information about where either went. An 1847 Jewish birth is precisely a synagogue-community record, so that route was shut five days before this row proposed it. Writing to Koszalin again would have been the eighth 'already had it'. GENETEKA TESTED TOO, 21 September, pomorskie births with Kowalski as the control returning rows from 1645: LEIBHOLZ nothing, LEIPHOLZ nothing. *** WHAT ACTUALLY JOINS THE LANES IS ALREADY IN THE POST: *** the SZUBIN MARRIAGE OF 24 NOVEMBER 1874, Sally to Friederike Schmul, which names the parents of both parties and is the second ask in the Bydgoszcz letter. The join runs through Bydgoszcz, not Koszalin, and the letter is sent and unanswered. *** 22 SEPTEMBER — THE TEST THIS ROW WAS WAITING ON HAS BEEN RUN, AND IT HALF-ANSWERS. *** The row said “what actually joins the lanes is already in the post: the SZUBIN MARRIAGE OF 24 NOVEMBER 1874, which names the parents of both parties”. IT DID NOT COME BY POST. Bydgoszcz answered by pointing at a portal where the register had been published since 2015, and it was read at the image the same hour. *** IT NAMES OUR SIDE: SALLY LEIBHOLZ, TWENTY-SEVEN, GEBOREN ZU HAMMERSTEIN, WOHNHAFT ZU HAMMERSTEIN, SOHN DES KAUFMANN JACOB LEIBHOLZ UND DER WILHELMINE GEB. POLLNOW. *** So the Schubin branch is a Hammerstein family and that is no longer an inference; and the archive now has a NAMED HAMMERSTEIN LEIBHOLZ HOUSEHOLD — Jacob Senior and Wilhelmine — where before it had only a birthplace. It also DATES THE MOVE: still at Hammerstein in November 1874, at Schubin by August 1884. *** BUT IT DOES NOT JOIN THE LANES, BECAUSE IT NAMES ONLY ONE SIDE OF THE JOIN. *** To place Georg beside Sally you need GEORG'S parents, and the archive has now exhausted the cheap routes for them: his Hammerstein birth entry of 1884 is in the Standesamt Czarne registers that Koszalin confirmed do not survive for 1874-1899; his Gedenkbuch entry names no parents; AND HIS YAD VASHEM PAGE WAS ALREADY CHECKED FOR PARENTS on 20 September — item 1684365, birth year 1883, birthplace the single word “Germany”, no father and no mother on it. THE ONE UNTESTED ROUTE TO GEORG'S PARENTS IS HIS OWN MARRIAGE to Lydia Perl, which would name them as Sally's did. Neither its date nor its registry office is known, and Berlin marriage indexes run to a couple of thousand reads per office, so this is a real job and not a lookup. AND WHAT THE HAMMERSTEIN LANE NOW LOOKS LIKE: five Gedenkbuch Leibholz were born there — Regina 1872, Arthur 1878, Else 1884, GEORG 1884, Hertha 1890 — a continuous presence from before Sally's birth in 1847 to at least 1890. Sally came out of that. NONE OF THEM IS JOINED TO HIM BY A DOCUMENT and the lanes stay apart.

rows.what: LYDIA NÉE PERL WAS BORN AT BISCHOFSTEIN — checked, and the check found a 50 km error on the atlas
rows.note: The Gedenkbuch gives a birthplace this archive did not hold: LYDIA LEIBHOLZ, born 16 JANUARY 1885 at BISCHOFSTEIN. She is Lydia née Perl, daughter of Julius and Mina, wife of GEORG LEIBHOLZ of the Michaelkirchstraße laundry, deported with him to Łódź and dead with him at Chełmno. *** BISCHOFSTEIN IS BISZTYNEK, IN THE ERMLAND, ABOUT FIFTEEN KILOMETRES FROM SAUERBAUM *** — where Auguste Luwinski was born and where her mother's people farmed. AND GEORG LEIBHOLZ LIVED NEXT DOOR TO THE LUWINSKIS at Chodowieckistraße in 1913 and 1914. NOT PROOF OF ANYTHING: two Ermländer households next door to each other in Prenzlauer Berg is how chain migration works, and Berlin was full of them. IT IS THE FIRST MECHANISM THE ARCHIVE HAS EVER HAD for how a Catholic dressmaker from Kreis Rößel came to marry a Jewish merchant from Posen. CHECK FIRST: that Bischofstein was in Kreis Rößel in 1885, which has not been verified. || CHECKED 21 SEPTEMBER, BOTH HALVES. The Kreis: German Wikipedia's Bisztynek article says Bischofstein was assigned to KREIS RÖSSEL in 1815 and was still Landkreis Rössel in 1945, so Kreis Rößel in 1885. CONFIRMED. The distance: published as fifteen kilometres, actually 17.8 — Zerbuń 53.935/20.846 to Bisztynek 54.093/20.888 — corrected to eighteen everywhere it appears. *** AND THE CHECK FOUND SOMETHING THE CLAIM DID NOT: THE ATLAS PIN FOR SAUERBAUM WAS FIFTY KILOMETRES WRONG. *** It sat at 54.35/21.15, placed before the village was identified at all, and the map had been showing Auguste Luwinski's birthplace fifty kilometres from where she was born. Correction 9500903. THE LESSON IS THE CHEAP ONE: the arithmetic that tests a claim also tests everything the claim is measured against.

rows.what: THE TWO PAGES OF TESTIMONY — opened, and they correct this archive's own note
rows.note: DONE 21 September. Both filled in by KHANAN ROSENBERG VARADI, recorded as "Family" on Willi's page and as NEPHEW on Jenny's — so a Rosenberg, a child of one of Jenny's siblings, who survived and wrote out what happened to his aunt and uncle. *** WILLI'S PAGE IS AN EXACT MATCH FOR A HOUSEHOLD THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HAD: *** born 30.12.1887, wife Jenny née Rosenberg, address WEINSTR 6 — the Weinstraße 6 household from the 1939 census and the 1938-41 directories. And it adds what a census card cannot: PLACE OF DEATH AUSCHWITZ, where Mapping the Lives could only say "died before 08.05.1945". JENNY'S PAGE GIVES HER PARENTS — ISIDOR and CECILLIE Rosenberg — and her birthplace, SCHLOCHAU, which is the district Sally Leibholz was born in and where the Gedenkbuch's fifty cluster. *** AND IT CORRECTS THE REGISTER OF LINES: *** the entry read "NOT the Wilhelm Yad Vashem has", written off a LEIBHOLZ search and true of that search. BOTH WILHELMS ARE AT YAD VASHEM — the 1890 one under LEIBHOLZ and the Weinstraße one under LEIPHOLZ. A DISCREPANCY LEFT OPEN: the Gedenkbuch gives Jenny's birthplace as Loosen, the Page of Testimony as Schlochau. NO APPROACH HAS BEEN MADE to the submitter and whether one should is David's call.

rows.what: TWO NAME FOLDS OFFERED BY THE SHARED TOOLING, BOTH REFUSED — and the decision is written down so it is not re-asked
rows.note: namefold.py held back two changes because each alters a letter in a name, and asked the archive that owns them. CORRECTLY. *** BOTH REFUSED. *** LUWINSKY → Luwinski, eighteen tokens: every one is either a QUOTED DOCUMENT — the Witwatersrand court index reads "Kurt LUWINSKY versus Ivone (born Mota Figueiredo)" — or a DELIBERATE VARIANT LIST on the lines page, the names page and the bounded negatives. The fold would have turned "searched LUWINSKI and LUWINSKY" into "searched LUWINSKI and LUWINSKI", which is a false account of work already published. HOSTOWSKI → HOSTOWSKY: *** AND THIS ONE RUNS THE WRONG WAY. *** Frances appears as Hostovsky on the 1956 marriage register, Hostowski in the Cape Town and Wynberg register and Hostowsky in the 1957 divorce. The archive has argued Hostovsky is her birth form, on the most formal of the three; folding onto HOSTOWSKY would enshrine the wrong one and destroy the other two. WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD: Frances added to the names page as a second person with all three forms and the document each comes from, and a method section stating the rule — quoted spellings are never altered, variant lists are never collapsed, and where the archive speaks in its own voice it says which form it chose and why. The underlying worry was fair and is answered; the fix is not the fold. || 21 SEPTEMBER: THE TOOL WAS CORRECTED AND THE REFUSAL SHOULD NOT BE READ AS A STANDING COMPLAINT. Where an archive spells a name several ways namefold now NAMES THE LABEL IT USED AND SAYS IT IS ONLY A LABEL, and applies the map to the query and the stored row alike, so every form finds every other and nothing claims one is correct. That is the honest version of the objection: the defect was the implication, not the choice. The two specific folds stay refused because they are still wrong for this content. AND THE DISTINCTION IS NOW ON THE METHOD PAGE: a fold of this kind is A SEARCH RULE WITH NO CONCEPT OF IDENTITY — these letters find those rows, not these people are those people. It is the line between LEIPHOLZ reaching Willi and Jenny and LEIPHOLZ reaching the Protestant family at Orzysz-Arys.

rows.what: THE MENU SPINE, WRITTEN DOWN AT LAST
rows.note: A peer session pointed out that seven sibling archives share a spine of "The families" and "People & places" and this one runs "Start · Our line · Places · People & names · Evidence", and that a deviation nobody has recorded is indistinguishable from drift. RIGHT, AND NOW RECORDED ON THE METHOD PAGE. "Our line" because the question this archive exists to answer is a single descent — whether Derrick is Kurt's son — and a families group would invite families that are not the subject. "People & names" because the naming is the obstacle, not an ornament: Ivone is filed under six maiden spellings, three forenames and four married surnames, and on 20 September an EIGHTH spelling of the Leibholz name turned out to reach people the other seven could not. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: the peer's supporting reason — "this archive is one woman and her documents rather than a family" — describes the /names page, which is about Ivone, and not this archive, which is a family of at least four generations. The spine is right; that reason for it is not.

rows.what: check:living WATCHED THE PAGES AND NOT THE DATA — widened to served JSON, and proved
rows.note: A peer session found this blind spot across the shared tooling and widened the KIT's gate. *** THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT USE THE KIT'S GATE — it runs its own tools/check-living.py — so the fix did not reach it. *** The gate walked *.html only, and this site serves two JSON files a browser fetches directly: dist/atlas-data.json behind the map and dist/searchindex.json. MEASURED BEFORE CHANGING: leak zero. A first crude grep looked like three hits and every one was a published dead namesake — Joachim Luwinski b.1865, Sally Leibholz, Gertrud Leibke — the same false-positive trap the peer reported. NOW WALKS *.html AND *.json: 27 pages became 29 files, still clean. AND PROVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: a scratch build with a guarded living person in a served atlas-data.json and nothing in the HTML — the old gate said "ok" and exited zero, the new one named the file, the person and the matched text and failed. The one thing a peer cannot do for this archive is fix a tool it does not use, so a shared finding still has to be re-landed locally.

rows.what: WHERE THE EVIDENCE FOR A BUG LIVES — three silent failures in one day, none visible in the case in front of it
rows.note: Written onto the method page because it is the most transferable thing the day produced. THE LANDESARCHIV: four offices returned nothing and this archive nearly published "Schöneberg has no online name index"; the database stores office names double-encoded, so the correct spelling finds nothing and the mangled one finds seventeen volumes, and the tell was that all four failures carried an umlaut and no success did. GENETEKA: both spellings returned an empty table with the province and record-type parameters left blank, and a blank parameter there is not 'everywhere' but 'nothing'. A PEER'S TOOL: a change of selection rule took a working map from 1,495 rows back to 59, caught by regenerating and reading the map rather than by reading the code. *** IN ALL THREE THE EVIDENCE WAS IN THE SET, NOT IN ANY ONE CASE *** — a shared character, a query shape that differed from the control, a count that moved. The standing rule was already that a negative is worth recording only if a positive control went down the same path. The addition: WHEN SEVERAL NEGATIVES HAVE SOMETHING IN COMMON, SUSPECT THE THING THEY HAVE IN COMMON BEFORE BELIEVING THE NEGATIVES.

rows.what: ISIDOR AND CECILLIE ROSENBERG OF SCHLOCHAU — two names arrived from a nephew's handwriting
rows.note: Jenny Leipholz née Rosenberg, born Schlochau 11 February 1893, daughter of ISIDOR and CECILLIE. From her Page of Testimony, written by her nephew. NOT THIS FAMILY ON ANY EVIDENCE HELD — she married into a Berlin Leipholz household with no shown connection to the Schubin Leibholzes. WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW ANYWAY: Schlochau is the district Sally Leibholz was born in, the Gedenkbuch's fifty cluster there, and this archive has been trying for days to get behind Sally's generation. A Rosenberg family at Schlochau with two given names attached is a thread in the right place. CHEAP TESTS: Geneteka and the Polish state archives for ROSENBERG at Człuchów, which is Schlochau; and the other Pages of Testimony submitted by the same nephew, which would give his own generation of the family. *** PUT TO THE BERLIN DIRECTORIES 22 SEPTEMBER AND NOT FOUND. *** “Rosenberg Isidor” returns 12 and every one is a company registration — Hermann Rosenberg GmbH, Gebr. Rosenberg, Max Rosenberg GmbH, a Rosenberg-Kleider-Werkstätte. NONE IS THE SCHLOCHAU ISIDOR. Rosenberg is among the commonest Jewish surnames in Berlin and a forename search cannot separate him from it.

rows.what: JACOB AT LUTHERSTRASSE 34 — which of the four Charlottenburg registry offices, and is he there before 1913
rows.note: Now that the street is placed in CHARLOTTENBURG, the office is one of Standesamt Charlottenburg I, II, III or IV, and all four have free name indexes in the Landesarchiv's online set — the same instrument that produced Kurt's birth number and the 1924 marriage number. WHAT IT WOULD ANSWER: how long Jaques Leibholz was at Lutherstraße 34, and whether anything of his is registered in Charlottenburg before 1924 — a first marriage, an acknowledgement of paternity, a death in the family. THE CHARLOTTENBURG STREET INDEX gives the office directly, the way the Berlin one did; it is in the Charlottenburg section of the volume rather than the Berlin Straßenverzeichnis, which is why the first search missed it. *** ATTEMPTED 22 SEPTEMBER BY FULL TEXT, AND IT IS NOT A FULL-TEXT JOB. *** The ZLB Solr index was queried for the street beside the office: “Standesamt Charlottenburg” AND “Lutherstr” returns ZERO. THAT ZERO IS NOT A FINDING — these volumes are Fraktur, the OCR renders ſ and the ligatures unreliably, and a street list sets the office as a heading rather than beside each street, so the two words need never sit close enough to co-occur on a page. The Straßenverzeichnis has to be found and READ AT THE IMAGE, in the Charlottenburg section of a Charlottenburg volume, which is what this row already said. *** AND THE ATTEMPT TURNED UP A TRAP WORTH RECORDING: THERE ARE TWO LUTHERSTRASSEN. *** Querying “Lutherstr” with “Standesamt” returns 41 pages, and the ones that look most promising are Standesbeamte directories where the hits are the REGISTRARS' OWN HOME ADDRESSES — and every one of those is “W 62, Lutherſtr.”, the Schöneberg/Tiergarten street, not the Charlottenburg one. Anybody searching this street by name without the postal district will find the wrong road and the right-looking word Standesamt beside it. *** 22 SEPTEMBER, SECOND PASS — THE INDEXES ARE NOW INVENTORIED AND ONE OFFICE IS RULED OUT. *** All four Charlottenburg designations were queried at the Landesarchiv's own finder and the result is 143 NAME-INDEX VOLUMES, listed in data/labsa-charlottenburg-inventory.tsv, which nobody here had ever written down. *** CHARLOTTENBURG IV DID NOT EXIST IN 1913 — its earliest volume of any kind is 1922 — and the unnumbered office closes in 1897, SO THE OFFICE IS ONE OF I, II OR III, not one of four. *** Births run only to 1914 in all three; marriages and deaths run to 1938. The three numbered offices hold 40 birth, 38 marriage and 36 death index volumes, so the job is 114 volumes and not the unbounded thing it was being costed as. *** AND THE FINDER ITSELF HAS A DEFECT WORTH MORE THAN THE INVENTORY. *** LABSA's three record-type checkboxes DO NOT UNION: ticking all three returns ZERO for Schöneberg, which returns SIXTY-ONE death volumes with the single box. A count or a zero from the combined form is worth nothing. The archive's existing Schöneberg work was checked against this rather than assumed safe — 61 is exactly the single-box figure, so nothing published is disturbed. tools/labsa.py now refuses the combined query and carries the control numbers. THE BLOCKER IS UNCHANGED AND IS THE STREET, NOT THE OFFICES: narrowing three to one needs the Charlottenburg street directory, and a second attempt today failed in the text layer exactly as the first did. "Lutherstr" with "Standesamt" and with "StdA" both return zero in the 1913 volume and THOSE ZEROS ARE NOT FINDINGS — Fraktur display type is what this OCR handles worst. It must be read at the image, and the two-Lutherstrassen trap is still live. *** 23 SEPTEMBER — AND YESTERDAY'S INVENTORY WAS A THIRD SHORT. *** There are SIX Charlottenburg designations and 207 volumes, not five and 143: STANDESAMT CHARLOTTENBURG VON BERLIN holds 64 more, 1938-1994. It was missed because the offices were GUESSED AT rather than enumerated, and LABSA matches the office name exactly. The conclusion is untouched — the von Berlin office begins in 1938, so a 1913 event is still one of I, II or III.

rows.what: WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ, GENERALDIREKTOR AND STADTRAT — is he the Melbourne man's father
rows.note: The Victorian death index names Joachim Peter Leibholz's father as WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ and his mother as NANETTE née NETTER. This archive's Berliner Adressbuch notes already hold a WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ — Generaldirektor and STADTRAT, a Berlin city councillor, in the 1920 volume, and "William, Kaufm., W15 Kurfürstendamm 169" in 1913, the only William on the 1913 roll. TESTS, IN ORDER OF CHEAPNESS: the Berlin name indexes for a Charlottenburg or Berlin marriage of William Leibholz to a NETTER, which the Landesarchiv's free set would give; the Gedenkbuch and Yad Vashem for NETTER; and the Victorian death certificate itself, which carries the parents in full and is a purchase. NOTE WHAT IT WOULD AND WOULD NOT SHOW: it would place the Melbourne lane inside Berlin's Leibholz community with a named, public father. It would not connect that lane to Schubin. *** TRACED ACROSS TWENTY-THREE YEARS, 22 SEPTEMBER. *** 1920 “GEN. DIREKT., STADTRAT”; 1921 Wilmersdorf; 1925 “Kaufmann, Direktor” at Sigmaringer Str. 30, Grunewald; 1929 “FABRIKANT, Grunewald, Königsallee”; 1932 and 1933 at KÖNIGSALLEE 29, BERLIN-GRUNEWALD — and a 1932 motor register entry, “Leibholz, William, Grunewald, Königsallee 29, HORCH 65”. THE RECORD STOPS IN 1933 and there is nothing after; no claim is made about why, since a sparse index, a death, a move or a changed entry all look the same. *** AND HE IS NOT IN THE GEDENKBUCH, WHICH WAS CHECKED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS SAID: *** its three Wilhelms were born 1887, 1890 and 1904 and lived in Neukölln and Friedrichshain, and a man already Stadtrat in 1920 was born about 1870. THE ROW'S QUESTION IS STILL OPEN: “Netter Nanette” returns ZERO in these books, and the eight pages carrying both Leibholz and Netter are a directory of thousands of names where sharing a page means nothing. What would join them is Joachim Peter's Berlin birth entry of 1903.

rows.what: check:evidence FAILED INTERMITTENTLY AND THE '26' WAS NEVER A CLUE — diagnosed, reproduced and fixed
rows.note: DIAGNOSED AND FIXED 21 SEPTEMBER. This row recorded two red runs, on 20 and 21 September, that passed again immediately afterwards, and it noted as suspicious that BOTH REPORTED EXACTLY 26 PROBLEMS. *** THE 26 IS NOT A FINGERPRINT. IT IS THE DISPLAY CAP. *** The gate builds a list called `problems`; for silent people it appends ONE header line plus `silent[:25]`. So any failure with twenty-five or more silent people prints exactly 26, whether twenty-five people are missing or all of them. Two investigations read a constant and inferred a deterministic subset from what was arithmetic. *** REPRODUCED. *** Pointed at an EMPTY dist the gate printed the signature exactly: 183 silent, capped to 25 names, 'FAIL check-evidence — 26 problem(s); evidence is not reaching the page'. astro clears dist before it rewrites it, so a second build against the same tree empties the directory under a gate that is mid-read, and every documented person goes silent at once. That is the mechanism this row suspected and could not show. The load-average-267 measurement is consistent with it and remains a circumstance rather than proof of which read lost. *** WHAT WAS CHANGED, AND ALL FOUR BRANCHES ARE TESTED. *** (1) The gate now SNAPSHOTS dist — every HTML path with its size and mtime — before and after reading, and if the two differ it says 'site/dist CHANGED WHILE THIS GATE WAS READING IT' and refuses to judge. Proved by touching a dist page mid-read. (2) An empty dist is named as such — 'holds NO HTML AT ALL, that is not a finished build' — instead of being blamed on the evidence. (3) If more than half the documented people are absent at once the gate says 'THAT IS A BROKEN OR PARTIAL BUILD, NOT AN EVIDENCE FAULT' and prints how many HTML pages it actually read. A real evidence regression touches a handful; it does not silence a hundred. Proved against a one-page dist: '179 of 187 documented people are absent from dist AT ONCE, having read 1 HTML page(s)'. (4) The failure line now reports THE TRUE NUMBER OF SILENT PEOPLE rather than the length of a capped list, and says '... and N more, not listed' when it truncates. *** THE STANDING RULE IN THIS ROW STILL HOLDS AND IS NOW ENFORCED RATHER THAN REMEMBERED: *** never run two builds against one tree. The difference is that the gate now tells you that is what happened instead of accusing the data.

rows.what: BUILD THE ADDRESS-TO-REGISTRY-OFFICE MAP FOR EVERY BERLIN ADDRESS THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS
rows.note: The Berliner Adressbuch's Straßenverzeichnis carries a column headed STANDESAMT, street by street. It is how Kurt's birth office was found — Chodowieckistraße to Berlin VIII to Geburtsregister 1912 Nr. 963 — and it has been used ONCE. This archive holds roughly thirty Berlin addresses: Meraner Str. 2, Levetzowstr. 13, Michaelkirchstr. 26, Kommandantenstr. 29, Waghäuseler Str. 9/10, Weinstr. 6, Treuchtlinger Str. 4, Leinestr. 32, Mehringdamm 109, Willmanndamm, Hasenheide, Egellsstr. 16, Ramlerstr. 15, Stephanstr. 7, Chodowieckistr. 32, Lutherstr. 34 and more. NOT ONE OF THE OTHERS HAS BEEN RUN THROUGH THAT COLUMN. *** WHY IT IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE ITEM ON THE LIST: *** every certificate this archive will ever ask for has to name an office, and at present it would be guessing. One afternoon converts a list of streets into a list of offices, and the Landesarchiv's free name indexes are organised BY OFFICE, so the map is also the key to searching them.  *** 21 SEPTEMBER, AND IT DID NOT WORK. *** The Adressbuch route was tried and abandoned with a reason. The 1913 Straßenverzeichnis carries the Standesamt column, but its OCR is a four-column table read as one stream of fragments -- which is why Kurt's office was read at the IMAGE and not from the text. The 1938 volume has no such column at all: its Teil IV is a house-by-house RESIDENT list, and the running heads that might have given a district are Fraktur mush ("IV. Seil", "IY, Zeit", "IV. jrdr"). A map of thirty addresses built from that would be a map of guesses. WHAT REPLACED IT, AND WORKED THE SAME AFTERNOON: go at the office indexes directly. LABSA answers a plain POST, lists every register volume an office holds, and the volumes are readable in place. The borough is knowable from the postal prefix the directory already prints. THE ITEM IS STRUCK, NOT DONE -- the map does not exist and the thing it was wanted for was got another way.

rows.what: THE SCHÖNEBERG AND WEDDING DEATH INDEXES FOR THE FOUR LEIBHOLZ WOMEN AND THE TWO POST-WAR LUWINSKI MEN
rows.note: Deaths leave the protection period after thirty years, which is why the Schöneberg death indexes run YEAR BY YEAR TO 1994 while the births stop in 1913. FOUR LEIBHOLZ WOMEN LEAVE THIS ARCHIVE'S STORY WITH NO DEATH RECORDED: ELLA, Krankenschwester, Willmanndamm, in the books to 1970 · CHARLOTTE, Hasenheide, 1957 to 1967 · AGNES née KERGER, Mehringdamm 109, to 1976 · ERNA, Spandau, 1980, the last Leibholz in the Berlin books. Three of those addresses sit in offices whose death indexes are online. THE SAME FOR THE TWO MEN THE POST-WAR SWEEP FOUND: Joachim the Ofensetzer of Ramlerstr. 15 in Wedding, and the second Kurt, the Postfacharbeiter, whom the family tree has dying in 1995. A death entry gives the date, the address, the informant, and usually an age — and an age gives a birth year to test against the tree. DEPENDS ON ROW 244 for the office of each address.  *** 21 SEPTEMBER: SEVEN OF SCHÖNEBERG'S SIXTY-ONE DEATH VOLUMES READ. *** 1970-1977 less 1975. Ella is in none of them. AND 1975 GAVE UP SOMEBODY ELSE: "Leipholz | Erna Frida Else | 13.1. | 79 | ev" -- Sterberegister Schöneberg 1975 Nr. 79. See data/schoeneberg-death-indexes.tsv. Three of the four women are NOT Schöneberg cases and this row was wrong to imply they were: Mehringdamm and Hasenheide are Kreuzberg and Neukölln, Streitstraße is Spandau. Only Ella's three addresses are Schöneberg.  *** 21 SEPTEMBER, CLOSED FOR SCHÖNEBERG: 1970 TO 1994 READ IN FULL, TWENTY-FIVE CONSECUTIVE YEARS, EVERY ONE BRACKETED ON BOTH SIDES. *** The only Leibholz or Leipholz in the entire run is ERNA FRIDA ELSE LEIPHOLZ in 1975. ELLA DID NOT DIE IN SCHÖNEBERG IN THE TWENTY-FIVE YEARS AFTER SHE LAST APPEARS IN A DIRECTORY. The row is done in the sense that the office is exhausted from 1970 on; what it did NOT do is find her, and the remaining possibilities are a different borough, a home, a marriage, or a death before 1970 in one of the thirty-two volumes covering 1938-1969 that have not been read.

rows.what: OPEN THE OTHER FORTY-SIX GEDENKBUCH RECORDS
rows.note: DONE 22 September 2026, and not by opening forty-six pages. The search form has an EXPORT AS CSV control; the same request was made inside the page and the response decoded in memory — it is windows-1252, and read as UTF-8 every umlaut is destroyed. It returns EIGHTEEN COLUMNS for all fifty at once: birth name, Geburtskreis, Geburtsland, borough, Inhaftierung, Emigration, both deportation legs with dates, Schicksal, place and date of death. leibholz-gedenkbuch.tsv held four and now holds FIFTY-TWO. THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE NEEDS CORRECTING AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE: forty-four of the fifty do live in Berlin, but the Gedenkbuch gives the BOROUGH, NOT THE STREET. A borough cannot be laid against the Adressbuch the way the Weinstraße household was; it can only say which pages are worth reading. That work is still to do and is bigger than this row supposed — see row 260. WHY FIFTY-TWO AND NOT FIFTY: a ten-spelling sweep of the same box found LAIBHOLZ, which returns GEORG LAIBHOLZ b. 01.01.1883 and LIDIA LAIBHOLZ b. 1884, both of Berlin, both dead at Auschwitz, and neither a duplicate of the Georg and the Lydia already in the fifty. One vowel had hidden two murdered people from every search run here. AND THE SWEEP CAUGHT A FAULT IN ITSELF: pressing Return in that box does not submit the form, and five terms read back '50 Results' that were all the previous page. Five untested negatives nearly entered this archive as five findings. See gedenkbuch-leibholz-findings.tsv and the negatives page.

rows.what: THE THIRTY-TWO BOUNDED NEGATIVES, CLASSIFIED — and the premise of this row was wrong
rows.note: THIRTY-TWO bounded negatives are published on this site and most were searched under LEIBHOLZ alone. Three separate institutions have since been shown to write the same murdered person both LEIBHOLZ and LEIPHOLZ. *** EVERY ONE OF THE THIRTY-TWO IS THEREFORE PROVISIONAL, and the archive has not said so on the page. *** Two things are owed: first, mark which of the thirty-two could be reached by the eighth spelling and which genuinely could not; second, re-run the ones that could. THIS IS THE SAME FAILURE AS THE UMLAUT AND THE BLANK GENETEKA PARAMETER — a negative is only as wide as the spelling it was searched under, and this archive learned that lesson after it had already printed thirty-two of them.  *** AND IT NOW HAS A WORKED EXAMPLE RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. *** On 21 September the Schöneberg death indexes were scanned for LEIBHOLZ across 1970-1977 and returned nothing four years running. The pattern was widened to Le[iy][bp]h and the 1975 volume answered immediately with ERNA FRIDA ELSE LEIPHOLZ. THE NARROW SCAN HAD ALREADY READ THAT VOLUME AND CALLED IT EMPTY. That is this row's claim demonstrated on a document, not inferred.  *** 21 SEPTEMBER — CLASSIFIED, AND THE FIRST THING IT FOUND WAS AN ERROR IN THIS ROW. *** This row says 'most were searched under LEIBHOLZ alone'. THEY WERE NOT. Of the thirty-two, ONLY THREE MENTION A LEIBHOLZ SPELLING AT ALL — no. 18 (NAAIRS), no. 28 (the Koszalin letter about Hammerstein) and no. 31 (TNA Discovery). The other twenty-nine are WEAR, LUWINSKI, CASTLE, FIGUEIREDO, SALKOW and record-class negatives that name no person. The row's principle is right and its arithmetic was not, and the corrected shape is more useful: THE QUESTION IS NOT 'WHICH WERE SEARCHED UNDER ONE LEIBHOLZ SPELLING' BUT 'WHICH WERE SEARCHED UNDER ONE SPELLING OF ANY NAME'. On a crude count eighteen of the thirty-two name a single form of their family name, though that over-counts, because several are not name searches at all — no. 12 is about whether a grave reopening was recorded and no. 13 about what a register asked for. *** WHAT WAS ACTUALLY RE-RUN, AND IT IS ONE. *** Only no. 31 can be re-run free and without an account today: NAAIRS has stopped answering altogether (row 178), FamilySearch needs a sign-in, and no. 28 is a letter awaiting a reply. TNA DISCOVERY WAS RE-RUN ACROSS FOURTEEN SPELLINGS AND THE NEGATIVE HOLDS AND IS NOW WIDER: LUWENSKI and LUWINSK also return zero, so four forms are bracketed instead of two, and LEIPHOLZ, LEYBHOLZ, LAIBHOLZ, LEIBHOLTZ, LEIPHOLTZ, LEIBOLZ and LEIPHOLS all return zero, so the sixteen Leibholz records are the whole of what Discovery holds under any spelling. Two neighbouring surnames DO return and are now named on the page so nobody finds them twice: LOWINSKI 20, LEWINSKI 228, neither this family. *** WHAT IS STILL OWED. *** The eighteen single-spelling negatives need reading one at a time to separate the name searches from the record-class ones, and the name searches re-run when their instrument is reachable again. THE ROW STAYS OPEN and it now says what it is asking for. *** 22 SEPTEMBER — ALL THIRTY-THREE CLASSIFIED ONE AT A TIME, AND THE ROW'S OWN COUNT COMES DOWN AGAIN. *** This row had already corrected itself once, from 'most were searched under LEIBHOLZ alone' to a crude count of eighteen single-spelling negatives. EIGHTEEN IS STILL TOO HIGH AND THE REAL NUMBER IS TEN. Reading each one: NINE ARE NOT NAME SEARCHES AT ALL (a coverage count, a structural argument about consular registers, a keyword search on NATURALIZATION, two questions about what a register FORM asked for, a holdings question about Krmpote, a question about what is online, a DNA argument, and an archive's signed answer about whether two series survive) — spelling cannot be the reason for any of those zeros. THREE ARE WITHDRAWN and are not live negatives. ELEVEN WERE ALREADY MULTI-SPELLING. That leaves TEN genuine one-spelling searches for a person. *** THREE WERE RE-RUN AND THE SCORE IS ONE HELD, ONE DOWNGRADED, ONE CLOSED WITHOUT SEARCHING. *** No. 3, Leonard's death in England and Wales, was re-run with FreeBMD's own PHONETIC flag: soundex WEAR returns 6,664 deaths for 1970-1985 against 241 for the exact string, TWENTY-SEVEN TIMES the pool the original saw. Narrowed by the forename it gives about forty Leonards across WEIR, WARE, WARR, WRAY, WHEAR, WYER, WERE, WROE, WERRY, WHURR, WIER and WERRA — and NOT ONE WAS BORN IN 1917, which is Leonard's year. THE NEGATIVE SURVIVES AND IS NOW MUCH STRONGER. No. 9, Kurt's naturalisation, needed no search: negative 0 already sweeps the SAME CORPUS under eight spellings with no year limit, so one negative widens the other, and the live re-count still returns exactly eight Luwinski documents. A NEGATIVE CAN BE WIDENED BY READING THE ONE NEXT TO IT. *** AND NO. 7 WAS DOWNGRADED, WHICH IS THE FIND. *** The 1973 probate calendar negative was a KEYWORD match over the OCR of scanned calendar pages. Re-run without the keyword, the image half returns FORTY-ONE DOCUMENT PAGES carrying the surname in 1973 and NOT ONE HAS BEEN OPENED; *** CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE REAL FINDING. *** The first write-up said a Zqxvwyrk null control returned zero and therefore the forty-one were a genuine surname result. IT DOES NOT. Run properly, “41 document pages” comes back for Wear, for Smith, for Luwinski, for nonsense, for 1979 as well as 1973, for the forename Leonard and for the keyword AUBREY. THE IMAGE HALF RUNS NO SEARCH AT ALL — it is a browse handle onto calendar images that opens at BAINBRIDGE. And the digital half holds nothing before 1996 and says so. SO NEGATIVE 7 IS WITHDRAWN, NOT DOWNGRADED: its zero was guaranteed before anyone typed a name. The bad control was published because it agreed with what this archive already suspected and was never repeated. *** SEVEN REMAIN BLOCKED behind NAAIRS, FamilySearch and Findmypast and are now marked provisional instead of being left to look settled. THE FIRST TO RE-RUN THE DAY NAAIRS ANSWERS IS NO. 18, the Leibholz search, because the eighth spelling is precisely the failure it is exposed to. *** The whole classification is in negatives-classified.tsv. THE ROW STAYS OPEN on the seven blocked negatives and on the forty-one unread probate pages, which are row 261. *** AND THE SCORE CHANGES WITH IT: one held, one closed by cross-reference, ONE WITHDRAWN — plus one error of this archive's own, made and corrected the same evening. *** AND THEN A THIRD TIME, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT IS ACTUALLY RIGHT. *** The withdrawal above was ALSO WRONG. Find a Will's image half is NOT a browse handle: it calls an OCR endpoint, pp_cowindex_default_search, and called directly it plainly works — WEAR 1973 returns 41 calendar chunks, SMITH 1973 returns 469, LUWINSKI and the nonsense string return 0. WHAT IS BROKEN IS THE PAGE, NOT THE SEARCH: it prints “41 document pages returned” for every one of those, after a fresh load, including with the keyword AUBREY. So negative 7 is NOT withdrawn and NOT proven — IT IS UNRESOLVED, and the two chunks that bracket the name (009223_weake_1973.pdf and 009225_wearmouth_1973.pdf) have never been opened. *** THREE WRONG ANSWERS IN ONE EVENING AND ONE FAULT BEHIND ALL THREE: reading the rendered page instead of the request underneath it. *** The first trusted a structurally empty half, the second trusted an unrepeated control, the third trusted a printed number. Each dissolves the moment the endpoint is called and the counts move with the surname. THE RULE: where a page and its own API disagree, the API is the instrument and the page is a report about it.

rows.what: AUDITED EVERY ATLAS PIN AND EVERY STATED DISTANCE — two pins were wrong, and the method nearly broke two right ones
rows.note: DONE 21 SEPTEMBER for the pins and the distances; the dates are carved off to row 259. Sixteen pins were checked against OpenStreetMap Nominatim at one request a second, great-circle distance from the published coordinate, anything over three kilometres read by hand. *** TWO WERE WRONG. *** PORTO was published at 41.35 N and Porto is at 41.15 N — ONE DIGIT, TWENTY-TWO KILOMETRES, and it is where Derrick's mother is buried; the move 'Johannesburg to Porto' carried the same wrong figure. SOMMERFELD was 52.95, 12.98 and belongs at 52.80, 13.03, seventeen kilometres, settled from the archive's own tree which gives Sommerfeld/Osthavelland, postcode 16766, Hohenbrucher Chaussee — that is Kremmen. It is where Siegfried was hidden for twenty-seven months. Both fixed. *** AND THE TRAP, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF. *** The first pass also flagged CHEŁMNO at 4.7 km and AUSCHWITZ at 4.3 km AND BOTH PINS ARE CORRECT. A gazetteer lookup of the modern town is not a check on a historical site: 'Oświęcim' returns the town centre four kilometres from the camp, and 'Chełmno nad Nerem' returns a different Chełmno altogether. Querying the Kulmhof camp and the Auschwitz-Birkenau museum puts both pins within 0.4 km. AN AUTOMATED PASS RUN WITHOUT THAT CORRECTION WOULD HAVE MOVED JACOB, SAMUEL AND OSKAR'S PLACE OF DEATH FOUR KILOMETRES AND GEORG AND LYDIA'S FIVE, in the name of accuracy. A flagged distance is a question, not a finding. *** THE STATED DISTANCES. *** There were three on the whole site. 'Some 45 km apart along the Dão' was right for one pair and understated the spread of the three places by nine kilometres — measured, Treixedo to Tondela is 9.4, Tondela to Castro Daire 44.6, Treixedo to Castro Daire 54.0 — and the river was wrong as well, so the sentence now gives the three measured figures and names no river. 'Ivone — 400 miles of railway' is LEFT ALONE AND MARKED UNVERIFIED: the straight line is 282 miles, the claim is about a rail route that detoured north through Komatipoort and Waterval Boven, and replacing one unsourced number with another is not an improvement. The third, 'about fifteen kilometres' for Bischofstein to Sauerbaum, is the error that started this row and was already corrected to 17.8. Full working in data/atlas-pin-audit.tsv.

rows.what: ERNA FRIDA ELSE LEIPHOLZ, SCHÖNEBERG STERBEREGISTER 1975 NR. 79 — and whether she is the Erna of Streitstraße
rows.note: The name index gives the date (13 January 1975), the register number (79) and the confession (ev). A DEATH ENTRY OF THAT VINTAGE CARRIES THE ADDRESS, THE BIRTH DATE OR AGE, THE BIRTHPLACE, THE MARITAL STATUS AND THE INFORMANT -- and the informant is usually the nearest relative, which is the thing this archive keeps running out of. *** THE TENSION TO RESOLVE FIRST, AND IT COSTS NOTHING: *** this archive records "Leibholz Erna · 20 Streitstr. 39" in the 1980-81 telephone book as the last Leibholz in the post-war run. A woman who died in January 1975 is not in a 1980-81 telephone book. EITHER THEY ARE TWO WOMEN OR A YEAR HAS BEEN MISREAD, and re-reading the Streitstraße line settles it before anybody orders a certificate. The certificate itself is a purchase and is not mine.  *** 21 SEPTEMBER, RESOLVED, AND THE TIDY ANSWER WAS WRONG. *** The Streitstraße line was re-read as this row asked. IT IS NOT A LEIBHOLZ AT ALL -- the 1980-81 telephone book OCR read a p as a b, and the 1975-76 and 1979-80 volumes print LEIPHOLZ ERNA plainly, same address, SAME TELEPHONE NUMBER 3 35 84 05 in all three years. See correction 9500904. AND THE DATES DO NOT COLLAPSE INTO ONE WOMAN: Erna Frida Else Leipholz died 13 January 1975 and Erna Leipholz of Streitstraße is listed on her own line for six years after that. TWO WOMEN OF THE SAME NAME. The certificate is no longer needed to tell them apart, which is the cheap half of this row done without spending the expensive half.

rows.what: DIEFFENBACHSTRASSE 58 — Paul Leipholz in 1924, Klara Leipholz in 1957
rows.note: PAUL, Schlosser, S59 Dieffenbachstraße 58, from the 1924 Adressbuch. KLARA, PUTZMACHERIN, SW 29 Dieffenbachstraße 58, from the 1957 and 1959 post-war Namenteil. SAME STREET, SAME HOUSE NUMBER, THIRTY-THREE YEARS AND A WAR APART; the postal prefix differs because Berlin renumbered its districts, not because the address did. A Putzmacherin is a MILLINER and the Leibholz trade in Berlin was hats. TESTS THAT NEED NOBODY'S HELP: the intervening volumes 1925-1943 and 1949-1956 for the same house, which would show whether the family held it straight through; the Kreuzberg registry indexes for both names; and the 1943 and 1949 volumes either side of the gap, which is where a household either survives or does not. NOT KIN ON ANY EVIDENCE HELD. *** CONFIRMED AND JOINED TO ROW 251, 22 SEPTEMBER. *** The 1957 and 1959 directories print the two together, Friedrich first and then the repeat-dash for the same surname: “Leipholz Friedrich Angest Tgl Berlin — KLARA PUTZMACHERIN SW 29 DIEFFENBACH[STRASSE]”. The adjacency is only alphabetical and proves no kinship, BUT IT SHOWS THESE TWO ARE THE WHOLE OF THE LEIPHOLZ NAME IN BERLIN IN THOSE YEARS. The 1924 Paul at the same house was not reached by this instrument: the only “Leipholz Paul” hits are the directory's own cross-reference line, “Leibholz, s. a. Leipholz”.

rows.what: FRIEDRICH LEIPHOLZ of Schwabstraße 4, Reinickendorf — now bracketed to 1974, and the death registers disagree
rows.note: Tegel, Berliner Straße 5a, Angestellter, 1957 and 1959. Reinickendorf, Schwabstraße 4, PENSIONÄR, 1961 through 1970, with the same neighbours in the street section both times. A man who retires between 1959 and 1961 was born around 1895 give or take, WHICH PUTS HIM IN JACOB LEIBHOLZ'S GENERATION. Reinickendorf's death indexes are in the same free LABSA set that gave up Erna, and his death would name a wife and an age. CHEAP, UNASSISTED, AND NOT YET DONE.  *** 21 SEPTEMBER: REINICKENDORF 1974-1981 READ, EIGHT CONSECUTIVE YEARS, HE IS IN NONE OF THEM. *** All eight bracketed -- the nearest name before and after the gap is recorded for every year in data/kreuzberg-reinickendorf-deaths.tsv. 1982-1994 still to read, and those volumes jump from 3 MB to 99 MB because the series changes format. *** EXTENDED AT BOTH ENDS 22 SEPTEMBER. *** The run is not 1961-1970, it is 1957 TO 1973-74. He is an ANGESTELLTER at Tegel in 1957 and 1959, a PENSIONÄR from 1961, at Schwabstraße 4 from at least 1967 — and he is in the TELEPHONE BOOKS at that flat in 1970-71 (49 80 11) and again in 1973-74 (4 91 82 51). TWO NUMBERS AT ONE ADDRESS: Berlin was lengthening subscriber numbers across that period, which is the ordinary explanation, but 49 80 11 does not expand tidily into 4 91 82 51 and no claim is made. *** 22 SEPTEMBER — BRACKETED, AND THE NAME SEARCH THAT WAS USED TO DO IT WAS WRONG. *** All twelve telephone volumes 1969-70 to 1980-81 were read AT THE ALPHABETICAL SLOT between LEIPERT and LEIPIC, which is the row 252 method transferred to these books, and it had to be: A FULL-TEXT SEARCH FOR THIS SURNAME IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT. The OCR prints it LEIPHOTZ in 1972-73, LELPHOLZ in 1976-77 and 1978-79, LEIPKSLZ in 1977-78 and LEIBHOLZ in 1980-81 — FIVE OF THE ELEVEN READABLE VOLUMES MANGLE IT, and a search for the right spelling misses every one.
