A healthy SCHMIDT control (133-191 a volume) sat over the top of that the whole time: A COMMON-NAME CONTROL CANNOT CLEAR A RARE-NAME NEGATIVE. *** THE RESULT: HE IS IN 1970-71, 1972-73 (A VOLUME THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE) AND 1973-74, AT SCHWABSTRASSE 4 IN ALL THREE, AND THE SLOT IS COMPLETE AND EMPTY IN 1974-75. *** His listing ends between the 1973-74 and 1974-75 books — a year tighter than before. 1971-72 has no text layer at all and is inconclusive, not a gap. *** AND THE BRACKET DOES NOT AGREE WITH THE REGISTERS. *** He leaves the book during 1974 and REINICKENDORF 1974-1981 IS ALREADY READ IN FULL AND HE IS IN NONE OF IT. So he moved and died elsewhere, or he died in Reinickendorf after 1981, or he gave up the telephone and lived on — and Heinrich Leibholz, who vanished from the directory in 1942 and did not die until 1948, forbids the easy reading. NEXT: Reinickendorf 1982-1994, the 99 MB volumes. Full working in data/leipholz-telephone-slot-audit.tsv. ERNA OF STREITSTRASSE 39 came out of the same sweep CONTINUOUS ACROSS ALL SIX VOLUMES 1975-76 TO 1980-81 on one number, where the archive had three — which hardens the two-Ernas finding rather than overturning it. *** 23 SEPTEMBER — THE REMAINING WORK IS THIRTEEN VOLUMES. *** The full LABSA catalogue puts Reinickendorf's death indexes for 1982-1994 at THIRTEEN, not the open-ended run this row describes. And if he moved, the whole of 'somewhere else in Berlin' is 296 death-index volumes across 25 offices — bounded, and listed in data/labsa-catalogue.json.

rows.what: THE OTHER OFFICES — Schöneberg is finished, and this row had not noticed
rows.note: Seven of sixty-one are read. The method is now routine and costs about fifteen seconds a volume: LABSA lists the volumes, pdf.js reads them in place over HTTP range requests without downloading a byte of the 40-380 MB files, and the test is not a name search but PULLING EVERY Le[hij]* TOKEN OUT OF THE MIDDLE THIRD AND READING THE ALPHABET FOR A GAP. *** THE PATTERN MUST BE Le[iy][bp]h AND NOT LEIBHOLZ *** -- that is the whole lesson of 1975. Then Kreuzberg for Agnes and for Dieffenbachstraße, Neukölln for Charlotte, Spandau for Erna, Reinickendorf for Friedrich, Wedding for Joachim the Ofensetzer.  *** AND THE METHOD NEEDED A GUARD BEFORE IT COULD BE TRUSTED AT SCALE. *** Carrying the Schöneberg band (33-64 per cent) over to Kreuzberg produced TWO FALSE NEGATIVES -- 1980 stopped scanning at Leipelt and 1981 at Leimbach, both of which sort BEFORE Leipholz, so each reported an absence it had never looked for. A scan must now return the nearest name on EACH SIDE of the target, and a result with an empty side is inconclusive rather than negative. It caught a third case within minutes. ALSO: a volume much larger than its neighbours may hold TWO alphabetical sequences -- Kreuzberg 1982 is 226 pages against 125 and has L twice. And a binary search keyed on a page's median word DOES NOT WORK here, because these registers print forenames in their own column.  *** PROGRESS 21 SEPTEMBER: Schöneberg 1970-1994 complete (25 volumes), Reinickendorf 1974-1981 (8), Kreuzberg 1980-1982 (3), Spandau 1982 (1). THIRTY-SEVEN VOLUMES READ IN A DAY, none downloaded. *** Remaining: Schöneberg 1938-1969, Kreuzberg 1983-1994, Reinickendorf 1982-1994, Spandau 1983-1994 and all of Neukölln and Wedding. *** CORRECTED 22 SEPTEMBER, AND THE CORRECTION IS THAT THE WORK WAS ALREADY DONE. *** This row opens “Seven of sixty-one are read” and closes by listing “Schöneberg 1938-1969” as remaining. NEITHER IS TRUE ANY LONGER, AND HAS NOT BEEN SINCE 21 SEPTEMBER. The resume pointer — schoeneberg-progress.tsv, which exists precisely so that a session reads it before starting — states it plainly: “COMPLETE. 1938 TO 1968 IS READ AT THE IMAGE WITHOUT A GAP, AND 1970-1994 BY TEXT LAYER”, thirty-one years page by page, 295 pages of L surnames, roughly 9,900 names. AND 1969, THE ONE YEAR COVERED BY NEITHER METHOD, IS RECORDED SEPARATELY AS “READ IN FULL” on the same date. ALL SIXTY-ONE SCHÖNEBERG VOLUMES ARE DONE. Two hits in the whole run: Günther Leibholz 1939 Nr. 780, and Erna Frida Else Leipholz 1975 Nr. 79. *** SO THIS ROW IS NOT A SWEEP OF SCHÖNEBERG, IT IS THE OTHER OFFICES, *** and it has been retitled to say so. WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS: KREUZBERG 1983-1994 (which is row 253), REINICKENDORF 1982-1994, SPANDAU 1983-1994, and ALL OF NEUKÖLLN AND WEDDING. The method, the Le[iy][bp]h pattern, the two-sided-neighbour guard and the two-alphabets-in-one-volume warning all stand and are the reason the Schöneberg run can be trusted. THE LESSON IS THE ROW'S OWN: a resume pointer only works if the row that sends you to it is updated when it closes, and this one was not.

rows.what: AGNES LEIBHOLZ née KERGER — 1983 now bracketed too, and the fast route turned out to be a false one
rows.note: She is in the telephone book at Mehringdamm 109 from 1972-73 to 1979-80 and gone from 1980-81, which made 1980-82 the obvious years. SHE IS IN NONE OF THEM, all three bracketed. Kreuzberg 1983-1994 remain, and so does the possibility that she did not die in Kreuzberg at all. *** THE CONTROL CASE THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY OWNS IS THE WARNING: *** Heinrich Leibholz, her husband, vanished from the Berlin directory after 1942 and DID NOT DIE UNTIL 1948. Leaving a telephone book is not dying. She was born 10 March 1889, so she was 91 in 1980 -- a move into a home in another borough is at least as likely as a death, and a home means another office.  *** 22 SEPTEMBER — 1983 BRACKETED, AND THE METHOD CORRECTED BEFORE IT COULD DO HARM. *** All twelve Kreuzberg volumes for 1983-1994 are labelled 'Durchsuchbares PDF durch OCR-Texterkennung', which promised the whole row in minutes. THE LABEL IS NOT TRUE OF THE NAMES. A frequency control on Kreuzberg 1983 — 211 pages, a whole year of a borough — finds SCHMIDT 6, MÜLLER 7, LEHMANN 4, LANGE 1 AND BECKER ZERO in the text layer. The registers are handwritten and the OCR has caught the printed headings and almost nothing else. The page image settles it: page 106, the first page of M, carries FIVE MÜLLERS IN JANUARY ALONE, nearly as many as the OCR found in the entire year. A text search here returns a clean nothing and the nothing is the instrument, not the record. *** AND THE SAME TEST CLEARED TWENTY-FIVE PUBLISHED YEARS. *** Schöneberg 1970-1994 was closed 'by text layer' and that closure is SOUND: 1975 gives Schmidt 31, Müller 29, Becker 7 and 1988 gives 29, 24, 8 — four to five times Kreuzberg's yield on fewer pages — and the 1975 layer returns exactly one Le[ip]h match, which is Erna Frida Else Leipholz, the find already held. An instrument that finds the one thing that is there is one whose silence means something. *** SO 1983 WAS READ AT THE IMAGE. *** L/1983 is pages 96-105, bounded by the tail of K on 95 and the opening of M on 106, all twelve months present and in order, about 150 L surnames. NO LEIBHOLZ, NO LEIPHOLZ, NO KERGER. The nearest are Liebsch, Liebau, Liebert, Liebe and Leyser. The twice-filing of married women runs here too — 'Lachmann geb. Lipinski' and 'Lipinski verh. Lachmann', both Nr. 4/83 — so the L block covers a Leibholz-born woman who married out. *** 1984-1994 REMAIN AND THE COST IS NOW KNOWN: *** eleven volumes, about ten L pages each, two legible half-screenshots per page, roughly 220 reads. Bounded and dull and the only honest route. AND THE PRIOR QUESTION IS UNCHANGED — she was 91 and left the telephone book; a home in another borough is at least as likely as a death in Kreuzberg, and reading eleven more Kreuzberg volumes tests one branch of that and not the other. Full working in data/kreuzberg-ocr-control.tsv. *** 23 SEPTEMBER — 'ANOTHER OFFICE' IS NOW A NUMBER. *** This row raises the possibility that Agnes, 91 in 1980, moved into a home in another borough and died there. The full LABSA catalogue makes that exactly 296 DEATH-INDEX VOLUMES ACROSS 25 OFFICES that reach 1982 or later; Kreuzberg von Berlin's own share of it is THIRTEEN. Not a vague elsewhere.

rows.what: A JEWISH WOMAN BORN LEIBHOLZ, married SCHÖNFELD — Spandau Sterberegister 1982 Nr. 1486
rows.note: Found on 21 September while sweeping Spandau for Erna, who is not there. "Leibholz verh. Schönfeld | [forename withheld] | 19. 5. | 1486 | mos. | verw." *** MOS. IS MOSAISCH. A JEWISH WOMAN BORN LEIBHOLZ, LIVING IN BERLIN-SPANDAU AND DYING THERE IN 1982. *** *** HER FORENAME IS WITHHELD AND THAT IS DAVID'S DECISION TO REVERSE, NOT THIS ARCHIVE'S. *** Set beside the surname she was born with, her forename is ALSO THE MAIDEN NAME OF A LIVING PERSON IN THIS FAMILY. The two are certainly different women -- one died in 1982 -- but a reader and a search engine cannot tell, and the rule here is that a living person's former name does not go on a public page whoever the page is about. The forename is in the private notes and the register number is published, so the certificate is orderable without it. THE FREE TEST BEFORE ANY PURCHASE: the Berlin marriage indexes for a LEIBHOLZ–SCHÖNFELD marriage, which names her father. TWO THINGS THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD AND NEVER JOINED: Yad Vashem 5415605 gives SAMUEL LEIBHOLZ a wife with the same forename, recorded as new and never followed; and the Arolsen tracing files hold a Leibholz correspondence file INDEXED UNDER SCHÖNFELD -- the same married surname. THE TWO WOMEN ARE PROBABLY NOT ONE: Samuel's widow would be indexed under her own birth name as "Xxx verh. Leibholz", and this entry makes Leibholz the birth name. *** 23 SEPTEMBER — THE FREE TEST MAY NOT EXIST, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. *** This row calls the Berlin marriage indexes the free test before any purchase. THE MARRIAGE INDEXES STOP AT 1944, EVERYWHERE — 1,595 volumes and the latest year in any of them is 1944, the 80-year closure moving forward a year at a time. She was a Jewish woman in Berlin, widowed by 1982, who survived the war; A MARRIAGE IN THE LATE 1940s IS AT LEAST AS LIKELY AS ONE BEFORE 1944. So the free route settles it if the marriage is pre-1945 and CANNOT TOUCH IT otherwise. Worth knowing before 1,180 volumes are read to find nothing, and it changes when the purchase of Spandau 1982 Nr. 1486 stops being avoidable. THAT REMAINS DAVID'S DECISION AND NOT THIS ARCHIVE'S.

rows.what: check:living PASSED LOCALLY AND FAILED CI ON THE SAME COMMIT — harvest does not guard maiden names
rows.note: Commit 8c1d8af failed CI in 17 seconds and the site did not publish. *** THE GATE WAS RIGHT AND THE LOCAL RUN OF THE SAME GATE WAS WRONG. *** --harvest builds each guard from the live tree's `first` + `last`, which is a person's CURRENT name, and NEVER CHECKS A MARRIED WOMAN'S MAIDEN NAME. --hashes carries nine salted digests where harvest built seven guards, and the two extra are maiden-name forms. So a page naming a living woman by the surname she was born with passed locally and was stopped in CI. *** A GREEN LOCAL RUN HAD BEEN READ AS PERMISSION ALL MORNING AND IT WAS NOT ONE. *** FIXED: check:living now runs BOTH modes locally and the build fails if either does; the limit is written into the tool's own docstring beside the one already recorded for --hashes. PROVED: the hashes run locally now reproduces the CI failure name for name and file for file. A peer session found this by reading CI while this archive was reading its own green terminal.

rows.what: SCHÖNEBERG 1938-1968 — thirty-one years that needed eyes, not a text search, AND THEY HAVE NOW HAD THEM
rows.note: DONE 21 SEPTEMBER, ALL OF IT. Twelve volumes, P Rep. 163 Nr. 584 to Nr. 595, read page by page at the image: 295 pages of L surnames, roughly 9,900 names. *** 1938 TO 1968 NOW RUNS WITHOUT A GAP, and with 1970-1994 already closed by text layer that is fifty-six years of Schöneberg death registration asked the question once and properly. *** THE RESULT IS ONE HIT IN THIRTY-ONE YEARS: Günther Leibholz, 1939 Nr. 780, which was found on the second day of the read and never repeated. Every year is bounded at both ends — a low opening register number and a closing entry in the last days of December followed by blank ruled lines — every page was read in two overlapping halves with the overlap confirmed by a shared row, and from 1954, when the register began grouping each letter-year by month, the headings were checked Januar to Dezember, all twelve, in order. *** READING ONLY THE L BLOCK IS ENOUGH, AND THAT IS PROVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. *** A daughter born Leibholz who married would die under her husband's name, which would have put a hole in the negative exactly where this family's women are. The register files every married woman TWICE, under her husband's surname and under her maiden name, with the same register number — demonstrated with a named pair in EVERY ONE OF THE TWELVE VOLUMES, thirteen pairs in all. *** AND THE CLERKS COULD FORM THE LETTERS. *** The 1967 L block contains LINDEHOLZ (Nr. 268), which is how these hands write -holz, and LEIPOLD (Nr. 1290), which is how they write Leip-. Both halves of the name occur in Schöneberg. Only the combination does not. Fourteen names had to be settled at scale 6, the two closest being LIEBHOLD (1958 Nr. 2136) and LEITHOLD (1963 Nr. 734, again 1968 Nr. 2366) — each one letter from Leibholz in the middle and one at the end, and each indistinguishable from it at page scale. The full method and every page range is in data/schoeneberg-progress.tsv, which is the control file any future session reads first.

rows.what: GÜNTHER LEIBHOLZ — Schöneberg Sterberegister 1939 Nr. 780, and the religion column is the problem
rows.note: The first and only Leibholz in eleven years of reading Schöneberg's death indexes at the image. *** THE ENTRY SAYS "ev." AND CARRIES NO "ISRAEL", AND IN 1939 THAT IS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN SILENCE. *** From 1 January 1939 Jewish men were compelled to add ISRAEL, and this register applies the rule relentlessly — the same nine pages carry Lehmann Bernhard Israel, Löffler Gustav Israel, Litten Minna Sara, Lichtheim Berta Anna Sara and dozens more, all marked mos. Günther carries neither. THE STATE DID NOT CLASSIFY HIM AS JEWISH. That damages the obvious hypothesis: Jacob Leibholz was mos. and his wife Auguste was kath., so a child of theirs would be Catholic or Jewish, NOT PROTESTANT. NOT KIN ON ANY EVIDENCE HELD. *** TESTS IN ORDER OF COST, AND THE FIRST TWO ARE FREE: *** (1) the 1939 and 1940 Berliner Adressbuch for a Leibholz household in Schöneberg — this archive's 1939 list has Ella, Fritz and Jaques there and no Günther; (2) the Berlin MARRIAGE indexes, which are open to 1938, for a Leibholz marrying a Protestant wife, since births are closed 110 years and a Günther of the 1920s or 1930s is unreachable; (3) the certificate itself, Schöneberg 1939 Nr. 780, which carries the age, the address, the parents if he was a minor, and the informant. THE CERTIFICATE IS A PURCHASE AND IS NOT MINE, and it is the cheapest document in the whole backlog that could turn a name into a person. *** 22 SEPTEMBER — TEST (2) COSTED AT THE IMAGE, AND THE WORD “FREE” IN THIS ROW IS DOING TOO MUCH WORK. *** The full inventory now exists for the first time: TWENTY-ONE Schöneberg marriage name-indexes across three offices, covering 1874 to 1943 without a gap — P Rep. 160 (Schöneberg I, ten volumes), P Rep. 161 (Schöneberg II, seven), P Rep. 163 (the merged office from 1938, four, of which 1938-39 IS SPLIT INTO SEPARATE MEN'S AND WOMEN'S BOOKS, the only place in the run where that happens and a trap for anyone who reads one and thinks they have read the year). The archive had previously named two of the twenty-one. *** THEN THE STRUCTURE WAS MEASURED ON P REP. 161 NR. 270 AND IT KILLS THE CHEAP VERSION OF THIS TEST. *** It is ONE ALPHABET with the years NESTED INSIDE EACH LETTER — the same shape the 1949-51 death indexes turned out to have — so you cannot open a volume at the year you want. AND WITHIN A LETTER THE ENTRIES ARE IN REGISTRATION ORDER, NOT ALPHABETICAL: page 256 of the L block reads Lintow, Lungwitz, Liebermann, Landois, Loewenthal, Lehmann. The first letter is sorted and nothing else is, SO THERE IS NO SKIPPING TO “LEI” — every page of every L block must be read. L occupies about forty-two pages of that four-year volume, the Kurrent hand needs scale 2.6 to be legible, and at that scale a page is THREE READS. About 125 reads a volume; sixteen volumes cover 1899-1938; *** ROUGHLY TWO THOUSAND READS, nearly ten times the Kreuzberg backlog in row 253. *** SO THE ORDER OF THE THREE TESTS IN THIS ROW IS WRONG AND IS HEREBY REVERSED. The certificate — Schöneberg 1939 Nr. 780 — is ONE DOCUMENT carrying his age, his address, his parents if he was a minor, and the informant, and it would settle in a page what two thousand reads might not settle at all, because a marriage index yields a surname and a register number and says nothing about a son. AND THE WHOLE ROUTE RESTS ON AN UNASKED ASSUMPTION: that his parents married in Schöneberg. He DIED there. Berlin had well over a hundred registry offices, and an empty Schöneberg sweep would prove almost nothing. THE INVENTORY AND THE ARITHMETIC ARE IN schoeneberg-marriage-indexes.tsv. THE ROW STAYS OPEN and now recommends the purchase over the sweep. *** TEST (1) COMPLETED FOR 1940, 22 SEPTEMBER. *** The row had the 1939 list already (Ella, Fritz and Jaques in Schöneberg, no Günther); 1940 was outstanding. The 1940 Berliner Adressbuch is in the ZLB full-text index — controlled by “Schmidt” returning 3,106 in that volume — and LEIBHOLZ RETURNS TWELVE, LEIPHOLZ SIX. The twelve, as the street sections print them (initials only, which is how the Straßenteil works): S. Israel · A. Israel · W. Israel · F., Pensionär · V., Witwe · one read as Bankbeamter · SL., Witwe · F., Asm. · M., Witwe · H., Verwalt. — plus the two cross-reference lines “Leibholz s. a. Leipholz”. *** THREE OF THEM CARRY “ISRAEL”, the forename compulsory for Jewish men from January 1939 — the same rule whose ABSENCE from Günther's death entry is this row's whole argument. *** AND THERE IS NO G. AMONG THE TWELVE. That is consistent with a man who died in Schöneberg in 1939 and would not be in the 1940 book — it is what the row expects rather than a discovery, and it is recorded because the row asked for it. TWO LIMITS: the OCR of this volume is poor, rendering initials as “tz.” and “SL”, so a G could be mangled; and the street sections list HOUSEHOLDERS, so a son living at home would not appear under his own name whether he were alive or dead.

rows.what: THE EVIDENCE 'PEOPLE' COUNT WAS INFLATED BY NARRATIVE ROWS — fixed, and the published figure falls from 187 to 136
rows.note: OPENED AND CLOSED 21 SEPTEMBER. Dumping every 'person' the evidence gate knew about showed that about a fifth were not people but ROW LABELS out of the narrative TSVs — '*** AND A CHILD THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE ***', 'AFRIKANISCHE STRASSE 37 — and a namesake to keep apart', 'who she was looking for (1)'. They arrive through the manifest's ["who"] key, because in a narrative file that column carries section headings as well as names. *** TWO COSTS, AND THE SECOND IS THE REAL ONE. *** The published figure overstated: /register/ and the evidence panels said 187 people and 252 records. And for those rows check-evidence's promise quietly degraded from 'this PERSON reaches a reader' to 'this STRING is somewhere on the site' — which it trivially is, because the sentence is printed on the page. THOSE ROWS WERE PASSING THE GATE FOR THE WRONG REASON. *** THE FIX IS RECOVERY, NOT REJECTION. *** The rows are written 'NAME — what the row is about', so build-evidence now cuts at the em dash, at ' (', and at a comma WHOSE TAIL IS PROSE — the last so that 'ARTHUR, THE SANITÄTSRAT' yields ARTHUR while 'Leibholz, Samuel' is left alone. What survives must then still look like a name: no digits, no leading asterisk or bracket, no opening lower case, no more than six words, no sentence words. THAT RECOVERED TWELVE PEOPLE WHO HAD BEEN STORED UNDER A WHOLE SENTENCE — HANS LEIBHOLZ, HEINRICH LEIBHOLZ, ANTON LUWINSKI, SOPHIE LEIBHOLZ, AUGUSTE LEIBHOLZ née LUWINSKI, IVONE LUWENSKI, PAULINE BERMAN, PAULINE MILLER and others — whose names were previously 'HANS LEIBHOLZ — read in full' and 'PAULINE BERMAN (formerly MILLER, born RAPPOPORT)'. *** NOTHING IS DROPPED SILENTLY. *** build-evidence now PRINTS every cell it refused, 52 of them, with its file, under the line 'if a real name is in this list, the data or the rule is wrong'. A filter you cannot see is the fault this archive keeps having, and the first draft of this rule wrongly rejected IVONE LUWENSKI, ARTHUR and JACOB — the printed list is how that was caught and corrected in one pass. *** VERIFIED BEFORE AND AFTER. *** The old and new people lists were diffed name by name and every real person was confirmed still present: George William Castle, Heinrich Leibholz, Hans Leibholz, Jacob Leibholz, Samuel Israel Leibholz, Oskar Leibholz, Auguste, Kurt, Sophie, Anton. THE PUBLISHED COUNT IS NOW 204 RECORDS ABOUT 136 PEOPLE, and it is the first time that number has meant what it says.

rows.what: THE DATES — first mechanical pass done, and it found a correction that never propagated
rows.note: Row 248 asked for three things — every atlas pin, every stated distance, every date converted between a register and a narrative. THE PINS AND THE DISTANCES ARE DONE AND FOUND TWO WRONG PINS; THE DATES ARE NOT STARTED, and saying so in its own row is better than letting a third of a task sleep inside a green one. WHAT IT MEANS IN PRACTICE: every date this archive prints in prose should be reconcilable to the register entry or document it came from, and nobody has ever walked that list. The known shape of the fault is the Sauerbaum pin and the 'about fifteen kilometres' — a figure that was close enough to survive a published page, a build gate and several re-readings, and was caught only because something unrelated touched it. A date that is a year out will behave exactly the same way. START WITH DATES THAT APPEAR IN BOTH A data/ FILE AND AN .astro PAGE, because those can be compared mechanically, and only then read the ones that exist in prose alone.  *** 22 SEPTEMBER — FIRST PASS RUN, AND IT FOUND ONE. *** A mechanical audit of all 149 register people (death before birth, born/died disagreeing with the derived by/dy, facts dated outside a life, impossible calendar dates, a child born before its parent was thirteen) returned THREE hits, of which one is real and published. *** KURT ISRAEL LUWINSKI READ 'died 15 December 1968' AND 'dy 1969' IN THE SAME RECORD. *** The archive corrected his death from Dec 15 1969 to 15 December 1968 on good evidence — the Johannesburg Chevrah Kadisha burial register, died 15.12.1968, buried 16.12.1968, Westpark block L grave 211, Yahrzeit 24 Kislev 5729, which is itself 15 December 1968, and burial the next day is what you would expect. THE CORRECTION WAS RIGHT AND IT DID NOT PROPAGATE. build-register.py applied it to `died` and never recomputed `dy`, and `dy` is what /bloodline/ prints and what /timeline/ PLOTS HIM BY. So the register page said 1968, the bloodline said 1912-1969, and the timeline put him in the wrong year. Two prose lines had gone stale with it — data/berlin-postwar-luwinski.tsv and a research-log entry both still read 'died in Johannesburg in 1969'. *** FIXED: *** the builder now recomputes `dy` from a died correction, and does the same for `born`/`by`, which was not triggered by the data either — and neither was the died case when it was written, and it still shipped a wrong year onto two pages. The two prose lines are corrected. The site now carries one death year for Kurt in every place, and the only 1969s left are Henry Robert Wear, who did die in Johannesburg in 1969, and the correction's own record of what it superseded. *** THE OTHER TWO HITS ARE BENIGN *** — a Residence dated to the year of birth, and a stray fact on the same record. *** STILL OWED: *** the 52 date strings the parser cannot read ('Circa 1912', 'Between Aug 1966 and July 1970', '25. o. 26 Mrz. 1871') are unaudited, and no date in prose has been reconciled to its source document. THIS PASS CHECKED THE REGISTER AGAINST ITSELF, WHICH IS THE CHEAPEST THIRD OF THE JOB. *** 22 SEPTEMBER, SECOND LEG DONE — AND THE ROW'S OWN NUMBER WAS WRONG AGAIN. *** This row said 52 date strings the parser cannot read. EVERY DATE STRING IN THE REGISTER PARSES; not one fails. The 52 counted strings that are not in the canonical shape, and most of those are just “Aug 8 1884”. THE REAL POPULATION IS THIRTY-ONE STRINGS CARRYING A QUALIFIER, and the danger was never that they parse badly — IT IS THAT THEY PARSE TOO WELL. year() takes the first four digits and throws the qualifying word away, so “Before 1955” reached the bloodline as 1955 and the timeline PLOTTED A POINT AT IT. A BOUND WAS BEING PUBLISHED AS A DATE, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Twenty-seven of the thirty-one are on facts, which print as the source wrote them and are safe. FOUR REACHED A READER AS BARE YEARS: Joachim Luwinski “Before 1955”, Elli Leibholz (Struzik) “After May 13 1942”, Johannes Antonie Oelofse De Witt “Circa 1923” and Maria Elizabeth van Straaten “Circa Jan 1876”. *** FIXED IN THE BUILDER, WHICH IS THE LESSON FROM THE KURT CASE FOUR HOURS EARLIER: *** build-register.py now has qualifier() and every record carries byq/dyq beside by/dy, the correction loop sets them too so a correction cannot re-introduce the fault, and both pages print the word — the bloodline reads “1865 – before 1955” and the timeline says in its date column what kind of point it is. *** AND ONE OF THE FOUR WAS REPLACED OUTRIGHT BY THE SAME EVENING'S OTHER WORK: *** Elli's “After May 13 1942” is the DEPORTATION DATE, and Gedenkbuch entry en1169257 — loaded into this archive hours before — gives her as dying at KULMHOF IN MAY 1942, birth date matching to the day. Correction 9500147. THE YEAR ON THE PAGE DOES NOT CHANGE, and that is worth saying plainly: the archive was right by accident, because a floor and the truth fell in the same year. Joachim's bound has no such luck behind it. The whole audit is in register-date-audit.tsv. *** THE ROW STAYS OPEN ON THE THIRD LEG, which is the expensive one: not one date printed in prose has been reconciled to the document it came from. Both passes so far have checked the register against itself. *** THIRD LEG, MECHANICAL PART DONE 22 SEPTEMBER, AND IT COMES BACK CLEAN. *** 156 distinct full prose dates across the pages; each taken with 160 characters of context; every published person with a known year looked for in that context; any date within two years of their register date but not equal to it flagged. ELEVEN FLAGS, ALL ELEVEN FALSE POSITIVES, each opened and read — every one is a date about one person sitting near another person's name. NOT ONE PROSE DATE CONTRADICTS THE REGISTER. AND THE CHECK PROVES ITS OWN LIMIT: proximity is not aboutness, so it can show that no prose date disagrees with a named person's register entry, but it CANNOT reconcile a prose date to the DOCUMENT it came from, which is what this row asks. That part needs a reader with the source in front of them, one date at a time. THE ROW STAYS OPEN ON THAT, and is now closed on everything a script can do.

rows.what: LAY THE FORTY-FOUR BERLIN BOROUGHS AGAINST THE ADRESSBUCH
rows.note: Row 246 expected the Gedenkbuch to hand over Berlin ADDRESSES and it hands over BOROUGHS. Forty-four of the fifty-two are Berlin — Schöneberg 6, Wilmersdorf 6, Charlottenburg 5, Friedrichshain 5, Tiergarten 4, Neukölln 4, Mitte 4, Prenzlauer Berg 3, Kreuzberg 1, three plain Berlin, two with two boroughs each. THE WORK IS THE REVERSE OF WHAT ROW 246 IMAGINED: not look up an address, but read the Adressbuch's Leibholz entries for 1933 to 1943 and match each one to a person by borough, forename and household. The Adressbuch prints street and borough, so a borough plus a forename is usually enough to decide. WHAT IT WOULD BUY: a trade and a street for each of forty-four people, and — for the fourteen who appear only under a married surname — the chance to find the household they left. THE TRAP TO AVOID IS THE ONE ROW 246 FELL INTO: a borough is a filter, not an identifier, and two Leibholz in Charlottenburg are two Leibholz in Charlottenburg until something else separates them. *** 22 SEPTEMBER — THE ADRESSBUCH HALF MEASURED, AND FOUR OF THE ELEVEN YEARS CANNOT BE DONE THIS WAY. *** The householder runs were read AS RUNS rather than by name search, which is the instrument row 251 arrived at the same morning: find the headword, take every dashed line under it, stop at the next surname. IT REPRODUCES THE IMAGE READING WHERE THE DASHES SURVIVE — 1938 returns exactly seventeen and 1940 exactly ten, matching what was read off the page images on 20 September. IT FAILS WHERE THEY DO NOT: 1935, 1937, 1939 and 1941 return no run at all because the headword is mangled past matching, and 1942 and 1943 return one and two entries against true counts of six and four, because the lost em-dashes swallow the next surname as a continuation. SO THE BOROUGH MATCHING NEEDS THE PAGE IMAGES FOR 1939, 1941, 1942 AND 1943 — which this row always implied and is now measured. The pass paid for itself twice on the way: THE 1940 COUNT WAS ELEVEN IN THREE FILES AND IS TEN (the eleven belongs to 1939), and JAQUES LEIBHOLZ & CO. WAS AT KRAUSENSTRASSE 59-60, NOT KRONENSTRASSE — four readings in three volumes, and the long-s artefact in "Kraufen" and "Kraujeu" is a letter Kronenstrasse does not have. Corrections 9500911 and 9500912. Working in data/adressbuch-namenteil-runs.tsv.

rows.what: THE PROBATE CALENDAR, READ — four chunks, sixteen Wear grants, and a twelve-year forename sweep
rows.note: DONE 22 September 2026, and it never needed a PDF viewer. The chunk's OCR text is served as a property, textract:docContent, so the page is never rendered at all — the CSP and the hidden-pane problem that blocked this an hour ago were both beside the point. *** FOUR CHUNKS READ IN FULL: *** 009223_weake_1973.pdf, which runs Weake to Weare and therefore holds the whole of WEAR; 009474_wear_1974.pdf; 008820_weale_1979.pdf; 009151_wear_1980.pdf. THE TWO FOLLOWING YEARS WERE READ BECAUSE THE CALENDAR RUNS BY YEAR OF GRANT, NOT YEAR OF DEATH — the 1973 volume contains people who died in December 1972, which is the trap this row was opened warning about. SIXTEEN WEAR GRANTS, COUNTED OFF THE PAGE: 1973 Alfred, Dorothy Winifred, Ellen, Elsie, Ernest Leslie, James Watson, Mary Rosine, William; 1974 Walter; 1979 James William, Arthur, Charles, Edith Maud; 1980 Annie Ellen, Norman, Rosetta Emma. NONE IS HIM. *** AND THE WIDER TEST IS WORTH MORE THAN THE NARROW ONE: *** the forename pair “Leonard Aubrey” put to every year from 1970 to 1981 returns TWENTY-SIX MEN and not one is a Wear — Bricknell, Dinsmore, Williams, Day, Hill, Beniston, Moore, Barton, Peters, Waghorne, Evans, Hogben, Pridole, Webberley, Howard, Briers four times, Cooper, Hillier, Palmer, Hawkins, Wines, Bright, Stuckey. CONTROLS WERE RUN BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BELIEVED, which is the whole difference from the three failed attempts: “Ernest Leslie” 1973 returns 18, the nonsense string returns 0, and WEAR/SMITH/LUWINSKI return 41/469/0. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: an English grant needs English assets, so a man who died in South Africa need never appear here. This closes a route, not a life. Written up in probate-calendar-wear.tsv. Nothing downloaded, nothing ordered.

rows.what: JACOB LEIBHOLZ'S BIRTH ENTRY — found and read, Schubin 1884 Nr. 63
rows.note: DONE 22 September 2026, within the hour of the Bydgoszcz letter arriving. *** STANDESAMT SCHUBIN, GEBURTSREGISTER 1884, AKT NR. 63. *** Registered at Schubin on 11 AUGUST 1884: “der Kaufmann SALLY LEIBHOLZ”, resident at Schubin, mosaischer Religion, reported that of “FRIEDERIKE LEIBHOLZ GEBORENE SCHMUL”, his wife, mosaischer Religion, living with him at Schubin, on the EIGHTH OF AUGUST 1884 a child of male sex was born, given the forename JACOB. SALLY SIGNED THE ENTRY HIMSELF. USC Szubin Miasto, sygn. 28, scan 64, modal id 295772956. *** WHAT IS NEW IS NOT THE PARENTS. *** The archive already held all three people and the link between them from the family record. WHAT CHANGES IS THE STANDING: Jacob's parentage rested on a tree this morning and rests on the civil register of his birthplace tonight, and the two agree to the day. Plus five things the tree did not have — Sally's trade (Kaufmann) dated to 1884, both parents' religion as the STATE recorded it, the registration date, the shared residence, and the first specimen of Sally's handwriting this archive has. *** AND IT DOES NOT ANSWER THE QUESTION THE LETTER WAS SENT TO ASK. *** A German birth entry names the parents and NOT THEIR ORIGINS — no birthplace, no age, no former residence for either of them. So whether the Schubin Leibholz are a Hammerstein family that moved east is exactly where it was: on the Gedenkbuch, and on a Hammerstein birth in 1847 that Koszalin has confirmed no surviving register can now verify. THE NEXT DOCUMENT IS THE ONE THAT WOULD SETTLE IT — see row 263.

rows.what: THE 1874 SZUBIN MARRIAGE — read, and it answers Hammerstein
rows.note: DONE 22 September 2026, the same evening it was opened. *** STANDESAMT SCHUBIN, AKT NR. 9 OF 24 NOVEMBER 1874 — the ninth and last marriage of the year. *** DER KAUFMANN SALLY LEIBHOLZ, mosaischer Religion, SIEBEN UND ZWANZIG JAHRE ALT, GEBOREN ZU HAMMERSTEIN, WOHNHAFT ZU HAMMERSTEIN, son of the Kaufmann JACOB LEIBHOLZ and his wife WILHELMINE GEB. POLLNOW; married FRIEDERICA SCHMUL, mosaischer Religion, geboren zu Schubin, wohnhaft zu Schubin. *** THIS ANSWERS THE STANDING QUESTION FROM A DOCUMENT. *** The Schubin branch is a Hammerstein family that moved east, and it is no longer an inference from the Gedenkbuch — a registrar wrote it down in 1874, and twenty-seven years old in November 1874 puts his birth in 1847, the year this archive has always carried and which Koszalin confirmed no surviving register can verify. THE MARRIAGE ENTRY DID WHAT THE LOST BIRTH REGISTER WOULD HAVE DONE. *** AND IT ADDS A GENERATION: *** JACOB LEIBHOLZ and WILHELMINE NÉE POLLNOW, Sally's parents and Kurt's great-grandparents, neither of whom existed in this archive in any form before tonight. It also explains a name — the Jacob born at Schubin on 8 August 1884 was named for his grandfather. THE MAIDEN NAME IS THE LEAST CERTAIN THING ON THE PAGE and is flagged as such: Kurrent P/T/Z confuse, and it is read as POLLNOW. IT DOES NOT MAKE GEORG A BROTHER — two births two months apart in different provinces still cannot be brothers — but the reason for expecting the Hammerstein Leibholz to be strangers has gone. AND ONE MISTAKE ON THE WAY, RECORDED: “page 10” is SCAN 10, not scan index 9. The first attempt landed on akt Nr. 8, then stepped back to Nr. 7 — 24 November 1874, THE RIGHT DATE AND THE WRONG PEOPLE, which is precisely the near-miss that gets published as a find. The unit's own “Indexes in unit” tab settled it in plain text. THE RULE: when a viewer offers an index, read the index before paging by arithmetic.

rows.what: SALLY LEIBHOLZ'S DEATH — try Berlin before paging 190 Szubin units
rows.note: He has no death date and no death place. Alive at Schubin in August 1884, born 1847, and that is the whole of it. *** THE SZUBIN ROUTE HAS BEEN COSTED AND IT IS BAD VALUE FIRST: *** 190 death units across the town's THREE registry offices, NO alphabetical death index (birth and marriage skorowidze exist; death ones return zero against a working control), and the portal's person index holds ONE Leibholz in 228,278 people. No index, no year, 190 units. *** TRY BERLIN FIRST. *** Kurt was born there in 1912, the household is at Chodowieckistraße in 1913, Jacob married there in 1924 — if Sally followed his sons he died in Berlin, and the Landesarchiv Namensverzeichnisse are an instrument this archive already reads fluently and has swept 142 offices with. A man born in 1847 dying in Berlin lands in a range the death indexes cover. IF BERLIN COMES BACK EMPTY, the Szubin sweep is still there and should start with USC SZUBIN MIASTO (6/1792), which is this family's office — not the two Wieś offices. *** PROBED 22 SEPTEMBER, AND THE CHEAP TEST CAME FIRST. *** Before sweeping any death index, the question is whether Sally was ever in Berlin at all — and the digitised Berlin address books are full-text searchable. The books print surname first, so the phrase had to be built that way. RESULTS: “Leibholz Georg”, the control, returns 4. “Leibholz Sally” returns 0. “Leibholz Salomon” returns 0. The null string “Leibholz Zqxvwyrk” returns 0. *** AND THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS WEAK RATHER THAN STRONG, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH STATING. *** FOUR HITS FOR GEORG IS FAR TOO FEW. He is in the Berlin directories across years — this archive has him at Chodowieckistraße 31 in 1913 and 1914 and at a Wäscherei in Michaelkirchstraße later. A phrase index that returns four for a man who should return dozens is SPARSE, so a zero from it is a weak negative and nothing more. It is recorded because it lowers the prior on Berlin slightly and cost three queries, NOT because it closes anything. Fraktur OCR mangles forenames, the digitisation does not cover every volume, and he may simply have died at Schubin before the family ever moved.

rows.what: THE SCHMUL SIDE — corrected: it is TWO scans at Szubin, not 119
rows.note: *** THIS ROW WAS WRONG WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN AN HOUR AGO AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY REDONE. *** It said 119 indexed Schmul scans were waiting to be opened, implying a rich Schubin Schmul archive. THE 119 IS REAL BUT IT IS REGION-WIDE. FILTERED TO SZUBIN IT IS **TWO**, and one of the two is the 1874 marriage itself. The other 117 are Schmuls elsewhere in Kuyavia-Pomerania with nothing yet joining them to this family. The contrast that IS real and does stand: 119 Schmul against ONE Leibholz in a 228,278-person index. *** THE BRIDE'S HALF OF THE MARRIAGE HAS NOW BEEN READ. *** FRIEDERICA SCHMUL, jüdischer Religion, twenty-something, GEBOREN ZU SCHUBIN, WOHNHAFT ZU SCHUBIN. AND THE PRINTED FORM SAYS “TOCHTER DER” WHERE THE GROOM'S SAYS “SOHN DES” — same page, same hand. That is either “Tochter der unverehelichten [name]”, which would make Schmul her MOTHER'S name with no father recorded, or “Tochter der Eheleute X und Y”, which is equally standard. THE WORD AFTER “der” WAS NOT LEGIBLE AND IS NOT BEING GUESSED. No parent of Friederica has been entered into this archive. *** THE ONE REAL LEAD: ABRAHAM SCHMUL, born Szubin 1846, died Koronowo 1904, son of JULIUSZ SCHMUL and JETTE NÉE MUSCHILL. *** A Jewish Schmul born in the same small town six to eight years before her. NOT CLAIMED AS HER BROTHER — no document joins them and the card is a volunteer transcription, not a register. AND THE TRAP THAT WAS AVOIDED IS WORTH THE ROW ON ITS OWN: Abraham's card names a MARRIED couple, which would make “Tochter der Eheleute” suddenly readable. A hypothesis that makes a hard word legible is the oldest way to misread a document, and this archive did exactly that twice today. *** AND THE NEXT STEP THIS ROW ORIGINALLY PROPOSED WAS IMPOSSIBLE, WHICH WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. *** It said to read Friederica's own birth entry in the Szubin birth books “which are online and cover the 1850s”. THEY DO NOT AND CANNOT. PRUSSIAN CIVIL REGISTRATION BEGAN ON 1 OCTOBER 1874 — which is why the whole 1874 marriage unit holds NINE entries — so a birth around 1852 has no Standesamt record anywhere in Prussia. A Jewish birth of that decade could only be in the records of the Jewish religious community, and the portal's team facet, probed with controls, has none: “Miasto” returns six registry offices including Szubin Miasto, “Gmina” returns exactly one religious fonds — the EVANGELICAL-UNIONIST community of Szubin, 286 units — and “ydow” returns NOTHING. Szubin's pre-1874 coverage in this portal is Protestant and nothing else. SO THE ROUTE IS CLOSED HERE, though not necessarily in the world: the Szubin Jewish registers may survive unscanned at Bydgoszcz, at the Jewish Historical Institute in Warsaw, or in JRI-Poland, and NONE HAS BEEN ASKED. Bydgoszcz answered one letter in eight days, holds USC Szubin Miasto, and is the obvious place to ask. See szubin-pre1874-jewish-records.tsv.

rows.what: SEND THE BYDGOSZCZ LETTER — the Szubin Jewish community registers
rows.note: DRAFTED 22 September 2026, NOT SENT. requests/36-SEND-THIS-to-bydgoszcz-jewish-registers.txt, Polish with an English translation beneath it. Send as a REPLY on the thread of IU.631.434.2026 so it lands against the same file. *** IT IS NOT A REPEAT, ALTHOUGH IT LOOKS LIKE ONE. *** The letter of 15 September already asked whether Bydgoszcz holds the Szubin Jewish community records — but only as a conditional, “if the entry is not there after all”. The entry WAS there, so the condition never triggered and the question was never answered. The draft says so in as many words, so nobody at the archive thinks they are being asked twice. WHAT IT ASKS: whether the archive holds the akta gminy wyznaniowej żydowskiej w Szubinie — Jewish community registers from before 1874 — and if not, where they might now be or whether they were destroyed. FRIEDERICA SCHMUL was born at Szubin about 1852, and Prussian civil registration did not begin until 1 October 1874, so no Standesamt record of her birth can exist. IT OPENS BY THANKING THEM AND SAYING WHAT THEIR ANSWER PRODUCED — both documents, with signatures and scan numbers. That is deliberate: they pointed at a portal and two records fell out of it within the hour, and an archivist who hears that reads the next question more carefully. IT ALSO STATES THAT THE PORTAL HAS ALREADY BEEN CHECKED and names the one religious fonds Szubin does have, the Evangelical-Unionist community, so the archive is not asked to re-point at something already searched. TWO SUBORDINATE ASKS, both explicitly marked as less important: whether any finding aid would give SALLY LEIBHOLZ'S death date (the death registers have no skorowidze and the letter says it is not asking for a search), and — if the scan happens to be to hand — a glance at the word after “Tochter der” in akt 9/1874, which decides whether Friederica was the daughter of an unmarried woman or of a married couple. *** THIS ARCHIVE DRAFTS LETTERS AND DOES NOT SEND THEM. *** Nothing goes without David. *** SENT 22 SEPTEMBER 2026 *** on the IU.631.434.2026 thread, message 1a0c8d2a92207d0f. Text preserved at requests/sent/2026-09-22-bydgoszcz-jewish-registers-SENT.txt.

rows.note: *** RAISED AND WITHDRAWN THE SAME HOUR, 22 September 2026. *** The row said the Rosebank reply turned the SANDF service-record request from a guess into a document, by giving Leonard's occupation as ARMY and his residence as ROBERTS HEIGHTS. rows.what: SEND THE ROSEBANK THANK-YOU — and ask for the Liber Matrimoniorum by name
rows.note: DRAFTED 22 September 2026, NOT SENT. requests/37, to go as a REPLY on the existing Rosebank thread. *** THE THANKS COMES FIRST AND IS GENUINE: *** they answered in a week, courteously, with a scan attached, under no obligation to do either. *** IT DOES NOT TELL THEM THEY SENT THE WRONG BOOK. *** It was an easy mistake — the priest was also the State's marriage officer, so the parish holds the Government form B.M.D. 3 as well as its own register, and the difference is invisible from outside a presbytery. The letter simply NAMES THE TWO BOOKS IT WANTS — the LIBER MATRIMONIORUM and the BANNS REGISTER — says what is in them that the form lacks, and stops. *** AND IT DOES NOT MENTION that this archive already held every field on the scan they sent. *** That is true, it is recorded here, and saying it to them would be graceless and would make the next request less likely to be answered. It states the reason plainly — an elderly man in Australia who has never known who his father was, and a chain of evidence every step of which is circumstantial — and it offers the parish an easy exit: if the 1940 books are with the Archdiocese rather than the parish, just say so and the letter goes there instead. It discloses that David is not a descendant and makes no claim to be. *** REWRITTEN AND SENT 22 SEPTEMBER 2026, message 1a0c8d21508292fb. *** The draft as first written asked for the Liber Matrimoniorum and the banns register — TWO BOOKS ARLENE HAD ALREADY RULED OUT IN THE BODY OF HER EMAIL, which had not been read because only the PDF attachment had been opened. Caught while checking the thread for the right reply address. WHAT WENT IS A PURE THANK-YOU with no request attached, naming the three things she settled — the parish, the survival of the register, and the No on parents.
